## 문제

`ci.yml` benchmark 잡이 호출하는 명령:
```
python main.py simulate --duration 60 --drones 20 --output results/bench_20.json
python main.py simulate --duration 60 --drones 50 --output results/bench_50.json

body:
## Summary

- New `FinalThreeJob` `@Scheduled(cron="0 30 6 1 * *", zone="Asia/Seoul")` that pre-filters rooms with ≥1 ACTIVE survivor (via new `SurvivalStateRepository.findRoomIdsWithAtLeastOneActive`) and fans out per-room poster generation onto a dedicated 8-thread `MonthlyPosterRenderExecutorConfig` pool, then emits `MonthlyPosterReady` STOMP frames per fresh-generated poster.
- `FinalThreeService.generatePosterWithResult(...)` now returns `(poster, created)` atomically inside the same transaction — closes the TOCTOU window between the original `existsPoster` pre-check and `generatePoster`.
- `JwtChannelInterceptor` `ROOM_TOPIC` regex extended with `posters` so Story 7.3's FE subscriber will pass channel-level auth (2-line proactive extension beyond original AC9 fence — captures the regex change in the same PR that introduces the publish surface, avoiding a chicken-and-egg open during 7.3 review).
- Builds on Story 7.1 (#93) which shipped the per-room render + `final_three_posters` table. Closes Story 7.1 deferred-work entry #1 ("zero-survivor chat fallback only safe if pre-filter excludes those rooms").

**Files (15):** 3 NEW BE source + 5 NEW BE test + 4 MODIFIED BE source + 1 MODIFIED BE test + 2 process files (story md + sprint-status flip). Detailed AC9 fence reconciliation in `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/7-2-monthly-final-3-scheduled-job.md` Dev Agent Record.

## Spec deviations (documented in story file AC12)

1. `FinalThreeJob.isOverBudget(long)` package-private seam — AC10 case 8 "test-only seam" allowance; `FinalThreeJobTest` `Mockito.spy(job) + doReturn(true).when(spy).isOverBudget(anyLong())` drives the budget-exceeded branch without sleeping 10 minutes.
2. Spring 7 `CronTrigger.getTimeZone()` removed → `FinalThreeJobSchedulerRegistrationIT` reads private `zoneId` via reflection (the only available accessor; `toString()` returns only the expression).
3. `FinalThreeService.generatePosterWithResult(...)` returns `(poster, created)` instead of inlined `existsPoster` + `generatePoster` pair from AC5 sample. Identical observable behavior; eliminates double-roundtrip on happy path + TOCTOU.
4. Per-page drain (the `inflight` list is scoped per page, drained inside the `do-while` loop) instead of session-wide accumulation. Bounds memory at `PAGE_SIZE` futures and naturally back-pressures the iterator if workers are slow. Verified by new `runBatch_productionExecutor_drainsPerPageWithoutQueueRejection` test (300 rooms × ~10ms each on real 8/8/256 pool).
5. `JwtChannelInterceptor.ROOM_TOPIC` regex extension to include `posters` — 2-line change beyond original AC9 scope fence. Reviewer's call to unblock Story 7.3's FE subscriber without a separate prerequisite PR.

## Verifications (local — GREEN unless noted)

- `./gradlew test --rerun-tasks` — **668 tests / 0 failures / 0 errors / 96 skipped** (5 of those 96 are this story's opt-in `yeosal.boot-smoke` ITs).
- `./gradlew checkstyleMain` — CLEAN (hex-literal guard inherited from Story 7.1 holds).
- `tools/brand-voice-lint` — 0 HARD / 198 warnings (baseline preserved; 0 FE changes per AC9 fence).
- `git diff --name-only main` — exactly the file list above.

## Docker-bound gates deferred to PR-CI (same precedent as #89 / #90 / #93)

Local dev host has no `docker` daemon. The following opt-in gates are expected to run in PR-CI under `-Dyeosal.boot-smoke=true`:

- **Gate 7**: `FinalThreeJobIT` — 4 cases (happy / idempotent / race-guard via Mockito-based pre-filter→worker delete / 50-room parallel correctness).
- **Gate 8**: `FinalThreeJobSchedulerRegistrationIT` — asserts cron `"0 30 6 1 * *"` + zone `Asia/Seoul` registered on `ScheduledTaskHolder`.
- **Gate 10**: `bootRun` smoke (confirm `MonthlyPosterRenderExecutorConfig` bean initializes without `NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException`).
- **Gate 11**: Manual STOMP `/topic/rooms.{id}.posters` subscribe (manual smoke; not a CI assertion).

CI workflow `.github/workflows/be-it-boot-smoke.yml timeout-minutes:30` may exhaust on accumulated opt-in IT layer — same caveat as Story 7.1 (#93). Follow-up `chore(ci):` PR to increase timeout / parallelize is tracked in `deferred-work.md`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Reviewer: confirm AC9 file fence — 13 production files match the list above + acknowledge `JwtChannelInterceptor` deviation rationale (Story 7.3 unblock).
- [ ] Reviewer: spot-check `FinalThreeService.generatePosterWithResult` — same transactional boundary, `created` derived inside the lock-protected branch.
- [ ] CI: `./gradlew test` (default profile) GREEN — 668/0/0/96.
- [ ] CI: `./gradlew test -Dyeosal.boot-smoke=true` (opt-in) — Gates 7 + 8 GREEN OR CI workflow timeout (Story 7.1 precedent acknowledged).
- [ ] CI: brand-voice lint baseline preserved.
- [ ] Post-merge: Story 7.3 unblocked (FE `FinalThreeCard` + Kakao share consumer surface) — `JwtChannelInterceptor` no longer blocks `.posters` subscribe.

## Related

- Story 7.1 (#93) — server-side SVG poster renderer + ceremony module.
- Story 7.3 (backlog) — FE `FinalThreeCard` + Kakao share.
- Closes Story 7.1 deferred-work entry #1.

author: barriosnahuel
body:
### Summary
Audios you share land better on the other side.

1. You share an audio from Bomp to a chat app.

**before:** in some apps (e.g. Telegram) it arrives as a generic "file to download" — the other person taps it and gets asked to pick a player.
**after:** it arrives as an inline, tap-to-play audio (with title).

### Technical detail
- **`ShareFeature.buildShareIntent`** — sends the file's real MIME via `ContentResolver.getType(contentUri)` instead of the hardcoded wildcard `audio/*`.
- **`resolveAudioMimeType` helper** — when the resolver returns `null` or a non-audio type, derives the MIME from an extension map (`mp3, opus, ogg, m4a, aac, wav`), then falls back to `audio/*` last. Covers the known `.opus → null` gap on API 23–25.
- Manually verified on a Pixel 8: Telegram now renders the inline player + title; WhatsApp keeps inline playback (no regression).

### Code review tips
- **ADR 0013 interpretation:** the fallback branches on a `null` `getType()`, **not** on `Build.VERSION.SDK_INT` — so per ADR 0013 (multi-SDK matrices are only for real `SDK_INT` branches) I used a deterministic pure-helper test (`ShareMimeTypeTest`) instead of a `@Config(sdk=[…])` matrix. Flagging because the original task suggested a multi-SDK test.
- `audio/*` inside a KDoc would open a nested block comment (`/*`) — kept MIME literals out of doc comments on purpose.
- Functional change to the share flow → run `./scripts/run-instrumented-tests.sh` locally before merge (CircleCI doesn't run it).

### Already tested
- `./gradlew check -x test` + `./gradlew test` green locally after rebase onto develop; new `ShareMimeTypeTest` (8 cases) + existing `ShareFeatureTest` pass.

author: ringerc
body:
## Summary

Add `pre_ready_for_query_hook`, fired by `PostgresMain` immediately before each `ReadyForQuery` message is sent. Gives extensions a stable end-of-command-cycle teardown point that no existing hook covers cleanly. Intended for per-Execute metadata that shouldn't leak across cycles, deferred per-cycle logging, statement-scope state attached to extension features that don't run through the executor.

The hook is named after its wire-protocol call site (mirroring `ExecutorStart_hook` / `post_parse_analyze_hook` / `emit_log_hook`). **Not** named `end_of_statement_hook` because `ReadyForQuery` is not per-statement:

- A simple Query message carrying `"SELECT 1; SELECT 2;"` produces **one** `ReadyForQuery`.
- In the extended-query protocol, every Bind/Execute cycle between two Syncs shares a single `ReadyForQuery` (one per Sync).
- `ReadyForQuery` also fires after error-recovery skip-till-Sync, after `CopyDone` / `CopyFail` completion, and other non-statement protocol transitions.

The full naming rationale and pointer to `post_parse_analyze_hook` + `ExecutorEnd_hook` + `ProcessUtility_hook` for true per-statement granularity is documented on the typedef in `src/include/tcop/tcopprot.h`.

No in-tree caller wires the hook yet; it defaults to NULL, and the guarded call is a single branch on the hot loop path.

## Immediate use case

Intended to support single-execution-scoped [OpenTelemetry trace contexts](https://github.com/ringerc/postgres/pull/1) that are supplied to the server via the proposed new [header passing](https://github.com/ringerc/postgres/pull/3)  mechanism.

There's currently no single reliable place to hook (per above) to provide a way to clear state when an operation or operation series delineated by a Sync ends.

Without this it is difficult to reliably support tracing that is scoped to a specific statement or batch of statements within a transaction. The OpenTelemetry convention is to trace each statement.

## Test plan

- [x] `meson test --suite regress` (no behaviour change expected; hook is NULL by default)
- [x] Confirm the guarded call adds nothing measurable to the per-cycle hot path

## Related

* https://github.com/ringerc/postgres/pull/1 - opentelemetry tracing API support
* https://github.com/ringerc/postgres/pull/3 - message headers

body:
## Summary

Implements V73 — Repair Plan Generator.

This milestone adds a plan-only repair planner that converts V72 runtime failure classifications into reviewable repair plan metadata. It does not apply repairs, modify files, restore files, roll out modules, or broaden runtime execution.

## Changes

- Add `repair_plan_generator_service.py`
  - Converts V72 classification results into structured repair plans
  - Produces repair kind, target file candidates, proposed change summary, rationale, confidence, approval requirements, and safety notes
  - Preserves plan-only safety flags

- Add API/dashboard wiring
  - `GET /platform/app-build/runs/{workflow_run_id}/repair-plan`
  - Dashboard Repair Plan Generator panel and button

- Add smoke check
  - `app/platform/agents/repair_plan_generator_check.py`
  - Synthetic V72-style analysis inputs for repair-plan coverage

## Covered Categories

- `command_not_found`
- `missing_dependency`
- `syntax_error`
- `import_error`
- `port_conflict`
- `env_var_missing`
- `process_exited_early`
- `unknown_runtime_failure`
- `none_detected`
- `no_logs_found`

## Validation

Local validation passed:

```bash
python -m py_compile app/platform/services/repair_plan_generator_service.py
python -m py_compile app/platform/agents/repair_plan_generator_check.py
python -m py_compile app/platform/api/app_build_routes.py
python -m app.platform.agents.repair_plan_generator_check
```

Smoke check result:

```json
{
  "check": "repair_plan_generator_check",
  "passed": true
}
```

## Safety Boundary

V73 is repair-plan-only.

It does **not**:

- apply repairs
- write generated files
- modify generated files
- restore files
- roll out modules
- execute generated code
- install packages
- start runtime servers
- auto-approve anything

The next milestone, V74, should add approval-gated repair application only after this plan layer is merged.

author: blamechris
body:
## WP-3.1 — Phase 3 · Interactive-flow correctness

Closes #5318.

### Audit finding closed
- **004** — `claude-tui-session.js` — the stream-stall / soft-inactivity backstops kept running while an AskUserQuestion was pending, so a human taking minutes to answer tripped a misleading "stream stalled — force-cancel".

### What changed
When an AskUserQuestion answer is pending, the **human** is the bottleneck, not claude — so the "claude went silent" backstops are suspended:
- `_armResultTimeout()` skips re-arming the **soft-inactivity**, **stream-stall**, and **pre-first-output** timers while `_pendingUserAnswers` is non-empty.
- An explicit `_suspendBackstopsForPendingQuestion()` fires the moment `user_question` is emitted (no wait for the next drain-loop re-arm); the `_armResultTimeout()` guard keeps them suspended across subsequent re-arms.
- **Resume is automatic:** PostToolUse clears the pending entry and the next drain-loop `_armResultTimeout()` re-arms normally.

**Deliberately preserved:**
- The **hard cap** (2h last-resort) stays armed even across a pending question and keeps its pending-answer cleanup (#4691) — a human who walks away and never answers still gets force-cleared.
- The dedicated **`_askUserQuestionWatchdog`** (armed on answer) is untouched, so a genuinely wedged form still recovers.

Defence in depth: the suspended backstops' handlers (`_handleInactivityWarning`/`_handleStreamStall`/`_handleFirstOutputTimeout`) also bail when a question is pending.

### Acceptance criteria
- [x] A human taking minutes to answer doesn't get a misleading "stream stalled" force-cancel.
- [x] A genuinely wedged form still recovers via the AskUserQuestion watchdog.

### Tests (claude-tui-session, 246 pass)
- `_armResultTimeout` arms all backstops with no pending question; suspends soft/stall/first-output (hard stays armed) while pending; resumes after the answer clears.
- `_handleStreamStall` does not tear down while pending; `_handleHardTimeout` STILL force-clears + clears pending (last-resort backstop not suspended).
- Driving an AskUserQuestion PreToolUse through `_emitToolHookEvent` suspends the backstops end-to-end.

author: 1crushhaus-netizen
body:
Follow-up to the merged **#53** (Profile + Progress → Dashboard). On real data the owner found three issues; this fixes them.

## Problems (from real-data screenshots)
1. The bottom **action bar spilled below the viewport** — with real (taller) data the grid no longer fit one screen and the page scrolled.
2. Overflow should scroll **inside each card**, not push the page.
3. The **radar axis labels clipped into the polygons**.

## Fixes
- **Viewport-fit, no page scroll (≥1024px).** The Dashboard becomes a viewport-tall app frame: `.np-shell--dash` → `100svh` flex column; a `min-height:0` flex chain `shell → main → .np-dash-frame → .np-dash`; `.np-dash` becomes `grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto` (identity/KPIs · panels · **pinned** actions). Each row-2 panel is a flex column — fixed `.np-dash-cardhead` + **scrollable `.np-dash-cardbody`** (`overscroll-behavior:contain`, `scrollbar-gutter:stable`, thin themed scrollbar, scroll-shadow fade, focus ring). Below 1024px it reverts to one column + normal page scroll. Pure CSS — no JS-measured height. *(Designed via a 3-agent web-research/spec workflow.)*
- **Radar (`charts.jsx`).** Label ring pushed to `1.38·R` with per-quadrant `text-anchor` + a numeric y-offset on the `central` baseline, 12px `var(--muted)` labels — names no longer clip the polygons.

## Adversarial review caught (and this fixes) what the Chromium-only live check couldn't
- **P1** — radar used `dominant-baseline: text-before/after-edge` (**unsupported in Safari/Firefox**) → switched to the universal `central` baseline + numeric `dy`.
- **P2** — the not-ranked empty state inherited the `overflow:hidden` height-lock with no scroll container → **gate `.np-shell--dash` on `scores`** so the empty state keeps page scroll (its "Prove it" CTA can't clip on a short viewport).
- **P3** — collapse breakpoint → `max-width: 1023.98px` (no fractional-width gap); scrollable-region `tabIndex` gated via `matchMedia` (no empty tab-stops below 1024px); By-subject reverted to a non-scroll card (no empty scrollbar gutter); dropped inert `flex` on `.np-chart`.

## Verification
- **454 tests + `npm run build` green.**
- **Live-verified headlessly** at **1920×1080** and **1920×800** (no page scroll, action bar pinned, radar/rank-moves/leaderboard scroll internally), **1200×480** (not-ranked empty state scrolls normally, CTA reachable), and a narrow width (radar labels cleanly spaced).
- README §12 updated.

author: madmax983
body:
💡 **What:** Updated vector initialization in `Cpu` and `NesCore` core structs from `Vec::new()` to `Vec::with_capacity(16)` for scratch and trace buffers.

🎯 **Why:** These vectors are cleared (`.clear()`) and reused heavily per CPU instruction or per-frame. Since `Vec::new()` initializes with 0 capacity, the first pushes trigger multiple rapid heap allocations before the capacity stabilizes. Pre-allocating small amounts of space avoids these constant reallocation spikes on the hot paths.

📊 **Impact:** Reduces frequent small heap allocations and allocator pressure at the beginning of frame or trace recordings, creating smoother throughput.

🔬 **Measurement:** Execute `cargo test --all-features` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` to verify stability and observe compilation/test speeds.

author: vendrabuck
body:
Fixes #106

## What the issue reported

Device boxes on the topology canvas and reservations views render as plain white boxes with no background tint and no text. PHYSICAL devices should be light-blue (`bg-blue-100` + `text-blue-900`), CLOUD light-purple (`bg-purple-100` + `text-purple-900`). The hypothesis was that these color utilities are not present in the compiled CSS because they only appear inside JavaScript object-map values composed into className strings at runtime, and Tailwind v4 content detection drops them.

## Root cause (verified empirically, and a correction to the hypothesis)

I reproduced first and the literal hypothesis does not hold on current `main`. A clean production build (`npm run build`, tailwindcss 4.3.0, `@import "tailwindcss"`, no `@source`) already emits every one of these utilities with their theme variables defined. Tailwind v4 automatic content detection scans raw file text for class-like tokens; it does not parse JS, so the strings inside object literals (`TOPOLOGY_COLORS`, `STATUS_COLORS`, `VARIANT_COLORS`) are detected just fine.

Before-fix built-CSS grep on clean `main` (the classes the issue claims are absent):

```
bg-blue-100    -> .bg-blue-100{background-color:var(--color-blue-100)}
text-blue-900  -> .text-blue-900{color:var(--color-blue-900)}
bg-purple-100  -> .bg-purple-100{background-color:var(--color-purple-100)}
text-purple-900-> .text-purple-900{color:var(--color-purple-900)}
border-blue-400-> .border-blue-400{border-color:var(--color-blue-400)}
border-purple-400 -> .border-purple-400{border-color:var(--color-purple-400)}
```

I also ruled out the other candidates: no recent change to `index.css` / `postcss.config.js` / `vite.config.ts` / `package.json` (all introduced at the initial release); the `--color-*` theme variables are defined in the emitted `:root`; the two `:root` blocks do not conflict; React Flow's stylesheet sets no `background` or `color` on any selector (so it is not whiting-out the boxes), though it is emitted unlayered before Tailwind's `@layer` blocks; and source files are not gitignored, so content detection covers `src/**`.

So the bug as literally described (classes missing from the compiled CSS) does not reproduce from current source via the production build. The real exposure is latent and fragile: the colors live only in runtime-composed strings with no safety net, so a refactor that splits a class across fragments (for example `"bg-" + shade`) would silently drop the utility and produce exactly the reported symptom (white box, no text).

## The fix

Smallest correct, app-wide change: an explicit Tailwind v4 `@source inline(...)` safelist in `frontend/src/index.css` pinning the topology and status color set, so those utilities are always emitted regardless of how the class string is assembled. This is the issue's recommended approach (safelist) and covers all the affected components in one shot (DeviceNode, TopoBadge, DeviceDetailModal, DevicePage, UserManagementTable, TopologyEditorPage).

After-fix built-CSS grep (all present): `bg-blue-{50,100,200}`, `text-blue-{700,800,900}`, `border-blue-400`, `bg-purple-{50,100,200}`, `text-purple-{700,800,900}`, `border-purple-400`, `bg-{green,yellow,red,gray}-100`, `text-{green,red,gray}-*`.

### Proof the safelist is load-bearing

To show this is not a no-op, I ran a controlled experiment simulating the exact failure mode (a refactor that hides every literal from the scanner): I replaced `bg-blue-100`/`text-blue-900` across all source files, then built with and without the safelist.

```
Refactor hides literal, NO safelist:   bg-blue-100=MISSING  text-blue-900=MISSING
Refactor hides literal, WITH safelist: bg-blue-100=PRESENT  text-blue-900=PRESENT
```

Without the safelist the classes vanish (white boxes, no text); with it they survive. The experiment files were reverted; only the safelist remains.

## Regression guards

1. `frontend/src/test/components/DeviceNode.test.tsx` (jsdom): renders DeviceNode for PHYSICAL and CLOUD devices, asserts the device name text is in the DOM and the expected color classes (`bg-blue-100`/`border-blue-400`/`text-blue-900`, and the purple set) are on the node wrapper.

2. `frontend/src/test/styles/tailwindSafelist.test.ts` (build-output): runs the real `@tailwindcss/postcss` compiler over `index.css` with the project root as base (reproducing the production pipeline) and asserts the color utilities appear in the emitted CSS. This catches a CSS-emission regression that jsdom cannot.

## Coverage gap (flagged honestly)

- A jsdom unit test cannot catch a Tailwind-CSS-generation regression: jsdom never runs the Tailwind build, so guard 1 only catches className regressions in the component, not CSS-emission regressions.
- Guard 2 closes most of that gap by compiling with the real plugin, but with one honest caveat: the plugin auto-scans `src/**` from the project base, so a class that is still written as a plain literal somewhere in the tree would keep guard 2 green even if the safelist were deleted. Guard 2 therefore protects the end-to-end property #106 cares about (the rule must exist in the compiled CSS); it does not, on its own, prove the safelist is the thing emitting it. The safelist's independent value is validated by the controlled before/after experiment above. A fully faithful guard would be an e2e/Playwright computed-style assertion against a real browser, which is out of scope here.

## Verification

- `make lint`: ruff `All checks passed!`; eslint `--max-warnings 0` exit 0.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: exit 0.
- Frontend tests: 76 files, 426 tests passed (includes the 2 new guards, 4 new assertions).
- `npm run build` (tsc + vite): succeeds; color utilities confirmed present in `dist/assets/*.css`.

## Files changed

- `frontend/src/index.css`: add `@source inline(...)` safelist.
- `frontend/src/test/components/DeviceNode.test.tsx`: new jsdom guard.
- `frontend/src/test/styles/tailwindSafelist.test.ts`: new build-output guard.
- `frontend/package.json` + `package-lock.json`: promote `postcss` to a direct devDependency for the build-output test (already present transitively; one-line lock change).

author: dkayiwa
body:
Reverts #29.

#29's "Keep the reasoning to one brief sentence" was measured on a **synthetic** chart where the ear→Hearing-Loss connection was trivial, so the verdict looked preserved. On the **real** reference-demo chart it is not: with brevity, "any ear problems?" goes back to "no records" (MISS, 2/2 deterministic); without brevity it correctly cites the Hearing Loss condition + diagnosis (HIT, 2/2). The brief reasoning starves the chain-of-thought that the #27 fix exists to provide.

The ~22% latency saving is not worth losing the core accuracy fix. Reverting restores the proven-correct behavior. A latency optimization can be revisited later, but only with **real-pipeline** validation (not synthetic).

body:
Follow-up to #607 — audits the SinterFS persistence surface for the same "written but never read back" pattern and closes the one active, high-value instance.

## Phase 1 — Audit
Full table in `docs/validation/sinter-accumulation-audit-2026-06-08.md`:

| Write path | Read-back consumer | Accumulates? | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Session turns + manifest** (`SessionGraph` 127/133, but built without `fs` at `TuiBridgeService.ts:321`) | `SessionResumer` reads in-memory `Map` only (docstring: *"ephemeral … Future: scan SinterFS"*) | **NO** — `/sessions` loses history on restart | **HIGH → fixed** |
| Archive entries | `EmergenceHooks.hydrateArchive` → gardener (#607) | YES | OK |
| Cortex goals | `GoalStore.getAll/getActiveGoals` (from disk) | YES | OK |
| Task ledger | `TaskLedger.get*` (from disk) | YES | OK |
| Gallery versions | `PreviewServer` gallery endpoints | YES | OK |
| `recordRun` (run_record) | none in repo | NO | LOW — telemetry; no consumer would justify a reader (manufacturing) |
| `writeArchiveState` | none | N/A | NONE — **zero callers** (dead) |
| `PreferenceEventsFSAdapter` | none | N/A | NONE — **never called** (only re-exported) |
| Taste model (preferences→train→weights→replay) | none invoked in live loop | N/A | OUT OF SCOPE — unwired scaffolding on *both* sides; a multi-joint feature, not a surgical read-counterpart |

## Phase 2 — Fix (session resume), #607 pattern, no new format
- `SinterFS.listManifests(prefix)` — manifest-dir enumeration counterpart to `listRefs` (shared recursive walk).
- `SessionGraph.load(fs, sessionId)` — read counterpart reconstructing a graph from persisted manifest + turns.
- `SessionResumer.hydrate(fs)` — registers persisted sessions; idempotent; empty store → no-op, never throws.
- `TuiBridgeService` — passes a shared SinterFS into `new SessionGraph` (turns now persist) and hydrates the resumer once before `/sessions` lists. Production root unchanged (cwd).

## Phase 3 — Proof of accumulation (cold 0 → hydrated 1)
`test/integration/session-resume-hydration.test.ts` (tmp `SINTER_PROJECT_ROOT`):
```
✓ first-ever hydrate of an empty store yields no sessions and does not throw
✓ a fresh resumer hydrates a session persisted by a prior process: cold 0 → hydrated 1
✓ hydrate is idempotent and accumulates multiple persisted sessions
```
Concrete assertions: cold `listSessions()` `toEqual([])`; after hydrate `loaded toBe(1)`, `turnCount toBe(2)`, restored turns `toHaveLength(2)`; multi-session `toBe(2)` then re-hydrate `toBe(0)`.

## Verification
- `pnpm build` — 0 TS errors
- `pnpm lint` — clean
- **37 files / 408 tests** pass (new + `src/fs`, `src/agent`, `src/cortex`, `src/learning`); pre-commit related run **77 files / 990 tests** pass.

Stayed clear of Agent B's territory (no `src/analytics`, `src/daemon`, `src/site`, `src/evolution`, `SiteCommand.ts`, `EvolutionIntegration.ts`, `htmlWrapper.ts`). No @sinter/core extraction.

author: kvfxkaido
body:
## What

The last follow-up from #823/#824. Semantic retrieval embeds records *on write* — but records written before the embedder existed (or during a local-model warmup window, where the provider returns lexical-now) persist with **no embedding** and stay lexical-only until rewritten. This adds a one-shot `push memory backfill` to embed them in place.

```
$ push memory backfill
Backfilling embeddings in ~/.push/memory …
  38/38 embedded
Done: 142 scanned, 38 embedded, 104 already current.
```

## Design

- **`lib/context-memory-backfill.ts`** — pure, idempotent backfill over a `ContextMemoryStore` + `EmbeddingProvider`. Batches, reports `scanned / needed / embedded / failed`.
- **Selection: missing embeddings only** (`!record.embedding`). Records already carrying a vector are left alone *even if from a different model* — re-embedding those would churn on every provider switch, and the same-model gate already handles cross-model records gracefully. Plain `!embedding` makes the pass idempotent (run twice → second finds nothing).
- **`EmbeddingProvider.warmup?()`** (new, optional) — the local provider's `embed()` is deliberately non-blocking while the model loads (correct for the agent hot path; see #824). But a backfill is explicit, user-initiated batch work where blocking is right — otherwise it'd get all-null from a still-loading model and "fail" every record. So backfill `await`s `warmup()` first; always-ready providers (remote HTTP) omit it and are treated as ready. The local `warmup()` also bypasses the transient-failure cooldown, since an explicit request should force a fresh load attempt.
- **CLI** — `push memory backfill` wires the default store + provider, streams progress + a summary to stdout, and degrades clearly when no provider is configured or the model is unavailable.

## Verification

- **6 unit tests** (deterministic, fake provider — no model load): missing-only selection, idempotency, not-ready short-circuit, partial-failure counting, empty store, filter scoping.
- **End-to-end**: seeded a record with no embedding, ran `push memory backfill`, confirmed it came back with a 768-dim `local:bge-base-en-v1.5` vector — exercising dispatch → provider → warmup → backfill → store write.
- Full CLI suite **2560/2560**, `typecheck:tsgo` clean, Biome + ESLint clean.

## Notes

- Scope is the CLI file store (`~/.push/memory`). The web IndexedDB store already embeds on write via the Worker; a browser-triggered backfill there would be a separate, UI-driven thing if ever wanted.
- Depends on the merged #824 (the local provider + warmup plumbing). Branch is cut from current `main`, which also includes the reviewer "first-open-only" fix pushed directly earlier.

author: nasyrov
body:
The core half of shareable draft preview links (#872). A draft can now be shown to someone without an account via an entry-scoped, expiring link.

**Minting** — `entry.createPreviewLink({ id })` is gated by `canReadEntry` (the same rule `entry.get`/`entry.duplicate` use), so only someone who can already see the draft — its author with `edit_own`, or an `edit_any` editor — can hand one out. It 404s (not 403) on a missing/unreadable/reserved entry so row existence isn't leaked. It returns the entry's public permalink with the token attached:

\`\`\`
{ token, url: "/post/my-draft?preview=<token>" }
\`\`\`

**Token model** — reuses the random-token-hashed-at-rest pattern already used for magic-link/invite tokens: a 192-bit random token, only its SHA-256 hash stored in the existing `auth_tokens` table (new `preview_link` type, payload `{ entryId }`, 7-day TTL, reusable until expiry). No new signing secret is introduced.

**Resolution** — the public single-entry resolver, both flat (`/post/slug`) and hierarchical (`/page/parent/child`), honours a valid `?preview=` token to reveal that one draft. It's scoped to the exact entry id, requires the URL's type+slug (and ancestor chain) to match, and never reveals a trashed row. Archive, search, front-page, and taxonomy keep their published-only gate untouched — `single` is the only widened surface.

**Deferred** (follow-ups, not blockers): a `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on preview responses so a draft's outbound assets can't leak the token, and an expiry sweep for dead `preview_link` rows. The admin "Copy preview link" button lands in a follow-up PR that closes #872.

Refs #872

author: razzamatazm
body:
## Summary

Documents a bug in `movie_output_path` (`vod_namer.py`): when a provider includes the year in the movie title (e.g. "Inception (2010)") and a year value is also extracted from `release_date` or the title itself, the filename gets the year appended twice.

- Actual: `Inception (2010) (2010).mkv`
- Expected: `Inception (2010).mkv`

Three failing tests cover the broken cases. Two control tests (title has no year, year=None) pass already, so the test file can be verified correct.

## Root cause

`movie_output_path` sanitizes the title (which preserves any existing `(YYYY)`) and then unconditionally appends `({year})`. The title and the year value both contain the same year, so it appears twice.

## Impact

IPTV providers commonly include the year in VOD movie titles. Every such download produces a non-standard filename that may confuse Plex and Jellyfin metadata matching.

Bug filed as TODO thread in #tasks.

## Test plan

- Run `python3 -m unittest tests.test_vod_namer_duplicate_year -v` on this branch: 3 tests FAIL, 2 pass.
- After the maintainer fixes `vod_namer.py`, all 5 tests should pass.

author: elares
body:
## What

Adds `docs/DURABILITY.md`, the authority for IronBus's DURABILITY CONTRACT and the levels model, plus cross-links from `docs/README.md` and `docs/WAL.md` and a terse `CHANGELOG.md` bullet. This is the M2 DESIGN deliverable for the #50 crash-injection / ack-ordering harness task (under the durability parent #6). Docs only, no source changed.

## The durability-model decision (stated honestly)

#50 assumes a menu of four durability levels (sync / batch / interval / async), each with a per-level loss guarantee. IronBus's FROZEN model is `fdatasync`-BEFORE-ack, so the doc states the honest truth:

- **v1 ships exactly ONE durability level, the safe `sync` level** = ack-implies-durable (invariant I2). A `Pub`/`PubAck` is emitted only after the covering `fdatasync` returns `Ok`; on power loss the unsynced tail is truncated and was never acked, so ACKNOWLEDGED loss is ZERO.
- The #177 append-actor **group commit AMORTIZES** the `fdatasync` (one sync per drained batch) but still acks each record only AFTER that covering sync. So the #50 "batch" level is the SAME safe level observed with the batcher on, not a relaxation, and it collapses into the `sync` row.
- The relaxed `interval` and `async` (the README's `none`) levels are **SPECIFIED, not implemented**: `interval`'s loss is BOUNDED by the flush window (time or bytes since the last completed sync), `async`'s is UNBOUNDED until the next sync. They trade durability for throughput contrary to the Edge-First safe default, so they are off by default, gated behind an explicit data-loss acknowledgement (and a #14 `durability_level` config knob), and cannot be reached from the current `serve` command line at all. The default is and remains the durable level.

## Mapping #50 acceptance to the EXISTING falsification

Every criterion is mapped to a real, named test (all verified present in the tree):

| #50 criterion | Status | Test(s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ack never precedes the level condition | PROVEN (`sync`) | `an_ack_is_sent_only_after_the_covering_fsync_completes_i2` (`actor.rs`) |
| crash drops unsynced bytes at arbitrary points; loss guarantee holds | PROVEN (`sync`) | `power_loss_at_every_boundary_no_roll` / `_with_rolling`, `power_cut_with_a_holed_unsynced_tail_loses_no_acked_record`, `power_loss_recovers_the_durable_prefix` (`crash_recovery.rs`) |
| fsyncgate: no false-success on a retried failed sync + writer freeze | PROVEN | `fatal_fsync_freeze_loses_no_acked_record`, `fatal_fsync_freeze_during_a_roll_loses_no_acked_record`, `a_sync_fault_at_any_point_loses_no_acked_record` (`crash_recovery.rs`); `Log::sync` -> `WriterFrozen` (`log.rs`) |
| crash-after-create: segments never vanish | PROVEN | parent-dir fsync in `Log::start_segment` + `recovery_fails_closed_when_a_fault_strikes_the_roll_forward` |
| group commit: syncs-per-record < 1 | PROVEN | `a_batch_of_concurrent_produces_issues_one_fdatasync_not_n` (`actor.rs`) |
| torn-mid-batch + checksum + stop-at-first-bad-frame | PROVEN | the corruption tests in `crash_recovery.rs`, the #45 corpus driven through real recovery (`conformance_recovery.rs`), and `corruption_corpus.rs` |
| per-level loss guarantee asserted (zero/bounded/declared) | PARTIAL | `sync` row proven; `interval`/`async` rows CANNOT be asserted until those levels exist |
| across-levels throughput/latency/bytes-at-risk curve on real ARM SD/eMMC for #19 | RESIDUAL (device) | not host-side reproducible (see below) |

## The residual

Two acceptance items genuinely cannot be satisfied by a design doc or in CI:

1. The **per-level loss assertions for `interval` / `async`** need those levels IMPLEMENTED first (durability #6).
2. The **across-levels throughput/latency/bytes-at-risk curve on real ARM SD/eMMC** is a DEVICE measurement: it needs both the relaxed levels and the reference hardware, must not be faked (emulated power loss cannot reproduce FTL reordering), and feeds #19 via the #111 macro-bench under the SLO ratification process. SLO.md already tables the durability modes side by side with their targets marked not-yet-ratified.

## Closes vs refs

I used **`refs #50`**, not `Closes #50`. The DESIGN deliverable is complete (the contract is specified, the existing falsification is mapped to real tests, the relaxed levels are designed with their loss bounds and opt-in contract, and the device curve is honestly scoped as a residual). But the issue's acceptance list genuinely includes items that require the relaxed levels IMPLEMENTED and the on-ARM-hardware curve RUN, neither of which is host-side or CI-achievable. So the orchestrator can decide whether to close the design and file an implementation (#6) and device (#19) follow-up, rather than this PR claiming the whole harness/levels task is done.

## Constraints honored

- No em/en dashes anywhere (verified).
- Docs only: `git status` shows only `docs/DURABILITY.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/WAL.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. No `.rs` touched, so no SPDX or fmt/clippy/test impact. Did not touch `crash_recovery.rs` / `src/fault.rs` (parallel PR #55) or `ironbus-bench` (parallel PR #284).
- All internal links resolve; every cited test name verified present in the source.

author: jasonfen
body:
Closes #63.

## What #63 was

A playtest reported that an **orbit-retrograde burn at ~45 km lunar altitude, at 1× warp**, *appeared* to reverse the orbit (vessel travelling backwards toward the dark side). The reporter (correctly) flagged it as likely a render/perception artifact and asked to disambiguate.

## Disambiguation

The physics rules out a real reversal from thrust:
- Reversing the orbit at 45 km means killing ~1.6 km/s (`v_circ` ≈ 1658 m/s).
- A few-second burn at 1× delivers only tens-to-hundreds of m/s — **two orders of magnitude short**.

So the on-screen "reversal" was a projection / day-night-terminator artifact near the disk edge. The real gap was **instrumentation** — the player had no readout to tell over-burn from frame-bug from illusion (matches issue action 1, the suspected real gap).

I also verified action 3: `StateVector.R/V` are primary-relative, and the live RK4 burn path resolves `DirectionUnit(BurnRetrograde, r, v)` on that Moon-relative state — retrograde is correctly `−v̂` in the Moon frame, **no frame bug**.

## Changes

**HUD orbit-direction indicator (action 1).** New `orbitDirectionLabel` adds an explicit `direction: prograde/retrograde` row to the **ORBIT** and **PROJECTED ORBIT** chips, keyed on the equatorial-frame inclination (>90° ⇒ retrograde, flagged). During a manual burn the live ORBIT chip updates each tick, so the player now has ground truth where the on-screen position misleads.

**Regression guard (actions 2 + 3).** `internal/sim/retrograde_lunar_burn_test.go` fires the **real `ActiveBurn` + `World.Tick` path at 1×** on an S-IVB in a 45 km prograde lunar orbit deep inside the Moon's SOI:
- A 300 m/s retrograde burn must **not** flip the equatorial-frame angular-momentum sign and must leave apo/peri sane.
- A Δv sweep through the production `DirectionUnit(BurnRetrograde)` vector pins the reversal threshold at `v_circ` — proving reversal needs ~1.6 km/s, never a 1× few-second burn. (A *sustained* burn can't even get there: it drives periapsis into the surface and the craft impacts first, so the threshold is shown impulsively.)

## Tests

- `go test ./... -race -count=1` → 1036 passed; `go vet ./...` clean.
- New: `TestModestRetrogradeBurnDoesNotReverseLunarOrbit`, `TestLunarOrbitReversalNeedsNearCircularDV`, `TestOrbitMetricsShowsDirectionIndicator`.

body:
shady.toGLSL could only emit two GLSL dialects: glslES3 ("300 es") and glslDesktop. Consumers targeting GLES2 hardware (notably the PS Vita via vitaGL/SceShaccCg, which hard-crashes at glLinkProgram on "300 es" but links "#version 100" cleanly) had no valid path: passing "100" to the string overload silently emitted desktop syntax under a #version 100 header — invalid GLSL.

Add a third GLSL dialect, glsl1WebGL (alias glslES1), emitting valid GLSL ES 1.00. ES1 is not stage-agnostic the way in/out is, so emission is now stage-aware:

- vertex inputs -> attribute, vertex outputs -> varying, fragment inputs -> varying
- the single user fragment output is rewritten to the builtin gl_FragColor (declaration dropped, references renamed); >1 output is a hard error (no gl_FragData[i] in v1)
- texture() -> texture2D()/textureCube() by sampler type
- mandatory stage-aware float precision: "precision mediump float;" in the fragment stage (highp-default vertex emits none), matching raylib's working Vita reference
- stage inference also scans the proc body for a gl_Position write, so a module-global gl_Position (assigned in the body, not a param) classifies the shader as vertex — required for the no-stage string overload

Fail loud (Nim compile-time error) under glslES1 on constructs ES1 cannot express, instead of emitting GLSL that crashes vitaGL's link-time translate: switch/case, round, inverse, derivatives, textureSize/textureGrad/texelFetch/ textureLod, non-float varyings, and integer bitwise/modulo operators (operand- type-checked so logical &&/|| stay legal).

Behavior change: toGLSL(p, "100" | "100 es", ...) now routes to glslES1. The old output for "100" was invalid GLSL, so any caller relying on it was already broken.

The gl_FragCoord origin_upper_left qualifier is now gated on `notin {glslES3, glsl1WebGL}` rather than `!= glslES3`; under ES1 gl_FragCoord is also skipped from declaration (redeclaring the builtin is illegal in ES1).

Zero change to glslES3/glsl3Desktop/glsl4Desktop/vulkanGlsl450/hlslDX12/metalMSL output (golden master: 41 insertions, 0 deletions). New ES1 coverage added to the golden test and to test_backends (positive output + fail-loud guards + no false positives on other targets).

## Summary

Adds basic script-runtime support for common spawn/helper routines seen during normal K1 module loading.

- implements `SetIsDestroyable` using supported engine state: `Plot` and `Min1HP`
- implements `GetHasSpell` using loaded creature known-spell data from `KnownList0`
- adds a conservative `GetIsEncounterCreature` implementation that validates the object is a creature and returns false until encounter-spawn ownership is represented in engine state

## Notes

Remaining warnings such as `GetAttemptedSpellTarget`, `SetCustomToken`, and fade routines are intentionally left for separate slices.

## Manual smoke:

- `tar_m03af`: target warnings for `SetIsDestroyable`, `GetHasSpell`, and `GetIsEncounterCreature` are gone
- remaining missing-routine warnings are unrelated/out of scope: `GetAttemptedSpellTarget`, `SetCustomToken`, `SetGlobalFadeIn`

author: heodongun
body:
## Summary
- allow `scripts/verify-real-device-e2e.sh` to fill manual KakaoTalk evidence fields from `MANUAL_KAKAO_*` environment variables
- preserve safe false/blank defaults for template-only runs
- document how to pass notification access, room/sender, IN/OUT log, visible reply, and note evidence into the E2E summary

## Why
The automated model/device proof and the manual KakaoTalk proof need to land in one artifact. Previously `--print-manual-template` and generated summaries always emitted static placeholders, so a physical-device run could not capture verified KakaoTalk evidence without editing the summary afterward.

## Validation
- `scripts/verify-real-device-e2e.sh --print-manual-template`
- `MANUAL_KAKAO_* scripts/verify-real-device-e2e.sh --print-manual-template`
- `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug assembleRelease`
- `git diff --check`

## Remaining real-device constraint
- `scripts/verify-real-device-e2e.sh` still requires exactly one attached Android device. Current local `adb devices -l` reports no attached devices, so the physical KakaoTalk notification/RemoteInput proof is still not complete from this machine.

author: copilot
body:
`SearchService.SearchContent` could time out even for trivial queries while the `BleveIndex` queue was active and growing. The failure mode was lock contention in the Bleve wrapper: search requests waited behind write-side reindex work instead of querying the current index snapshot.

- **Search path**
  - Removed the read lock from `QueryWithTags`, so content searches no longer wait on the wrapper’s mutation lock while background Bleve jobs are reindexing pages.
  - Kept write-side locking around the delete/reindex sequence so page mutation remains serialized where it needs to be.

- **Lock scope**
  - Narrowed the mutex contract from “all Bleve operations” to “multi-step mutation coordination”.
  - This aligns the wrapper with Bleve’s concurrent read/write model instead of turning every active index write into a search bottleneck.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Added a focused concurrency test that fails if a query blocks behind the indexer mutation lock.

```go
type Index struct {
	index              bleve.Index
	pageReader         wikipage.PageReader
	frontmatterQueryer frontmatter.IQueryFrontmatterIndex
	mu                 sync.Mutex // Serializes multi-step delete/reindex mutations
}

func (b *Index) QueryWithTags(text string, requiredTags []string, boostTokens []string) ([]SearchResult, error) {
	q := buildSearchQuery(text, requiredTags, boostTokens)
	searchReq := bleve.NewSearchRequest(q)
	// ...
	return results, nil
}
```

author: alanvito1
body:
## Summary

This PR proposes a deliberate scarcity adjustment to the mint drop weights for the new **High Tier NFTs** (rarities 6–9), reducing their probability by 100× to properly reflect their status as next-generation, ultra-rare assets.

## Motivation

When the advanced rarities (Mega, Super Mega, Mystic, Super Mystic) were introduced, their drop weights were defined as integers on the same scale as the classic rarities (0–5). This placed their combined mint probability at ~0.36%, which — while low — does not adequately distinguish them as a fundamentally different class of NFT.

These four tiers represent the **High Tier NFT generation**: assets with superior stats, expanded ability pools, and designed scarcity. Their rarity must signal exclusivity at the economic and gameplay level.

## Change

| Rarity | Name | Old Weight | New Weight | Old Chance | New Chance |
|--------|------|-----------|-----------|------------|------------|
| 6 | Mega | 22 | 0.22 | 0.2200% | 0.0022% |
| 7 | Super Mega | 9 | 0.09 | 0.0900% | 0.0009% |
| 8 | Mystic | 4 | 0.04 | 0.0400% | 0.0004% |
| 9 | Super Mystic | 1 | 0.01 | 0.0100% | 0.0001% |

**Combined High Tier chance: ~0.0036%** (previously 0.36%)

Classic rarities (0–5) are **unchanged**.

## Design Philosophy

High Tier NFTs should be treated as a new generation — comparable to ultra-rare collectibles in traditional gaming economies. A player might never see one drop in thousands of mints. This creates:

- Genuine secondary market value
- Long-term demand for mint activity
- Clear differentiation from the classic tier ceiling (Super Legend, rarity 5)

## Files Changed

- `server/BombChainExtension/src/com/senspark/game/data/model/ServerHeroDetails.kt` — `dropRateNew` list, indices 6–9

## Test Plan

- [ ] Verify `dropRateNew` values at line 159 of `ServerHeroDetails.kt`
- [ ] Run mint simulation: confirm High Tier NFTs appear at ~0.0036% combined rate
- [ ] Confirm classic rarities (0–5) percentages are unaffected
- [ ] New total weight: ~9964.36 → Common = 8118/9964.36 = 81.47% ✓

body: ## Summary - honor Factory CLI compaction token defaults and per-model overrides in session creation, live session updates, and agent model changes - map mission worker/validator model and reasoning settings into Droid mission settings instead of keeping them UI-only - stop preloading model and skill catalogs during app startup; lazy-load skills on slash menu use and cache model catalog refreshes ## Why Startup was doing unnecessary Droid work before normal chats needed it, and frontend settings were not fully reflected in sidecar session and mission payloads. This makes normal sessions snappier while preserving the selected model/reasoning/compaction settings when a prompt is actually sent. ## Validation - `npm test` - `npm run sidecar:test` - `npm run typecheck` - `npm run sidecar:typecheck` - `npm run build` --- ## Summary by cubic Honors Factory CLI session defaults and per‑model compaction limits across creates, live updates, and agent changes with catalog‑backed validation. Speeds up startup by serving models from a local cache, refreshing in the background, and loading skills only when the slash menu opens. - **New Features** - Apply CLI compaction defaults and per‑model limits for orchestrator and session updates; clearing limits disables threshold checks, and we choose the agent’s default model when unset. - Map worker/validator model and reasoning into Droid `missionSettings` so missions match UI choices. - Persist compaction limits in history; add `compactionTokenLimit` and `compactionTokenLimitPerModel` to `mission.create`, `session.create`, `session.updateSettings`, and `settings.agent.update`. - Validate Factory defaults against the model catalog; on cold start without a cache, seed only safe compaction settings; at runtime, preserve saved model choices if the catalog is unavailable. - **Refactors** - Cache the model catalog from `droid --help` at `~/.factory/droid-control/model-catalog.json`; read from cache on first load, emit immediately, and refresh in the background. - Lazy‑load skills per session on slash use; include `sessionId` in `catalog.updated` (skills) and filter in the UI. author: squall321
body:
## NEXT_STEPS §2.4 — `launcher_agents` router (enroll / refresh / manifest + Phase 2 stubs)

Wires §2.2 (JWT auth) and §2.3 (manifest builder) to the HTTP surface under `/api/v1/launcher-agents`, kept separate from the polling `/api/v1/agents` routes so the two request shapes never collide (contract `openapi.yaml` v0.2.0).

| Method | Path | Phase 1 | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/enroll` | **real** → `redeem_enrollment_token` | none (`security:[]`) |
| POST | `/refresh` | **real** → `rotate_refresh` | none (`security:[]`) |
| GET | `/manifest` | **real** → `cached_manifest` | launcher JWT |
| POST | `/installs` | 501 stub | launcher JWT |
| POST | `/audit` | 501 stub | launcher JWT |
| POST | `/heartbeat` | 501 stub | launcher JWT |

### Audience isolation (both directions, tested end-to-end)
- `get_launcher_agent` enforces `aud='hwax-agent'` via `verify_agent_jwt` → a **user token is rejected** on `/manifest` (401).
- A **launcher token is rejected on user routes** by the existing audience-less `get_current_user` decode — `GET /api/v1/users/me` with a launcher token → 401. **No change to `deps.py` needed** (this falls out of the §2.2 `decode_token` audience logic).

### Portal `/heax-hub` correctness
Manifest installer-download URLs are built from a public base derived from `X-Forwarded-Proto/Host/Prefix`, so they're correct when the portal proxies us under `/heax-hub` (Caddy strips that prefix before forwarding, so the backend only learns it from `X-Forwarded-Prefix`). ⚠️ **If the portal/Caddy does not forward `X-Forwarded-Prefix`**, set the new `agent_public_base_url` (e.g. `https://hwax.sec.samsung.net/heax-hub`) — it overrides the header derivation. Please confirm which the deployment does.

### Contract fidelity
`EnrollOut`/`RefreshOut` (and the request models) use `extra='forbid'`, mirroring the contract's `additionalProperties:false` — the happy-path tests assert the response key set is exactly `{agent_id, access_token, refresh_token, expires_in}` / `{access_token, refresh_token, expires_in}`, and an unknown request field → 422. Stubs require the launcher JWT now (auth wired), so Phase 2 only adds body handling: anonymous → 401, authed → 501.

### Tests
`TestClient` against the real app, but `get_db` is overridden to a savepoint-bound session ⇒ **everything rolls back** (skips when Postgres unreachable): enroll happy path + access-token-drives-manifest, unknown-token 401, service-agent 403, extra-field 422, token-burn-on-second-enroll, refresh rotation + reuse-401, manifest-needs-bearer 401, manifest-rejects-user-token 401, launcher-token-on-`/users/me` 401, stubs 501-when-authed + 401-when-anonymous.

### ⚠️ Verification the maintainer must run before merge
No Postgres here; only `python -m py_compile` was run (passes). Please run:
```bash
cd backend && pytest app/tests/test_launcher_agents.py
```

### Stacking
Stacked on `hwax-agent/backend-manifest-builder` (§2.3, PR #6). **Base this PR against that branch**; merge after #6. Final piece: §2.5 `GET /api/v1/installers/{id}/download` (the 302 the manifest URLs point at).

body:
## What

Adds a **"Tell me anything"** free-text extraction panel to the Discovery page, **above the AI Mirror panel** (order: dump-mode → AI Understanding → pattern blocks).

- **Input** (`#dumpModePanel`, navy `#0d2137`): a textarea labelled **"Describe this process in your own words"** (placeholder: *"Paste meeting notes, a rough description, an email — anything. I'll extract what's relevant."*) with a teal **"Extract and Fill"** button below it.
- **On click**: `POST /api/dump-extract` with `{ text, grid }`. Empty textarea is **toast-guarded**; the button is never hard-disabled (soft re-entrancy guard + an "Extracting…" state).
- **Confirmation**: on a successful response it shows *"Found: X steps, Y personas, Z systems — Apply to grid?"* with a teal **Apply** and a grey **Discard** button.
- **Apply**: merges extracted steps into `state.workflowGrid` — matches existing steps by name, adds new ones otherwise, and **never overwrites a `"confirmed"` cell** (filled cells become `inferred`). Sets `workflowName` only if the grid has none. Toasts **"Workflow updated from your description"**.
- **Server** `handleDumpExtract(req, res)` (raw `http`, `readJson`/`sendJson`, no Express): calls `claude-sonnet-4-6` (`max_tokens: 1500`) with the raw text + a summary of the current grid, returns `{ extracted: { workflowName, steps: [{name, personaActors, systemsTools, painFriction, output}] } }`, **JSON-only with defensive parse** (strips code fences, falls back to the first `{…}`). 400 on empty text or missing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

## Notes
- **No new CSS variables** (inline styles); **no schema changes** — dump text/result/loading are module-level vars. Re-render is focus-safe (won't clobber the textarea mid-type).
- Based on `main` after #54 and #56 merged, so the panel sits correctly above AI Mirror.

## Testing

author: wookieejedi
body:
Fixes #7508.

The subsystem flag "ignore if dead" that many mods use is supposed to "prevent homing weapons from attempting to hit the now destroyed submodel and instead tells them to home on the main hull of the target."

Though, in actuality, the code makes the weapon dumb fire instead of home. This bug means if you destroy a subsystem with this flag, then lock onto it with an aspect weapon and fire the weapon, the weapon will just dumb fire.

With `wp->homing_subsys` cleared as this PR does, the homing code at `weapons.cpp`:5730 falls into its else branch and picks an attack point on the ship body (`ai_big_pick_attack_point / hobjp->pos`) — which is what the flag promises. Javelins, which can only home on engines, will still just drop lock if there's none though (edited for correction, previously stated javelins would acquire a new engine).

This fix is tested and now the flag works as expected.

author: ziliangpeng
body:
## Summary

Replace the dynamic np.concatenate-based KV cache with a pre-allocated
array + slice-write pattern. Eliminates O(T²) memory allocation overhead.

### Changes

- **_init_cache()** now allocates (n_kv_head, max_seq, d_k) arrays
  once. Defaults to config.max_position_embeddings (8192).
- **_cache_len** tracks populated positions instead of deriving from
  cache[0]['k'].shape[1].
- **Prefill**: slice-write into cache['k'][:, :seq, :].
- **Decode**: slice-write into the next position
  cache['k'][:, prev_seq:prev_seq+seq, :].
- **Attention**: k_view / v_view sliced to total_after positions.
- No np.concatenate in the forward pass.

### Verification

- 85/85 regression tests: ✅
- Real-weight correctness vs HF: ✅ (cosine >0.999, top-5 35/35, decode 3/3 match)
- H100 benchmark:

| Case | Steps | Total | Per-step |
|------|-------|-------|----------|
| 8+50 | 51 | 19.54s | **383ms** |
| 8+200 | 201 | 72.88s | **363ms** |

Per-step time is constant (~360-380ms), confirming O(T) scaling.

author: pkgdemon
body:
Fixes **#252** and **#148** — the real cause of the PR nextbsd#250 boot panic (`page fault, write 0x70`, proc 1 `DispatchWorker`). #253 (pset ref+revalidate) was necessary but didn't fix this; root-caused by a 4-agent static review (see the [plan](https://pkgdemon.github.io/nextbsd-evfilt-machport-native-plan.html)).

### Root cause (source-confirmed)
`kqueue_register` calls the filter's `f_event` (`filt_machport`, `hint=0`) for initial state during `EV_ADD`. `filt_machport` does `self->ith_msg_addr = kn->kn_ext[0]` with `self = current_thread()` = `curthread->td_machdata`. A libdispatch `DispatchWorker` (pthread-workqueue) thread reaches the filter **without ever issuing a guarded Mach trap**, so `td_machdata` (and sometimes `p_machdata`) is **NULL** — the per-thread Mach eventhandlers are compiled out (`mach_thread.c` `#if 0`). `self == NULL`, and `ith_msg_addr` sits at **offset `0x70`** of `struct thread_shuttle` → write to `0x70`, page-not-present. Exact match.

### Fix
Lazily promote the caller to full Mach state at filter entry, reusing the proven `mach_task_init_lazy()` / `mach_thread_init_lazy()` helpers the syscall wrappers already use (`mach_syscall_wire.c`):
- new `filt_mach_state_init()` — inits per-process task + per-thread shuttle; idempotent, race-safe, **no IPC lock held** (no lock-order risk).
- called at the top of `filt_machportattach` (covers `current_space()` at translate + re-lookup) and in `filt_machport`'s `hint==0` arm, which then **re-reads `self`** (covers `self->ith_*`, `ipc_mqueue_pset_receive`, `mach_msg_receive_results`).
- `filt_machportdetach` derefs no Mach state — unchanged.
- On allocation failure both paths degrade to a clean knote teardown, not a panic.

Makes worker-thread `EVFILT_MACHPORT` registration **actually work** (not merely not-panic) → unblocks #250. Complements #253 + #29.

### Validation
The #250 boot panics deterministically today at this exact site; with this fix it must boot clean past launchd. A standalone concurrency stress test (#251) follows to catch regressions in isolation.

author: anshul23102
body:
## Summary

Closes #39

The drop zone advertised **"Drag & drop or paste text"** in its heading but had **zero drag event handlers**, making the feature entirely non-functional — dropping a file produced no effect at all.

---

## Root Cause

`document-input.tsx` was missing `onDragEnter`, `onDragLeave`, `onDragOver`, and `onDrop` handlers on the container `<div>`. Without `onDragOver` calling `e.preventDefault()`, browsers never consider the element a valid drop target and will not fire the `drop` event.

---

## What Changed

### `src/components/legiflow/document-input.tsx`

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Drag events | None | `onDragEnter`, `onDragLeave`, `onDragOver`, `onDrop` |
| Visual feedback | Static dashed border, always the same | Border turns `border-primary` + `bg-primary/5`; full-zone overlay with upload icon appears |
| Drag counter | N/A | `dragCounter` ref prevents `isDragging` flicker when pointer crosses child elements |
| File reading | Not implemented | `FileReader.readAsText()` populates textarea from `.txt` / `.md` / `.mdx` drops |
| Text drag | Not implemented | `dataTransfer.getData('text/plain')` handles dragged text selections |
| Error feedback | None | `role="alert"` error message shown for unsupported types or read failures |

### Key Implementation Details

**Drag counter pattern** — a `useRef(0)` counter is incremented on `dragenter` and decremented on `dragleave`. `isDragging` is set to `true` on the first enter and cleared to `false` only when the counter returns to 0. This prevents the common flickering bug where dragging over a child element triggers a `dragleave` on the parent.

**`onDragOver` must call `preventDefault()`** — without this, the browser does not recognise the element as a drop target and the `drop` event never fires (the original bug).

**`e.dataTransfer.dropEffect = 'copy'`** — communicates the intended action to the OS, showing the correct cursor.

**File type validation** — checks `file.type.startsWith('text/')` and the file extension against `['.txt', '.md', '.text', '.mdx']` before attempting to read. Unsupported files surface a clear user-facing error.

**Drag counter reset on drop** — counter is unconditionally reset to 0 in `handleDrop` to keep state consistent regardless of how many children were involved.

---

## Testing

1. Open the document input page.
2. Drag a `.txt` file over the drop zone — border turns primary, overlay appears.
3. Release the file — textarea is populated with file content.
4. Drag a `.md` file — same behaviour.
5. Drag an unsupported file (e.g. `.png`) — error message appears below textarea.
6. Drag a text selection from another tab — textarea is populated.
7. Drag into the textarea child element specifically — no flickering; state remains consistent.
8. Confirm paste still works as before.

---

## Labels Request

This PR resolves a **Level 2 bug** (labelled `bug`, `frontend`, `ui/ux`, `GSSoC 26`, `Level 2` on the issue). Could you please add the following labels to this PR?

- `gssoc-approved`
- `Level 2`
- `bug`
- `frontend`

These labels are important for GSSoC 2026 point tracking. Thank you!

## 관련 이슈

closes #70 

## 변경사항

ISBN을 기준으로 네이버 도서 API를 호출해 도서 정보를 조회하는 기능을 구현했습니다.

API 명세서 기준으로 `GET /api/books/info?isbn={isbn}` API를 추가했습니다.

이번 이슈에서는 `RestTemplate` 방식으로 네이버 도서 API 연동을 먼저 구현했습니다.

이후 별도 이슈에서 `RestClient` 방식으로 교체할 예정입니다.

### 1. 네이버 API 설정 추가

`external.naver` 설정값을 바인딩하는 `NaverProperties`를 추가했습니다.

네이버 API 호출 전용 `RestTemplate` 설정을 추가했습니다.

### 2. 네이버 도서 API Client 추가

`NaverBookClient`를 추가해 네이버 도서 API 호출 책임을 분리했습니다.

ISBN을 `query` 파라미터로 전달하고, `display=1`, `start=1`, `sort=sim` 조건으로 네이버 도서 API를 호출하도록 구현했습니다.

### 3. 네이버 응답 DTO 추가

네이버 도서 API 응답을 매핑하기 위해 `NaverBookSearchDto`, `NaverBookItemDto`를 추가했습니다.

프로젝트 네이밍 규칙에 맞춰 외부 API 응답 매핑 객체도 `Dto` 접미사를 사용했습니다.

### 4. 도서 정보 조회 응답 DTO 추가

`GET /api/books/info` 응답으로 사용할 `BookInfoDto`를 추가했습니다.

네이버 API 응답을 도서 등록 화면에서 사용할 수 있는 형태로 변환해 반환합니다.

### 5. 도서 정보 조회 API 추가

`BookController`에 `GET /api/books/info?isbn={isbn}` API를 추가했습니다.

**`/info` 경로가 `/{bookId}`로 해석되지 않도록 단건 조회 API보다 위에 선언했습니다.**

### 6. Service 로직 추가

ISBN 형식을 검증하고, 네이버 도서 API를 호출한 뒤, 응답 결과를 `BookInfoDto`로 변환하는 로직을 추가했습니다.

네이버 응답에 포함될 수 있는 HTML 태그와 HTML 엔티티를 정리하도록 처리했습니다.

### 7. 예외 처리 추가

잘못된 ISBN 형식에 대한 예외를 추가했습니다.

네이버 API 조회 결과가 없을 때의 예외를 추가했습니다.

네이버 API 설정 누락 또는 호출 실패에 대한 예외를 추가했습니다.

### 8. API 문서 추가

`BookInfoApi` 문서 어노테이션을 추가했습니다.

200, 400, 404, 500 응답 케이스를 문서화했습니다.

## Summary
> Add the regression test + cross-OS CI that should have caught the macOS installer breakage (issue #39).

Closes #39.

The actual code fix already landed upstream (`e31722c`, literal space in the sed expression). This PR adds the **safety nets** that were missing — the buggy function `get_latest_version` had no test, and shell scripts weren't exercised in CI at all, which is why a BSD-vs-GNU sed bug shipped.

## Type
- [ ] feat  - [ ] fix  - [ ] docs  - [ ] refactor  - [x] test  - [ ] chore

## Changes
- **Regression test** (`tests/install_test.bats` + `tests/fixtures/release.json`): hermetic test for `get_latest_version` — stubs `download()` to copy a fixture GitHub-API response (no network) and asserts the parsed tag is exactly `v0.3.13` with no spaces/quotes. Runs on the host's own `sed`, so the BSD (macOS) vs GNU (Ubuntu) difference is exercised. The old `\s` expression returns `  "tag_name": "v0.3.13",` on BSD sed → fails both assertions.
- **`install.sh`**: run `main()` only when executed or piped, not when sourced, so tests can load the functions without triggering a real install. Verified `main` still runs under `./install.sh` **and** `curl … | bash` (the piped path was the tricky one — the naive `BASH_SOURCE==$0` guard breaks it; used `(return 0 2>/dev/null)` sourced-detection instead).
- **CI** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`): new `install-script` job on the `macos-latest` + `ubuntu-latest` matrix running `shellcheck --severity=warning install.sh` + `bats tests/`. This is the authoritative cross-platform gate — pre-push only runs on the pusher's OS.
- **`.githooks/pre-push`** (opt-in): runs shellcheck + bats locally for fast feedback. Enable with `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`.

## Testing

author: ampiazza
body:
## Summary

Adds `.github/workflows/release.yml` so future releases happen automatically when a SemVer tag is pushed.

## What it does

On `push` of a tag matching `v*.*.*`:

1. Checks out the tagged commit
2. **Verifies the tag matches `package.json` version** (fails fast on mismatch — catches "I tagged v0.2.0 but forgot to bump package.json" before anything publishes)
3. Sets up Node 20 with npm cache
4. `npm ci`
5. `npm run build`
6. `npm run package`
7. Renames the zip to `ollama-sidekick-v{tag}.zip` so each release artifact is uniquely named
8. Creates a GitHub Release with the zip attached and auto-generated changelog (from PR titles since the previous tag)
9. Marks pre-release tags (containing `-`, e.g. `v1.0.0-beta.1`) as prereleases automatically

## Future release flow

```
# 1. Bump version in package.json on main via PR
# 2. After merge:
git tag v0.2.0
git push origin v0.2.0
# 3. Workflow runs and creates the Release
```

## Deferred

Chrome Web Store auto-upload via `chrome-webstore-upload-cli` is **not** included yet. That requires OAuth refresh-token setup in repo secrets and is worth deferring until first manual CWS publish has proven the listing flow.

## Test plan

- [x] YAML syntactically valid
- [ ] After merge, next tag push (v0.2.0 or similar) should produce a Release identical in shape to the manually-created v0.1.0
- [ ] The version-mismatch guard should fire if someone tags without bumping package.json

author: atzurody
body:
Two independent papercuts that surface when building real multi-file programs
(both pass `almide check` / `almide test` but break `almide build`).

## 1. `almide build -o <dir>/<bin>` doesn't create the output directory

```
$ almide build src/main.almd -o build/app
Compile error: …                 # actually compiles fine
Failed to copy binary to build/app: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

The compile succeeds; only the final copy fails because `build/` doesn't
exist. `-o <dir>/<bin>` is the natural way to place a binary, so every caller
otherwise needs a manual `mkdir -p`. Fix: create the output's parent dir
before copying (`src/cli/build.rs`).

## 2. auto-? unwraps the Result argument of `result.*` / `option.*` functions

The auto-? pass wraps every Result-typed call in a `Try`, including a call
passed as the **first argument** to a `result.*` / `option.*` function — which
consumes it *as* a Result (UFCS: `r.unwrap_or(d)` == `result.unwrap_or(r, d)`):

```almide
effect fn main() -> Unit = {
  let cap = result.unwrap_or(int.parse(env.get("CAP") ?? ""), 512)  // lowered to (int.parse(...))?
  ...
}
```

lowered to `result.unwrap_or((int.parse(...))?, 512)` — unwrapping the very
Result the callee needs → `error[E0308]: expected Result<i64,_>, found i64`
at `almide build` (passes check/test). It also bites effect-fn call sites
(typed `Result[T,String]`) consumed by `result.unwrap_or`, e.g.
`result.unwrap_or(run_once(), seq)`.

Fix: same shape as the existing `??` (UnwrapOr) and match-subject exceptions —
suppress the top-level auto-? on the first arg of `result.*` / `option.*`
calls (`crates/almide-frontend/src/lower/auto_try.rs`).

## Verification

- Repro (both patterns + `-o build/x` into a missing dir) builds and runs.
- Spec suite green with the patch: **stdlib 100 / lang 121 / integration 27**, 0 failures.

Found while building the Fizz component repos (multi-package CLIs) on v0.25.

author: a-whitmore-exec
body:
## Problem

A wedged outbound send could lock out the entire gateway — and it was unrecoverable remotely.

When Telegram's API became unreachable (TLS handshake timeouts to `api.telegram.org`), the send path had **no timeout anywhere** in the chain:

1. `tgbotapi`'s HTTP client had no timeout → `bot.Send` blocked forever.
2. The daemon socket handler passed an unbounded `context` to the send.
3. The `goat send_user_message` client had no read deadline → blocked forever waiting on the daemon.

So: the send blocked forever → the runtime (`claude -p`) that spawned the client blocked forever → the session never returned to idle → new inbound messages queued behind it indefinitely. The watchdog only checked `kill -0` (process alive), so it saw the **live-but-wedged** daemon as healthy and did nothing.

Observed: two `goat send_user_message` processes stuck for ~2 days, holding the session open, with all message processing blocked.

## Fix — three layers of defense

**1. Bound the actual send (root cause)**
- **telegram**: give the bot a 60s HTTP client timeout — above the 30s `getUpdates` long-poll, below the client deadline. `bot.Send` ignores `context`, so this transport-level cap is the real fix.
- **slack**: switch outbound `PostMessage` → `PostMessageContext` so it honors the daemon's deadline.
- **daemon**: wrap each send in a 45s `context.WithTimeout`.

**2. Client can't hang either**
- `send_user_message` / `send_user_file` set a 90s `conn.SetDeadline`, so a wedged handler can't hang the helper (or the runtime blocked on it). Layered: **45s send < 60s transport < 90s client**.

**3. Readiness, not just liveness**
- new `goated daemon status --probe` does a bounded socket round-trip; exits non-zero if the daemon is down **or** alive-but-wedged.
- watchdog now probes every run and force-restarts on an unresponsive socket, reaps `send_user_message`/`send_user_file` helpers older than 10 min, and takes a lock so overlapping runs don't fight during a multi-minute restart.

## Testing
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt` clean; `bash -n scripts/watchdog.sh` clean.
- `daemon status --probe` returns healthy (exit 0) against a live daemon and non-zero when down; verified backward-compatible (new probe round-trips against an older running daemon).
- etime→seconds parser verified for `mm:ss`, `hh:mm:ss`, and `dd-hh:mm:ss` (macOS `ps` has no `etimes` column).

body:
## 概要

tmux finder(`prefix+T` / `prefix+G`)を **Panda 配色のツリー表示**に刷新する。

- **worktree も「同一リポジトリ」でグループ化**(ghq と同じツリー)。`host/owner/repo` を見出しに、branch を配下に `├─/└─` でぶら下げる。両モードのツリー描画を共通化。
- **Panda カラーでカラフルに**: 見出し=**pink 太字** / 枝罫線=**subtle** / branch=**mint**・repo=**cyan**。fzf UI も Panda(pointer=pink・prompt=mint・hl=cyan)。

```
github.com/Hirayama61/dotfiles      ← pink(見出し)
├─ feat/foo                          ← mint(branch)
└─ main
github.com/Hirayama61/cc-dotfiles
└─ fix/script-review-bugs
```

## 実装

- **`jump.sh` を `.tmpl` 化**(cheatsheet と同方式)。`{{ .panda.X.rgb }}` を ANSI truecolor に、`.hex` を `fzf --color` に展開。popup は `FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS` / PATH を継がない場合があるため `--color` を明示 + 冒頭で `fzf` 不在チェック(無言終了を防ぐ)。
- **検索性を維持**: 表示は色付きツリー(`--with-nth=1`)、検索は隠し列に `group/leaf` を入れて `--nth=2`。**repo 名でも branch 名でも owner 名でも絞れる**(前回 ghq ツリーで失われた owner 検索もこれで復活)。
- 見出し行は隠し列(search/path)を空にして**選択 no-op**・**preview 即終了**(空走査回避)。
- 宣言を先頭に集約(トップレベル実行で `local` 再宣言が `name=value` を表示する zsh 仕様の回避)。

## レビュー / テスト

- self-review(code-reviewer / security-reviewer + Codex)実施。
  - security: 選択値は `tmux -c "$target"` に引数渡し(再パースなし)、preview `{3}` は fzf 単引用符化、色は固定 chezmoi 値 — 注入面なしを実機/バイナリで裏取り。
  - Codex 指摘(見出しの preview 空走査・コメント精度・fzf 不在の無言終了)を反映。
- `chezmoi execute-template` で展開 → `zsh -n` clean。スタブで両モードのツリー・no-op 見出し・dispatch・検索列を確認。

> 注: popup 内の見た目(色・ツリー)は対話 UI のため、マージ + `mise run apply` + `prefix+r` 後に実機確認をお願いします。色味の好みは `C_HEAD`/`C_LEAF`/`C_TREE` の Panda 色を差し替えれば調整できます。

Salvages PR #33221 (@draix) onto current `main`. VolcEngine's `api/plan` endpoint leaks raw XML attribute fragments into `tool_use.name` (e.g. `terminal" parameter="command" string="true`), so every tool call fails after 3 retries and aborts as partial. This adds a minimal sanitizer at the top of `repair_tool_call` that trims at the first `"`/`'`/`<`/`>` character, letting the existing normalize/fuzzy pipeline resolve the cleaned name.

Upstream is a VolcEngine server-side translation bug (parser splits the opening tag at whitespace, not at `>`); the reporter can't reach VolcEngine and has no alternate endpoint, so a defensive Hermes-side fix is the only mitigation for affected users.

## Changes
- `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`: 4-line XML-fragment strip in `repair_tool_call`, before `_norm` (@draix)
- `tests/run_agent/test_repair_tool_call_name.py`: 11 regression cases for the polluted-name patterns (@draix)
- `scripts/release.py`: AUTHOR_MAP entry `martin.alca@gmail.com -> draix` (the commit's authoring email, distinct from the already-mapped `draixagent@gmail.com`)

## Validation
- Reproduced on current `main`: polluted names (`terminal"...`, `execute_code"...`, `session_search"...`) all return `None` → tool call dies. With the fix they recover to the real tool.
- All 71 registered tool names are clean `snake_case` — none contain `"`/`'`/`<`/`>`/space, so the sanitizer can never truncate a valid name.
- Whitespace deliberately excluded: `"write file" -> write_file` repair path preserved.
- `idx > 0` guard leaves leading-quote names for the fuzzy path.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `terminal" parameter="command" string="true` | Unknown tool → partial abort | routes to `terminal` |
| `write file` (legit multi-word) | `write_file` | `write_file` (unchanged) |
| `no_such_tool" parameter="x"...` | `None` | `None` (invalid root still rejected) |

Tests: `tests/run_agent/test_repair_tool_call_name.py` 29/29 pass (18 pre-existing #14784 + 11 new). Repair argument/streaming suites: 62/62.

Fixes #33007. Supersedes #33221 (cherry-picked with @draix's authorship preserved).

## Summary
Adds a **Generate Missing Descriptions…** action to the catalog tree's schema and table context menus, so undocumented assets can be filled in bulk instead of one dialog at a time.

Flow (wizard-first, AMX convention):
1. Scope pick — tables only, or tables + columns.
2. Enumerate undocumented assets from the catalog cache and show the count ("N tables, M columns — generation consumes tokens on the active LLM") **before** any LLM call.
3. Multi-select QuickPick (all pre-checked) to trim the batch.
4. Cancellable progress notification runs the existing `POST /api/generate/table|column` endpoints through a 3-wide concurrency pool; per-asset failures are collected, not fatal; cancelling keeps what was already generated.
5. Review QuickPick — generated rows pre-checked, failed rows shown unchecked with the error.
6. Apply to catalog (local override) or database (`COMMENT ON`) via the existing `comments.*` client methods, then invalidate the cache and refresh the tree.

Client-side orchestration over the existing endpoints — no new server endpoint, no Studio-bundle change.

## Modularity
Pure logic (`enumerateMissing` / `generateOne` / `applyOne`) lives in `bulkGenerateCore.ts` with no vscode import; the vscode UI orchestration is in `bulkGenerate.ts`. A reusable bounded-concurrency `mapPool` helper lands in `util/async.ts`.

## Test plan
- New `test/unit/bulkGenerate.test.ts` (enumerate filtering, profile fallback, column inclusion, generate success/failure capture, apply routing) and `test/unit/async.test.ts` (`mapPool` concurrency width, cancellation, index alignment). 92 unit tests green.
