- DocFetchService: save prep encodes tildes, verification accepts entity-encoded returns
- Export transforms: HTML/MD exports preserve lone tildes

author: orendor
body:
## What

`ssh` was unconditionally `high_stakes`, so read-only remote diagnostics (e.g. `ssh -o ConnectTimeout=15 ubuntu@ec2-… 'npm list -g | grep @oked'`) fired "irreversible action" approvals. ssh is a transport — the effect is whatever runs remotely — so classify by the remote command.

## Change

- New `classifySshStage`: strips ssh options + `[user@]host`, then classifies the **remote command** with the same effect rules.
- Interactive ssh (no command) and port/dynamic forwarding (`-L`/`-R`/`-D`/`-W`) aren't inspectable → `review` floor.
- `scp`/`rsync` to a remote stay `high_stakes` (file transfer = outward write).
- Removed the blanket `ssh` pattern from the full-command high-stakes scan.

## Result

| Command | Tier |
|---|---|
| `ssh host 'ls /'`, remote diagnostics | `safe` |
| `ssh host 'cp a b'` | `warning` |
| `ssh host 'rm -rf /data'`, remote `DROP TABLE`, `sudo …` | `high_stakes` / `review` |
| `ssh host` (interactive), `ssh -L …` | `review` |
| `scp f host:/p`, `rsync --delete … host:/b` | `high_stakes` |

SDK suite **289 pass**, `tsc` clean.

author: kaluang
body:
Whether a delivery is piped is currently decided solely by whether the stored smtp field begins with "|"; the routers never check on_piped or the domain's pipe flag. on_avscan and on_spamassassin are already re-checked against the domain in the routers, so pipe is the odd one out.

Add a virtual_piped router that only pipes when the user is on_piped and the domain has pipe enabled, and set forbid_pipe on virtual_domains so a stray "|command" smtp value can't be executed there. Piped users keep working; for everyone else a pipe can no longer be reached.

The catchall and group routers also set a pipe transport, but their data comes from a validated forward address / the group member list rather than the raw smtp field, so they are left unchanged.

I haven't been able to test this against a live Exim setup, so please sanity-check the new router before relying on it.

author: youtube-at-vach
body:
💡 **What:** 
Optimized `track_jitter` and `track_jitter_fractional` in `src/core/transmission_logic.py` to eliminate repeated array allocations using `np.concatenate`. It now pre-extracts a contiguous `search_window` of length `2*max_search + N` outside the `for` loop, handling any boundary wrap-around exactly once. Inside the loop, it creates zero-copy slices from this pre-allocated window.

🎯 **Why:** 
The original implementation repeatedly sliced and called `np.concatenate` to handle ring-buffer wrap-arounds on every iteration of the `for delta in range(-max_search, max_search + 1)` loop. Memory allocations inside hot paths (especially for audio DSP logic evaluated block-by-block) cause measurable CPU overhead and GC churn. 

📊 **Measured Improvement:** 
Using Python `timeit` for `1000` iterations at an offset where wrap-around happens heavily (`last_offset = 47990` in a `48000` sample buffer, `N=1024`, `max_search=8`):
*   **Original:** `~0.435s`
*   **Optimized:** `~0.370s`
*   **Improvement:** `~15%` faster computation time near the boundaries with zero regressions in alignment accuracy or behavior. Tests pass seamlessly.

body:
## What

The admin character editor now has a separate **"User-generated chat images"** block showing the photos users generated with that character in chat.

## Why

The existing "Media gallery" only lists admin-managed media (`media-assets.ownerCharacterId`). Chat images are owned by the *user* and linked to the character only through `message → conversation → characterId`, so they were invisible in admin.

## How

- **`GET /api/admin/characters/[id]/chat-images`** (new, admin-role gated) — resolves conversations for the character (all users) → completed `image` messages → `media-assets` (soft-delete filtered), newest first, tagging each item with the user id that generated it.
- **`ChatGeneratedImages`** admin component — read-only thumbnail grid under the media gallery (click → opens full size, shows dimensions, date, and a `user #id` badge). Registered as a `ui` field on the Characters collection + in the admin `importMap`.

Read-only by design (just display, per request). Moderation actions (e.g. soft-delete) can be added later if needed.

## Verification

`tsc` clean · `next lint` clean · full vitest **186/186**. (`payload generate:importmap` has an env-loader bug in this repo, so the import map entry was added by hand — the key→binding mapping is what Payload resolves.)

author: assh-odoo
body:
Currently, an error occurs when a user insert a dynamic product snippet onto website.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

 - Install `website_sale` without demo data.
 - Go to `Website` > `eCommerce` > `Products` > `Ribbons`.
 - Open any ribbon and set `Assign` to `When New`.
 - Go to the `Website` > `Edit` > drag and drop the `Catalog` block, and select a `Dynamic Product` 
   block (`Generic Product Template (customizable)` [ref](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ZYeQA8DhfYAf_jbPwL-tZXaVi1YAyFbd/view?usp=drive_link)).

`TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'datetime.datetime' and 'bool'`

After this [recent commit], when a user drops a dynamic product snippet, the system attempts 
to set the ribbon value [1]. If no product records are available, it falls back to using sample products [2]. 
These sample products are virtual records created with model.new() [3] [4] and are not stored in 
the database, so they do not have a publish date.
When auto-assigned ribbon with the When New option assign, the system compares the ribbon's 
new period with the product's publish date. Since the sample products do not have a publish 
date, this comparison raises an error [5].

This commit ensures that the comparison between new period and publish date is only 
performed when the product has a valid publish date.

body:
## Why

Follow-up to #16651. While auditing `apps/web` references during the API-routing doc cleanup, I found a **second** set of stale paths from a different migration: database schema, migrations, and Zero token capability gating moved out of `apps/web` into the `@vm0/db` package (`packages/db`) and `apps/api`. Several skill and deployment docs still pointed at the old `apps/web` locations.

Verified current locations:
- schema: `apps/web/src/db/schema/` → **`packages/db/src/schema/`** (`apps/web/src/db` no longer exists)
- schema barrel: `src/db/db.ts` → **`packages/db/src/index.ts`**
- data-migration scripts: `apps/web/scripts/migrations/` → **`packages/db/scripts/migrations/`**

- `apps/web` no longer exposes a `globalThis.services` singleton

## Changes

- **`database-development` skill**: run db commands from `packages/db`; schema lives in `src/schema/` and is exported via `src/index.ts`; data-migration scripts live in `packages/db/scripts/migrations/`.
- **`feature-switch` skill**: point token capability gating at `apps/api/src/signals/auth/tokens.ts` (2 refs).

author: crisptrutski
body:
Stacked on #75385; tuning follows in #75396.

A structural refactor of the search-ranking machinery. **No weight *values* change here** — only the structure and which contexts share a profile (the actual numbers are tuned in #75396).

- Split `static-weights` into `static-default-weights` (the inherited base) and `static-context-weights` (pure per-context overrides). `:default` is no longer a key alongside real contexts.
- `context->normalized-context` collapses surfaces that should rank/filter alike onto a shared profile. The broad-search surfaces — search app, command palette, type-filter — share `:global`; the **nav search bar is intentionally left off** for now (TODO to decide what to DRY up).
- `normalized-context` is applied once at the top of the search call tree (the `search-context` constructor) **and** at the `/api/search/weights` endpoints, so introspection and stored overrides agree with what search applies.
- Derive `normalized-contexts` + the `NormalizedContext` enum from the map; add `known-rankers` (the union of scorer keys across all profiles) for `/weights` override validation.

**Behaviour change vs. today**: the broad-search surfaces now share one ranking/filter profile (search-app picks up the command-palette profile). Weight values are unchanged.

🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability:** The authentication check `document.cookie.includes('bt_auth=true')` evaluates to true for ANY cookie name containing that string (e.g., `fake_bt_auth=true`).
🎯 **Impact:** An attacker could bypass the client-side authentication gate simply by crafting and injecting a dummy cookie via the browser console or through other injection vectors on subdomains.
🔧 **Fix:** Changed the loose substring check to a strict Regular Expression check `/(^|;\s*)bt_auth=true(;\s*|$)/.test(document.cookie)` to ensure exact key-value match.
✅ **Verification:** Verified that the patch works by successfully building the app via `pnpm run build` and checking the modified `src/App.tsx` logic.

author: yuechen-li-dev
body:
### Motivation
- Expose a controlled source surface for compile-time evaluation so callers can write `comptime expr` and have supported expressions evaluated and erased before MIR/backend.
- Leverage the existing P9-M1 typed-HIR `CompileTimeEvaluator` for a hermetic, deterministic subset (ints and bools) without adding host capabilities or function-call evaluation yet.
- Provide stable diagnostics and test fixtures so the new surface is well-specified and regressions are catchable.

### Description
- Add `comptime` as a reserved token and lexer test coverage so nearby identifiers (e.g., `comptimeValue`) remain identifiers and `comptime` tokenizes as a keyword. (`src/compiler/token.zig`, `src/compiler/lexer.zig`)
- Parse `comptime expr` as a prefix AST node `CompileTimeExpr` and include AST debug/deinit support. (`src/compiler/parser.zig`, `src/compiler/ast.zig`)
- Lower AST `compile_time` nodes to a HIR `compile_time` kind, preserve the operand, and wire the HIR so the checker can evaluate it later. (`src/compiler/semantics.zig`, `src/compiler/hir.zig`)
- Integrate the existing `CompileTimeEvaluator` into the HIR checker so operands are type-checked, evaluated (int/bool only), and stored in a semantic side table `SemanticModule.compile_time_values` keyed by HIR `ExprId`, with stable diagnostics on unsupported forms, type mismatches, division-by-zero, and overflow (diagnostic codes `CON0120`–`CON0124`). (`src/compiler/hir_checker.zig`, `src/compiler/diagnostics.zig`, `src/compiler/compile_time.zig`)
- Lower evaluated compile-time values in MIR lowering to ordinary int/bool literals and add tests ensuring no `CompileTime` artifacts remain in MIR debug output. (`src/compiler/mir_lowering.zig`)
- Add unit/parser/lexer/HIR/MIR tests and language fixtures for P9 compile-time valid and invalid cases and register them in the test harness. (`src/compiler/lexer.zig`, `src/compiler/parser.zig`, `src/compiler/hir_checker.zig`, `src/compiler/mir_lowering.zig`, `src/compiler/testing/conception.zig`, `language/phase9-compile-time/*`)
- Document P9‑M2 behavior and scope in `docs/design/phase-9-compile-time-execution.md` and note out-of-scope items (no compile-time functions, no static_assert, no host capabilities, no reflection, etc.). (`docs/design/phase-9-compile-time-execution.md`)

### Testing
- Ran `zig version` which reported `0.16.0` and confirmed the toolchain used. (success)
- Ran the full test suite via `zig build test`, which executed the added lexer/parser/hir/mir unit tests and the updated fixture suite, and the run completed successfully. (success)
- Ran `git diff --check` to ensure no whitespace or diff errors. (success)

author: galke7
body:
## What

The **"אזל המלאי"** badge rendered *behind* the product image on sold-out cards (visible only dimly through the 70%-opaque image). This adds a `z-index` to `.product-badge` so it always paints on top.

## Root cause

A sold-out card's image gets `opacity: 0.7` + `filter: grayscale(0.6)` — **each forms a stacking context** on the image. The badge (`position: absolute`, `z-index: auto`) sits *before* the image in the DOM, so under CSS painting order both land in the same paint step and the later element (the image) paints over the badge. In-stock sale badges were unaffected because their images have no opacity/filter (plain in-flow, painted earlier).

Fix: explicit `z-index: 2` on `.product-badge` → it paints in the positive-z-index step, above the image's stacking context. One-line, scoped to the badge; helps the sale badge too.

## Verification
- `npm test` → **45/45** (CSS-only change, no logic touched).
- Browser: `elementFromPoint` at the badge's center returns the badge element itself (nothing covering it); badge renders as a solid grey label on top of the greyed image.

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a focused laboratory that teaches Docker user-defined bridge networks, built-in DNS service discovery, published ports vs container ports, aliases and network isolation using a small real workload (API, diagnostic client, proxy).
- Deliver a compact step-by-step lab that exercises inspection and automated verification of real Docker state (networks, containers, ports, health, aliases) and produces machine-checkable evidence files.

### Description

- Added new assignment under `lab/docker/networking` with `assignment.yaml`, `main.qmd` and an `_assignment-description.qmd` overview; the lab contains nine sequenced steps from inventory to cleanup.
- For each step created `step.yaml`, student-facing `*_theory.qmd` and `*_task.qmd`, plus root action scripts `prepare`, `pre-step`, `check`, `solution` and `post-step` that use absolute paths and run as expected by the course runner.
- Included real workload assets under `assets/`: `net-api` (JSON HTTP API), `net-client` (diagnostic HTTP client) and `net-proxy` (reverse proxy), each with a small Python service and `Dockerfile` for reproducible testing inside the lab environment.
- Integrated the lab into course manifests and Quarto book configuration so it appears in both student and full profiles (`lab/_course.yaml`, `_quarto-student.yml`, `_quarto-full.yml`).

### Testing

- Static/automated checks run: YAML parsing of modified files with Ruby (`YAML.load_file`) succeeded.  `ruby -e 'require "yaml"; ...'` — OK.
- Shell scripts syntax check with `bash -n` over all `prepare`, `pre-step`, `check`, `solution`, `post-step` files — OK.

author: ndrew1337
body:
## Problem
`/api/chat/history` built one combined list of chat + progress messages and returned a single `combined[-limit:]` tail. A burst of progress/telemetry (high-frequency subagent/skill lifecycle, swarm fan-out) therefore **evicted the user's real messages** from the recency window — the "messages disappear from the chat" symptom.

## Fix (backend-only, ~24 lines)
The human conversation (`chat.jsonl`) and progress telemetry (`progress.jsonl`) are now tailed with **separate quotas**, then merged and sorted:
- `n_human` — default **750**, cap 1500
- `n_progress` — default **300**, cap 600
- both overridable via query params; `limit` still accepted for backward-compat.

A progress flood can no longer push human messages out of the response. **All subagent-lineage progress** (`delegation_role` / `subagent_event`) is kept regardless of the progress quota, so the client can still reconstruct child-card lineage on reload (the `fix/subagent-reliability` pre-pass depends on this).

Response shape is unchanged → **no frontend change**.

## Deliberately deferred: scroll-up pagination
Cursor pagination (load only the latest page, fetch older on scroll) conflicts with three in-memory frontend mechanisms that assume the **full** history is present: the subagent lineage pre-pass, the `seenMessageKeys` dedupe set, and the ordered `insertMessageNode`. A multi-agent design pass flagged this; doing it safely (additive older-page loads, DOM-based dedupe, render old cards terminal from `task_terminal_status`) is a larger follow-up and is tracked separately. Neither quotas nor pagination address the unbounded `progress.jsonl` read cost (separate issue).

## Tests
Adds `tests/test_chat_history_quotas.py`: a 50-message progress flood does not evict the human conversation; all subagent lifecycle events survive a tiny progress quota; defaults keep recent history. Existing `test_gateway_history` / `test_bugfixes_airi` / `test_restart_reconnect` stay green.

author: movingavgjoe
body:
## Summary

Adds `valuation_metrics`, a small, dependency-light Python package that computes
valuation ratios for any US ticker on a given date using **only free data
sources** (no API keys, no paid tiers). Also adds the first analysis built on top
of it: a study of the June 3–5, 2026 mega-cap tech sell-off.

The goal is a reproducible, point-in-time-aware way to ask "how expensive was this
stock on this day?" without a Bloomberg terminal.

## What's included

**`valuation_metrics/` — the reusable engine**
- Computes: trailing P/E, forward P/E, PEG, price/FCF, EV/EBITDA (forward),
  revenue growth vs. valuation multiple, and FCF margin.
- **Prices** from Yahoo Finance (`yfinance`).
- **Fundamentals** from the SEC EDGAR `companyfacts` API — point-in-time (only
  filings dated on/before the requested date, to avoid look-ahead bias),
  self-throttled to 8 req/s (SEC's ceiling is 10).
- **Forward estimates** from `yfinance` (current analyst consensus).
- CSV caching keyed by ticker + date, so re-runs are fast and stay well within
  rate limits.
- `get_metrics(ticker, date)` entry point plus a CLI.

**`adhoc_analysis/2026-06-05_selloff/` — first study**
- Compares two-day price moves vs. the P/E each name carried going into the week,
  across nine mega-caps; generates a chart for write-up.

## Design notes & caveats

- **Forward estimates are current consensus.** `yfinance` returns today's
  consensus regardless of the historical date requested — accurate for current
  analysis, a present-day proxy for past dates.
- **EBITDA is approximated** (it isn't a reported line item): operating income +
  D&A, falling back to net income + interest + taxes + D&A.

## Testing

- 12 unit tests covering the pure ratio math (`pytest`), no network required.

## Notes

- Requires **Python 3.11+**.
- No secrets committed: the SEC EDGAR contact email is read from the
  `EDGAR_USER_AGENT` environment variable and is never hardcoded.
- Generated outputs (cache CSVs, chart PNGs) are git-ignored.

## Summary
Fixes the P0 "CTA clips off-screen" Dynamic Type class (#271) on the **capture**, **onboarding**, **auth**, and **export** surfaces. Non-scrolling centered cards and segmented pickers dropped their primary buttons — and truncated labels — at large/accessibility text sizes. Several of these gates are compliance- or flow-blocking (consent, MFA enrolment, onboarding, export), so an unreachable CTA traps the clinician.

> **Stacked on #358** (`lane-ios/dynamic-type-session-start-271`). Opened against `main` per the lane convention — merge #358 first; this PR's diff includes #358's commit until then.

## What changed
**Capture (`Capture/`)**
- **CaptureView consentOverlay (HIGH):** card now scrolls (GeometryReader + min-height centering) so **Confirm consent** is always reachable — recording is hard-blocked behind consent. Extracted to `consentCard`.
- **CaptureView consent-method picker (HIGH):** `.segmented` → `.menu` at accessibility sizes (segmented can't wrap/scale; "Paper Form"/"Digital Form" truncated, worse in FR).
- collaborationPill (MED): drop `lineLimit(1)`, wrap + `fixedSize(vertical)`.
- liveCaptionsUnavailableChip (MED): `lineLimit(2)` + `fixedSize(vertical)`.
- specialtyBadge (LOW): `.system(12)` → `.aurionFont(12, relativeTo: .caption)` to match sibling chips; icon stays a fixed glyph, tail truncation + 132pt cap keep the HUD bar intact.
- DeviceHubView activeSummary (MED): `ViewThatFits` two-up → stacked + `minimumScaleFactor(0.7)`.
- DeviceHubView permissionsGrid (MED): single column + label wrap at accessibility sizes.
- DeviceHubView SourceRow detail (LOW): `minimumScaleFactor(0.8)` + `fixedSize`.
- LivePreviewOverlay header (MED): `ViewThatFits` reflows version/time meta to a 2nd line.
- LivePreviewOverlay draftBadge (LOW): `.system(9)` → `.aurionFont(9, relativeTo: .caption2)`.
- FrameGalleryView frame-count (LOW): moves out of the toolbar into a content header at accessibility sizes.

**Onboarding / Auth / Export**
- **MfaSetupView (HIGH):** card in a centered ScrollView (200pt QR + **Complete setup**) — blocks MFA enrolment.
- MfaChallengeView (MED): card in a centered ScrollView; extracted to `challengeCard`.
- **WearableSetupView (HIGH):** ScrollView + `.safeAreaInset(.bottom)` footer (Scan/Skip, or Continue once paired) — blocks onboarding. Device name `lineLimit(2)` + `minimumScaleFactor(0.7)`.
- **ExportView (HIGH):** pinned format selector + scrollable state content + `.safeAreaInset(.bottom)` footer for **Export**/**Share**. File-info card `ViewThatFits` (3-up → stacked) with a `@ScaledMetric` divider height (MED). Format pills clamped to one line + `minimumScaleFactor` — fixed short tokens, no vertical fallback (LOW).

`#271` — large/accessibility Dynamic Type made primary CTAs unreachable on these surfaces. Compliance: consent + MFA gates must stay actionable at any text size.

- `xcodebuild build -scheme Aurion -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.
- Spot-checked at AX5 in previews: consent overlay, MFA setup, and export all keep their CTA reachable (scroll / pinned footer).
- Normal text sizes unchanged (`.aurionFont` is a no-op at default; ScrollView/footer collapse via `scrollBounceBehavior(.basedOnSize)`).

## Security checklist
- [x] No PHI in logs/errors/responses (UI-only changes).
- [x] No secrets, no provider keys, no network/audit behavior changed.
- [x] Consent hard-block preserved — the gate is now more reachable, not bypassable.

## Out of scope
- Lens/zoom toggle area (owned by another lane — CaptureManager/lens untouched).
- VoiceProcessingView (already carries the ScrollView/footer fix from #268/#271).

## Summary

- **ADR 0012 — SSE session tokens (#99)** — replaces admin secret in URL query parameters with short-lived HMAC-SHA256 tokens obtained via `POST /api/auth/session`. Cookie-based delivery, 10-minute TTL, signing key in registry, admin secret explicitly rejected as SSE token.

author: thll
body:
Previously, Collectors were not usable in Graylog Cloud, because it requires the Collector Ingest Input to run and be managed by Administrators.

This PR adds a background service that starts an ephemeral Ingest input once the Collectors settings page has been saved for the first time, which at the moment serves as the bootstrapping trigger for Collectors both on premise as in the Cloud.

The implementation aims at re-using most of the on-premise code, e.g. the actual input is launched by the service but not registered in the usual way, so that it is not visible. For that to work reliably, an artificial input ID had to be added. We also use this ID to render the "received by" indicator in the Messages UI to link to the collectors page.

author: robsv
body:
Summary
-------
Refactors the DIS web UI in api/ off hand-built HTML strings and duplicated
front-end code. Introduces a small HTML-rendering toolkit in dis_responder.py
and migrates every multi-row data table (~59 view functions, 70 render_table
call sites) to it, with HTML-escaping by default. Also consolidates shared
JavaScript, variabilizes/dedupes the CSS, and fixes several latent bugs found
along the way.

No intended behavior change for end users beyond bug fixes and more consistent
styling/sorting; output was verified per-endpoint against the live app.

Files changed (14)
------------------
  api/dis_responder.py            - HTML helpers + table migration (bulk of diff)
  api/static/css/main.css         - :root variables, collapsed table classes, tfoot styling
  api/static/js/dis.js            - NEW: shared JS helpers (loaded once)
  api/templates/base.html         - load dis.js; minor cleanup
  api/templates/bokeh.html        - drop duplicated inline JS
  api/templates/custom.html       - drop duplicated inline JS
  api/templates/doi.html          - drop duplicated inline JS
  api/templates/general.html      - drop duplicated inline JS
  api/templates/home.html         - drop no-op btn-md
  api/templates/coauth.html       - drop no-op btn-md
  api/templates/people.html       - drop no-op btn-md
  api/templates/ror.html          - drop no-op btn-md
  api/templates/subject.html      - drop no-op btn-md
  api/templates/subscription.html - drop no-op btn-md

Server-side HTML toolkit (new, in dis_responder.py)
---------------------------------------------------
  render_table(headers, rows, table_id=, css=, row_classes=, footer=, width=)
      Builds a <table> from a header list + list-of-cell-lists. Cells are
      HTML-escaped by default; wrap pre-rendered HTML in safe().
  safe(value) / Safe       - mark a value as trusted HTML (not escaped)
  fcell(value, colspan=, align=, header=)  - a <tfoot> cell
  cell(value, sort=, align=, style=)       - a body <td> with data-sort
                                             (numeric sort), alignment, or style

Table migration (#8)
--------------------
  - ~59 view functions migrated off hand-built table-string HTML, including the
    shared standard_doi_table() builder (16 callers) and all <tfoot> total
    tables, dynamic-column tables (dois_time, the subscription matrices, apcs,
    show_subscriptionlist, top_entities heatmap), and multi-table views
    (acknowledgement_stats, preprint_with_pub, doi_relationships, datacite_dois).
  - HTML-escaping by default closes a stored-XSS surface (DB-derived titles,

author: youssefalw2001
body:
This pull request was created by @kiro-agent on behalf of @youssefalw2001 :ghost:

Comment with **/kiro fix** to address specific feedback or **/kiro all** to address everything.
<sub>[Learn about Kiro Web](https://kiro.dev/web/)</sub>

---
## What was making the Arena chippy

Every Predator and King wallet card had **continuous `box-shadow` animations** running 60× per second. `box-shadow` forces a full **repaint** of the card on every single frame. With 16 cards on screen, the browser was doing 16 repaints/frame at 60fps = constant paint storm. That's the chippiness.

## The fix: static box-shadow + opacity animation

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `@keyframes predatorGlow` animated `box-shadow` values | `::after` pseudo-element with **static** `box-shadow`, only `opacity` animates |
| `@keyframes kingPulse` animated `box-shadow` | Same pattern — static glow, `opacity` pulses |
| `sparkPulse` animated `transform: scale` | Now `opacity` only |
| `auraPulse` animated `box-shadow` | `opacity` only |
| `btnPulse` animated `box-shadow` | `opacity` fade |
| `scanPulse` animated `box-shadow` expand | `outline-color` animation |

**The rule:** `opacity` and `transform` run on the GPU compositor thread — free. `box-shadow`, `filter`, `background` force a CPU paint pass — expensive.

## Also fixed

- **Framer Motion stagger on wallet grid** → replaced with pure CSS `animation-delay` on `.arena-grid-item:nth-child(n)`. Same visual result, zero JS overhead during gameplay.
- **`filter: blur` entrances in YoinkResult** → removed (blur forces paint on every frame of the animation).
- **`will-change: transform`** added to the arena grid container (promotes it to its own compositor layer).

## Testing
- `npm run build` ✅ passes
- `npm run lint` — 4 pre-existing errors only, 0 new

author: tsavo
body:
## Tokio await implication edge: `post(before .await) ⊨ pre(after resume)`

The first real *reasoning* across an async effect — the implication lifter relocated to the awaited seam. A Rust `.await` is lifted as a structural `await(term)`; WP discovery recurses through await; the verifier's `locate_producer_post` peels `await(producer())` so the awaited producer's **postcondition** reaches the consumer's **precondition** across the suspension.

**Strictly `post ⊨ pre` at the seam.** No type/borrow/drop reasoning (that's rustc), no interleaving/deadlock/lock reasoning (that's a model-checker). The `.await` is only *where* post meets pre.

- `sugar-walk`: `await_lifts_as_structural_seam`; `awaited_let_binding_reaches_later_consumer_pre_as_structural_seam`.
- `sugar-verifier`: `locate_producer_post_resolves_through_single_await_seam` **and** `locate_producer_post_refuses_non_producer_await_base` (the refusal guard).
- RED-first: each went red on await-term loss / missing producer-post-through-await / seam loss.

### Two-twin showcase `examples/tokio-await-implication-edge` (real tokio `=1.43.0`, `#[tokio::test]` witness, battleaxe)
GOOD — producer post establishes consumer pre across `.await` → `await_edge=discharged witness=discharged`. BAD — producer post does **not** entail consumer pre → `await_edge=unsatisfied witness=unsatisfied`. Consistency receipt scoped loudly to the awaited edge row (`bridge=consumer`).

### Acceptance (verified by me, real exit captured)
- `../../bin/bcargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` → **2541 passed / 0 failed**; await + refusal tests ran.
- `run.sh` exit 0 — I re-ran it: SCOPE banner, good discharged, bad flips to unsatisfied, self-check passed.
- `make ci` PASS; `grep -rn 'concept_name\|conceptName' implementations/` → 0.

First real cross-effect edge; channel `post(send) ⊨ pre(recv)` and the mutex critical-section edge build on the same machinery.

body:
关联 #154。完整排查证据链贴在 [issue 评论](https://github.com/Memento-Teams/Memento-Research/issues/154#issuecomment-4649903571)。

## 一句话原因

`hire_from_cv` 判断"talent 是否需要 repo"时**只看 tools 不看 skills**，导致 `tools: []` 但 `skills: [...]` 的 talent（如 `result-analyst`）在远端瞬时故障时被静默降级成 placeholder CV-only hire，加上 `_bootstrap_hire_list_employees` 的 idempotent skip，**一次失败定终身**。

## 修法

`api/routes.py:5123`：

```diff
-    if cv.get("tools"):
+    if cv.get("tools") or cv.get("skills"):
         await _publish_cv_error(...)
         return False
```

声明了 tools **或** skills 的 talent 都不允许 silent fallback —— 两者的实体（`tool.py` / `SKILL.md`）都在 repo 里，CV 只列名字。真正的 pure-prompt talent（两者都空）保持原有的优雅降级行为。

## 引入点

commit `7f1f377` (`fix(hire): degrade to CV-only hire when Talent Market is unreachable for tool-less talents`)。原作者本意是修另一个真实问题——Talent Market 偶尔抽风时整个 AutoResearch roster 起不来——但判断模型错了：以为"`tools: []` ⇒ 所有内容在 CV 里"，忽略了 skill 实体在 repo 的 `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`。

## 不在本 PR 范围

- **idempotent skip 不重试**（已经被 placeholder 化的存量员工不会自动修复）：另一个独立的 hire-flow 改造，分开 PR。
- **`_bootstrap_hire_list_employees` 的 startup-time validation**（对比员工实际 skills/ 目录 vs CV 声明，对不上的触发 re-hire）：同上。

## 测试计划

- [x] `uv run pytest tests/unit/api/test_cv_hire_offline_fallback.py` —— 3 passed
  - `test_pure_prompt_talent_hires_when_market_down`：tools=0 AND skills=0 → 优雅降级
  - `test_tooled_talent_still_fails_when_market_down`：tools 非空 → 报错
  - **新增** `test_skilled_talent_fails_when_market_down`：tools=0 但 skills 非空 → 报错（这就是 #154 的回归用例，`result-analyst` 的形态）
- [ ] 真实环境：unhire `result-analyst` + 重新 hire，验证 `employees/00012/skills/result-analysis-runbook/SKILL.md` 出现。

版本号 bump 到 0.8.73（避开 PR #153 的 0.8.72）。

Phase 24C — focused follow-ups to Phase 24B (PR #84). Two of three deferred items completed; third deferred to Phase 24C-2 per mission's explicit defer clause.

2. **Fixed:** GovCon NAICS filter dropdown converted to profile-driven render.

## Root cause of the carry-over failure

Wall-clock vs injectable-clock mismatch in `services/govcon/email-compliance.js#activeSolicitation()`. The function used `Date.now()` to compare against an opportunity's `responseDeadline`. The MOCK-A test fixture sets `responseDeadline` at `agent.nowFn() + 5d` where `nowFn` is frozen at `2026-06-01`, but the test process runs at real wall clock (`2026-06-08+`), so `due > Date.now()` evaluated false → `activeSolicitation()` returned false → the agent drafted a direct outreach instead of the expected Q&A-only blocked draft.

**Fix (production behavior under real wall clock unchanged):**
- `activeSolicitation(opp, nowMs)` accepts an optional clock; defaults to `Date.now()`.
- `draftOfficialEmail(input)` accepts and forwards `input.nowMs`.
- `buildDraft()` threads the agent's `now()` into `draftOfficialEmail`.

Closes the Epic-3 board-load Story (3.8) test deliverable. Adds `tests/e2e/board-load.spec.ts` — a UI-driving Playwright spec (grep handle `board-load`) that proves the Jira-faithful corrected load model (`notes.html` mistake #33) end-to-end through the real Next + Postgres stack:

1. **No "Load more"** — the flat board renders the whole bounded set; no button, footer, or scroll sentinel.
2. **Virtualized / DOM-bounded** — a 200-card column mounts only a window of cards (`useRowWindow` kept), not all 200; the count badge still shows the full total.
3. **Done-age window** — the Done column loads only the recent (~14d) set; an old (back-dated) done card is not in the DOM, while the header count still surfaces the full denominator.

### Decision: over-cap banner is covered at the unit/component tier, not re-rendered in the browser
Triggering the over-cap "refine the filter" banner end-to-end needs a board **past `BOARD_ISSUE_CAP` (5,000)**, and the projection then loads the full cap — rendering 5,000 cards through the **dev** server cannot complete within a sane E2E budget (measured: `/api/board` for a normal board ≈30 ms; the 5,000-card load never returns in 180 s). That is the "combined at-scale journey" the card explicitly assigns to **Story 3.5**, not a robust per-PR check. The banner's correctness is already proven, end-to-enough, at two cheaper non-flaky tiers:
- **predicate** — `tests/boards/projection.test.ts` (`truncated` true at `cap+1` / false under, full count surfaced) against real Postgres;
- **banner render** — `tests/components/board-completeness.test.tsx` (renders iff `truncated`, names the cap, above both flat + swimlane, disabled Epic-6 filter seam).

A process-wide cap-override env would have skewed the other tests (it caps every board), so it was rejected. The spec documents this in a footer NOTE.

### AC status
- ✅ `pnpm test` covers the bounded projection + `truncated`/`cap` + Done-age window, the banner predicate, the no-load-more assertions (flat + swimlane), and DOM-bounded virtualization (existing `projection.test.ts` / `board-completeness.test.tsx` / `board-column.test.tsx` / `board-swimlanes-render.test.tsx`).
- ✅ `pnpm test:e2e --grep board-load` green over the real stack (3/3 locally, isolated DB).
- ✅ Reuses `tests/helpers/db.ts` truncation + the seeded project; the at-scale combined journey stays in Story 3.5.
- ✅ AC #4: no stale per-column "Load more"/cursor assertions remain to supersede (3.8.3/3.8.5 removed the affordance; `board-column.test.tsx` asserts its absence). 3.2.7 / 3.3.7 drag/reducer/grouping/reassign/WIP coverage untouched.

### Checks
`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm exec eslint`, `pnpm exec prettier --check` all clean.

author: dukefromearth
body:
Adds **codex-duo** — stress-test an idea with two persistent Codex agents.

## What it is
Agent A holds and defends an idea; agent B challenges it with no priors (Socratic by default). Over N turns the claim is driven into its strongest bounded, falsifiable form, or shown to fail. The value is the asymmetry — scrutiny from a mind that didn't author the belief.

## Packaging
- Pip-installable CLI: `pyproject.toml` console entry point `codex-duo`; package data via `importlib.resources`. Install anywhere with `uv tool install .` (or `pipx install .`).
- `--smoke` — low-model, short-loop sanity run.
- `--doctor` — checks prerequisites (codex CLI, auth) and installs/fixes them. The tool preflights on every run and points here on failure.
- Streamed JSONL run log (one record per line, flushed per turn) — a killed run keeps every completed turn.

## Layout / CI
Simple unregistered skill (like `go-architecture-diagrams`): not in the `packages/skills-build` registry, so `validate:all` / `build:all` ignore it and the in-sync check stays green. `SKILL.md` is usage; `README.md` is install/troubleshooting.

author: clemenselflein
body:
This PR targets two points: Charger termination issues and inconsistencies between hardware boards.

## Charger Termination Issue
On some platforms (universal with 5S battery), we have the issue that the charging termination current is higher than the drain current for the CM4 hardware. This leads to the fact that charging never terminates and after the safety timer uns out, the charger just errors.

The termination current is the **lower setting** of both, the hardware resistor and the software setting. For universal with 1A jumper, this leads to 100mA fixed termination current which is too low (CM4 needs ~250mA).

This PR fixes this issue by disabling the hardware resistor while the software has control. This way we can set higher termination current and let the charger terminate properly.

## Inconsistencies in PCB designs
We have some consistency issues with the charger on different hardware boards and this also leads to charger issues on some boards.

### Mode 1:
The issue is that on some boards, the hardware limit is the "standalone charging current" i.e. the current which is used by the board, if no firmware is running (e.g. Sabo, new Universal Charger).

### Mode 2:
On some boards, the resistor was used to limit the software setting instead (so the board did NOT charge stand-alone at all and only charges when the firmware is active). This is the YardForce board and current universal boards.

In this PR, we decide to switch to **Mode 1** completely. This means, that we allow boards to charge without firmware with a very conservative setting which helps boards to come up when battery is in low-voltage mode.

It does not allow existing non-firmware charging boards to suddenly start standalone, the behavior will not be changed.

author: gavinadams80-ui
body:
## Why
The keystone of the Engineering→Drafting→Engineering flow: a shared, versioned **DesignSet** payload. Engineering computes a design and emits it; Drafting ingests it to generate drawings (with the existing shared generators), the user amends freely, then hands it back for Engineering to re-run the calcs, re-check, value, and produce the calc PDF.

## What (MINOR — purely additive)
New `src/designSet.ts`:
- **Types:** `DesignSet`, `DesignSetInput`, `DesignMember`, `MemberCheck`, `DesignGeometry`, `DesignResults`, `DesignLoads`, `DesignSchedule`, `ScheduleLine`, `DesignStatus`.
- **Functions:** `makeDesignSet` (stamps format/schema/units/generated + derives status), `serializeDesignSet` (→ pretty `.designset.json`), `parseDesignSet` / `validateDesignSet` (throw `DesignSetParseError`; reject a schema newer than the lib), `computeDesignStatus`.
- `project` reuses the shared `TitleBlockData`; each member has a stable `id` matching Drafting's `data-member-id` so edits survive the round-trip.

## Design notes
- Mirrors Engineering's real in-memory state (`config` → `geometry`, `calc.sel*` → `members`, `materialSchedule` → `schedule`), so the producer side is a thin mapping.
- `loads` travels so the **handback can be re-calculated**; `check`/`status` carry the green/fail state.

## Verification
`npm run build` passes. Node round-trip test confirms: lossless serialize→parse, status derivation (`all-pass`/`has-fail`/`unchecked`), and rejection of bad format / non-JSON / newer schema.

After merge: tag `v0.6.0`, then re-pin Drafting and wire its DesignSet import.

### Motivation
- Update deprecated PySide6/PyQt API usages (primarily `exec_()` and `QLocale` enums) to current calls and fix font sizing to avoid runtime warnings and breakage.  
- Improve stability of the tree model by adding defensive checks and exception handling to avoid crashes when Qt queries model state during async updates.  

### Description
- Replaced numerous `exec_()`/`QEventLoop.exec_()`/`menu.exec_()` calls with `exec()` to align with modern Qt bindings.  
- Normalized `QLocale` constructor/enum usage (`QLocale.Territory` → `QLocale.Country` and related changes) and adjusted locale creation sites.  
- Hardened `TreeModel` methods (`rowCount`, `columnCount`, `index`, `parent`, `headerData`, `data`, `setData`, `flags`, `removeRows`, `insertRows`, `nodeFromIndex` and others) with input validation and `try/except` blocks to prevent exceptions escaping Qt model callbacks.  
- Adjusted font APIs to use `setPointSizeF` and ensured `setPixelSize` receives an integer to avoid type issues when fonts come as floats.  
- Minor dialog/menu and widget compatibility fixes across many plugins (project, admin, work_data, synonym_dictionary, eizm_dictionary, help dialog, plot context menus, etc.) to use the updated APIs.

author: luke-bradford
body:
Docs-only. Refs #1534.

Extracts the engineering lesson Codex caught at #1534 checkpoint-2 into `docs/review-prevention-log.md`. It shipped in the #1534 PR body + the `sources.py` docstring but not the prevention log — the project's skill-ownership rule (clause 3) wants reusable review lessons in the log, so this closes that gap.

## The lesson

#1527 established "verify write-target disjointness before extracting a job to its own lane." #1534 showed that's **necessary but not sufficient**: sharing a write target is fine *only if the writes are ordering-safe* (idempotent `ON CONFLICT`, monotonic `CASE`/`GREATEST` guard, or per-row advisory lock). A shared concurrency lane can be **load-bearing for correctness**, not just throughput — de-serializing it exposes any blind `COALESCE(EXCLUDED, existing)` last-writer-wins upsert. In #1534 that was `record_poll_outcome` regressing a `data_freshness_index` watermark once `sec_per_cik_poll` ran concurrently with the other `sec_rate` producers.

## Verification

Docs-only (+8 lines, one new `###` entry). Pre-push gate ran clean (no code touched). No perf claims.

## Summary
Promotes newt's **persona** from a prompt-only overlay into a **role profile** that also binds a toolset, capability (caveat) profile, and router policy — the seam the one-airframe-many-roles topology depends on. Fully **backward compatible**: a persona `.md` with no `+++` front-matter parses to an all-`None` profile and behaves exactly as today.

- **`newt-core`:** new `role_profile` module — `RoleProfile { prompt, role, tools, caveats, model, tier }`; `CaveatProfile` converts into the canonical `Caveats` (re-exported from agent-mesh-protocol).
- **`newt-tui`:** persona loading parses into a `RoleProfile`; `/persona show` reports role + tool allow-list + caveat summary + router policy; new `--keep-context` swaps profile without resetting the conversation (default still resets).
- **Shipped templates:** `personas/dragon-rider.md` (orchestrator — the new name for the retired "foreman"/"The Desk"), `personas/wing-commander.md` (arbiter), `personas/worker.md` (worker).
- **Naming:** orchestrator role is `dragon-rider` everywhere.

**Deliberately deferred (documented in `docs/design/role-profiles.md`):** *enforcement* — the TUI records but does not yet gate dispatch on tools/caveats (no agent-bridle registry at the TUI dispatch site); router application of `model`/`tier`; worker/MCP entry points minting authority from a profile.

Part of the drake-swarm migration foundation (Track 0: persona → role-profile seam).

## Test plan
- `cargo test --workspace` green (54 test binaries, 0 failures): role-profile parsing (front-matter present/absent/malformed), caveat→Caveats conversion, `/persona show` reporting, `--keep-context`, all three templates parse.

author: joacominatel
body:
Closes #257 (lands on the epic branch).

## Problem
With `REDIS_URL` unset/wrong (the prod incident — an existing `.env.prod` predating the var, so the api container fell back to `redis://localhost:6379` where no Valkey runs), the old `new IORedis(url, { maxRetriesPerRequest: null })`:
1. reconnected **forever** (no `retryStrategy` cap) → unstoppable `ECONNREFUSED` loop;
2. logged an error on **every** reconnect (no throttle) → log **flood**;
3. buffered `queue.add` in the offline queue and never errored → the import POST **hung** as a 202 that never resolved.

## Fix (apps/api/src/queue/redis-connection.ts — new)
- **Boot log, redacted.** The resolved `REDIS_URL` is logged at boot with any password `***`-redacted; the localhost fallback logs a loud WARN naming the misconfig. No secret is ever logged.
- **Bounded reconnection.** `retryStrategy` caps the backoff *and* the attempt count, then returns `null` (ioredis stops) — finite, not infinite. A single CRITICAL "giving up — degraded" fires once.
- **Throttled errors.** First `error` logged loudly, then ≤1 per 10 s window with a running count — the flood is impossible.
- **Producer fail-fast.** `enableOfflineQueue: false` makes `queue.add` reject immediately when the broker isn't ready; `maxRetriesPerRequest: null` is **kept** because BullMQ requires it on the worker's blocking connection (verified via Context7 — the two settings are orthogonal, so the worker is not broken).
- **503, not a hang.** `ArticleImportService.enqueue` catches a queue-down error (`isQueueUnavailableError`) and throws `ServiceUnavailableException` (clean 503, never the raw error — ADR-0031). A **stalled** job (worker died/OOM mid-parse — BullMQ's default stalled-job detection moves it to `failed`) maps to a friendly, retryable message.

## How it prevents BOTH failure modes
- **Flood:** bounded retryStrategy (finite attempts → terminal) + throttled error handler. At most ~1 first + a few throttled + 1 give-up line.
- **Hung import:** `enableOfflineQueue:false` → `queue.add` rejects at once → 503 on the POST. The job is never enqueued against a dead broker, so there's nothing to poll forever. And a job that *did* go active then died becomes terminal `failed` via stall detection.

## DevOps / contract
`REDIS_URL` documented as **required** in `apps/api/.env.example` and `infra/env/.env.prod.example` (with an **upgrade note**: existing `.env.prod` files predate it and must add it by hand — `start.sh` only writes it on a fresh render). Runbook notes added: upgrade step in `deploy-self-hosted.md` §4 and an ECONNREFUSED/import-hang troubleshooting entry in `docker-build-troubleshooting.md`. **`infra/env/.env.prod` (the gitignored real-secrets file) was NOT touched.**

## Verification
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` → clean.
- `node node_modules/.bin/jest` → **79 suites / 1080 tests pass**, including the **new** specs: `redis-connection.spec.ts` (redaction, retry cap + give-up, throttle, `enableOfflineQueue:false`/`maxRetriesPerRequest:null`, `isQueueUnavailableError`, boot logging/redaction) and `article-import.service.spec.ts` (enqueue-down → 503, unrelated error re-thrown, stalled → friendly message).
- ESLint clean on all changed files (scoped; no repo-wide reformat).

### PR Category
Cleanup

### Summary
Part of #22219. Moves matmul kernels to the new init model: call `compute_kernel_hw_startup` once at the top of the kernel, then `matmul_init` / `matmul_block_init` before the op.

- Adds `matmul_init` and `matmul_block_init` in `matmul.h`.
- Deprecates the old `mm_*` inits and the unused `matmul_tiles_math`.
- Migrates every matmul kernel to the new API.

To switch input formats there is no special matmul reconfig anymore — call the generic `reconfig_data_format_srca` / `reconfig_data_format_srcb` and then the init.

Matmul kernels still pass operands in normal `(in0, in1)` order, but use `compute_kernel_hw_startup<SrcOrder::Reverse>` because matmul puts in0 in SrcB and in1 in SrcA. The `SrcOrder` tag landed in #27166.

The API change and the kernel migration are in one PR on purpose, so the deprecation warnings don't pile up in kernel builds in between.

### Notes for reviewers
- The only file to really read is `matmul.h`; the rest is mechanical call-site updates.
- `compute_kernel_hw_startup` must run once at the top of the kernel, so for in-loop inits it was hoisted out of the loop.
- `compute_kernel_sentinel.cpp` keeps using the deprecated inits on purpose (it tests them).
- Removal of the deprecated `mm_*` is tracked by the reaper (#46282).

## Summary

Builds on the interactive `/set` menu introduced earlier in this branch. Adds three things users will notice:

3. **Model-cache fix** — changing the `model` key (via `/set` or the menu) used to silently leave the in-process `_SESSION_MODEL` cache stale; the menu kept showing the old value until a process restart. Now invalidated automatically.

Also packs in a handful of code-review fixes (sensitive-value masking on the slash path + password prompts in the menu, reset path recording into `changed_settings` so the coalesced reload actually fires, `max_pause_seconds` typed as float, `allow_recursion` restored to the curated catalog).

### What changed

Fixes two very small issues in `ignite/metrics/nlp/rouge.py`.

#### 1. Internal attribute typo

Previously:

```python
self._mutliref_reducer = _MultirefReducer(...)
...
self._mutliref_reducer.update(...)
```

Now:

```python
self._multiref_reducer = _MultirefReducer(...)
...
self._multiref_reducer.update(...)
```

The old name was just a typo (`mutliref`), and we only use this attribute inside `_BaseRouge`.  
No public API, arguments, or return types changed; this is just a private variable rename.

#### 2. Error message grammar

Previously:

```python
raise NotComputableError(
    "Rouge score must have at least one example before be computed"
)
```

Now:

```python
raise NotComputableError(
    "Rouge score must have at least one example before being computed"
)
```

Same exception type, same condition; only the message text is adjusted: be --> being

### Why this is low risk

- The renamed attribute is private and referenced in exactly one class, in two places, which were updated together.
- The `NotComputableError` is raised in the same scenario as before; only the human‑readable string changed.
- No behavior, configuration, or user‑facing APIs were modified.
- All tests passed throughout the entire codebase

All relevant tests pass locally; the rest of the suite will run in CI.

author: yukimemi
body:
@
## What

`Checker::auto_update` is documented to replace the binary *silently*, but on the background path `self_update` still printed its own status transcript — `Checking latest version...`, `The new release will be downloaded/extracted and the existing binary will be replaced`, `Downloading...`, `Extracting archive...`. A plain `shoka cd` (with auto-update mode = install) would suddenly dump that mid-command.

## Why

kaishin already gates its **own** `println!`s and the download-progress bar on `show_progress`. But `self_update`s status chatter is controlled by a **separate** builder flag, [`show_output`](https://docs.rs/self_update/0.44.0/self_update/backends/github/struct.UpdateBuilder.html#method.show_output), which **defaults to `true`** and was never set. So the "silent" background path was never actually silent.

## Fix

Tie `show_output` to the same `show_progress` flag as the progress bar:

```rust
.show_download_progress(show_progress)
.show_output(show_progress)
```

- background auto-update (`show_progress == false`) → fully silent
- explicit `self-update` (`show_progress == true`) → output unchanged

`cargo make check` (fmt + clippy + test + lock-check) is green.

author: arkstack-dev
body:
## Summary

Mode: **COMPATIBILITY_MODE** — confined to `*.compat.filter.*` and the `@CompatibilityMode` autoconfiguration.

`ExerisSecurityContextFilter` hardcoded `new JwtAuthenticationConverter()`, so a brownfield app's custom claim-to-authority mapping (a `Converter<Jwt, ? extends AbstractAuthenticationToken>` / `JwtAuthenticationConverter` bean — e.g. Keycloak `realm_access.roles` or a non-default `ROLE_` prefix) was **silently dropped** on the Exeris-hosted compat path. `@PreAuthorize("hasRole(...)")` that worked on plain Spring would fail after migration.

## Change

- The filter now accepts a `Converter<Jwt, ? extends AbstractAuthenticationToken>` (new constructor; the `JwtDecoder`-only constructor is retained and delegates to the default converter for backward compatibility).
- The compat autoconfiguration injects the application's converter via `ObjectProvider`, falling back to a default `JwtAuthenticationConverter` when none is registered — the same "honour the user bean, don't hardcode the default" pattern as the other compat wirings in this module. Generic resolution disambiguates the JWT converter from the module's existing `Converter<String, T>` beans.

## Out of scope (separate, security-sensitive)

Under `spring.main.web-application-type=none` (how Spring-on-Exeris runs), Spring Boot's OAuth2 resource-server auto-config is `@ConditionalOnWebApplication` and creates no `JwtDecoder`, so `@ConditionalOnBean(JwtDecoder)` leaves this filter inactive unless the app declares its own decoder. This PR unblocks apps that declare their own `JwtDecoder` (common under `none` precisely because auto-config is web-gated) + custom role mapping. Supplying a compat `JwtDecoder` from the resource-server properties is tracked separately.

## Tests

`ExerisSecurityContextFilterTest` (custom converter drives authority mapping); `ExerisCompatAutoConfigurationTest` (user `Converter<Jwt,…>` bean is wired; the unrelated `Converter<String,Integer>` is not). Web module green (127).

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The server crashes on startup with "duplicate key value violates unique constraint admins_username_key". The upsert in `backend/database.js` used `ON CONFLICT (id)`, but the database already contained a row with `username='admin'` under a different `id`. The INSERT attempted to add a new row with `id='super_default_001'` and `username='admin'`, hitting the `username` unique constraint before the `ON CONFLICT (id)` clause could activate, causing `process.exit(1)` and preventing the Express server from ever starting.

## Solution

Changed the upsert to `ON CONFLICT (username) DO UPDATE SET id=$1, password_hash=$3, role=$5`. This targets the `username` unique constraint directly, so any existing row with `username='admin'` is updated in place (including normalizing its `id` to `super_default_001`) rather than triggering a constraint violation. The server can now initialize successfully and pass the healthcheck.

### Changes
- **Modified** `backend/database.js`

### Context
- **Deployment**: [#9d2db1](https://railway.com/project/f0bb35c0-c96d-4b5e-bb8c-8e587c2f6312/environment/597f71cb-966e-4d75-847d-397029ae9418/deployment/9d2db1c7-3a62-4399-99f6-561e1adec340)

author: difcsi
body:
Ports `.circleci/config.yml` to a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`).

## What it does
Mirrors the CircleCI `build` job step-for-step:

| CircleCI | GitHub Actions |
|---|---|
| `docker: ubuntu:18.04` | `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` |
| Install dependencies (`apt`) | `Install dependencies` step (same package set, via `sudo apt-get`) |
| `checkout` + `git submodule update --init` | `actions/checkout@v4` with `submodules: recursive` |
| `make -C contrib -j 2` | `Build submodules` step (unchanged) |
| `. contrib/env.sh && ./autogen.sh && ./configure && make -j 2` | `Build project` step (unchanged) |
| `make -C tests -j 2` | `Run tests` step (unchanged) |

Triggers on `push` and `pull_request`. The build/test commands are copied verbatim.

## Notes
- `.circleci/config.yml` is left in place (additive, non-destructive); it can be removed separately to fully cut over.
- Uses the `ubuntu-latest` runner instead of the EOL `ubuntu:18.04` image (whose apt repositories are archived and would fail). A `container: ubuntu:18.04` job could be used instead if exact 18.04 parity is required.

author: o6lvl4
body:
Implements derived `Codec` decode for tuple- and record-variant payloads (#411).

## Fix
`T.decode` for a `Codec`-deriving variant type previously returned `Err("variant … payload decode not yet implemented")` for any non-unit case — only unit variants decoded. It now decodes both shapes, mirroring the tagged wire format the encoder produces:
- **tuple variant** `Wrap(Color)` → payload is a positional array; each element is decoded by its field type and the constructor is applied.
- **record variant** `Tag { name, c }` → payload is an object; each field is decoded by key/type (incl. `Option` fields) and the record-variant is constructed.

## Verification
- Round-trip (encode → decode → pattern-match) for tuple, record, multi-element, `List`-field, nested-`Codec`, and unit variants.
- `almide test spec/` 249/249 pass — no regression. Added `spec/lang/codec_variant_decode_test.almd`.

Known follow-up (not in this release): a derived codec placed in a *submodule* still emits unqualified cross-module `T_encode`/`T_decode` references (`E0425`) — tracked separately with the cross-module variant-construction work (#412).

author: alexdalgleishmorel
body:
Root cause of the post-Google-login hang/error. `_stripQuery` did `current.replace(query: '', queryParameters: {})` — Dart's `Uri.replace` throws `ArgumentError: both query and queryParameters specified`. It runs in the redirect handler *before* the token exchange, so the whole callback aborted (hence `/me` was never invoked — empty logs — and the gate spun/errored).

Fix: drop `Uri.replace` and rebuild the clean URL from `window.location.origin + pathname`.

`flutter analyze` clean, 35 tests pass.

author: backmeupplz
body:
## VEY-370

Players reported missing fleet units, raid loot not landing, and transport cargo not crediting destinations. Root cause (code side): the backend mission resolver only auto-resolved **Attack/Harvest/Colonize** arrivals and **never ran the return leg**.

- `resolveFleetMission` was never submitted for **Transport** and **Deploy**, so transport cargo and deployed ships were never delivered to the target.
- `completeFleetMissionReturn` was never submitted at all, so surviving fleets + carried loot only landed if the owner manually completed the return in the UI. Everyone else's fleet/loot/cargo got stuck (e.g. mission #12).

## Changes (backend resolver — this ticket)

- **`listResolvableFleetMissions`**: now includes `Transport` and `Deploy` arrivals (in addition to Attack/Harvest/Colonize) so `resolveFleetMission` delivers cargo to the destination / credits deployed ships.
- **`listReturnableFleetMissions`** (new): surfaces `Returning` missions whose `returnAt` has passed, for **all mission types**.
- **Resolver loop**: now submits both `resolveFleetMission` (arrival leg) and `completeFleetMissionReturn` (return leg, selector `0xc2472852`), with **separate per-leg dedup sets** so each mission is resolved once on arrival and completed once on return. Already-resolved/returned missions naturally drop out of the readers (status-filtered), so no double-submits.
- Wire `listReturnableFleetMissions` through the server resolution reader.

## Tests

- Resolver: resolves Transport/Deploy arrivals; completes Returning-past-`returnAt` missions without double-submitting across runs; resolves-then-returns the same mission id once each.
- evm reader: `listResolvableFleetMissions` includes Transport/Deploy and excludes unsupported (e.g. Intercept) and not-yet-arrived missions; `listReturnableFleetMissions` surfaces only due Returning missions across types and excludes not-yet-due ones.

Local: `bun test` (backend) 180/180 pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Out of scope (flagged separately, not this ticket)

- **Ops/deploy**: set `VEYDRIFT_MISSION_RESOLVER_ADDRESS` + a funded least-privilege signer and enable the resolver (`/health` currently shows `missionResolverConfigured=false`). The auto-resolution code is inert until that is configured.
- **UX (VEY-366)**: distinguish fleet-destroyed (`Resolved`) vs `Returning` vs `Returned` so a legit combat loss isn't read as "missing units".
- **Anomaly**: verify whether `launchFleetMission` for Transport/Deploy reverts on `test.veydrift.com` (zero such missions exist on-chain) — separate bug if so.

## Summary
- New `--agent` flag picks the in-container AI coding agent: `copilot` (default, GitHub Copilot CLI), `claude` (Anthropic Claude Code), or `opencode` (sst/opencode). The RBAC + scoped kubeconfig sandbox is unchanged — only the launched agent differs.
- **Claude Code** authenticates against a Claude Pro/Max subscription via `claude /login` on first run. Session is persisted via `--claude-config` (default `$HOME/.kpil/claude`). `IS_SANDBOX=1` is set so `--dangerously-skip-permissions` works as the in-container root user, and `/root/.claude.json` is shuttled in/out of the persisted dir on each run so the login survives container teardown. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` still honored if set.
- **OpenCode** authenticates via `opencode auth login` on first run. Session is persisted via `--opencode-config` (default `$HOME/.kpil/opencode`, with `data/` → `~/.local/share/opencode` and `config/` → `~/.config/opencode`). `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` are forwarded if set.
- Dockerfile installs `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` and `opencode-ai` globally via npm. Entrypoint routes on `AGENT`.

author: chrisschinnerl
body:
This PR decouples pinning into a separate routine instead of synchronously doing it after uploading one or more objects. This has a few reasons.

1. Pinning is slow when uploading lots of tiny, packed files. To a point where uploads can be bottlenecked by pinning.
2. A temporary issue when pinning a file shouldn't cause you to waste all that bandwidth again. So S3d will happily continue to upload until the backend becomes available again and then pin all files.


Closes https://github.com/SiaFoundation/s3d/issues/189

Users configure `memorySearch.provider: "google"` but the Google memory embedding provider is registered with id `"gemini"` only. This causes "Unknown memory embedding provider: google" at runtime.

Fixes #90786.

author: hathach
body:
## Summary
Replaces the HIL config's `build.flags_on` with an explicit, named **`variant`** schema. Each variant declares its own `name` (used as the build dir `cmake-build-<name>` and the HIL report row) and raw `flags` (CFLAGS, e.g. `-DCFG_TUD_DWC2_DMA_ENABLE=1`). A board with no `variant` builds a single target named after the board.

```json
"variant": [
  { "name": "stm32f723disco",     "flags": "" },
  { "name": "stm32f723disco-DMA", "flags": "-DCFG_TUH_DWC2_DMA_ENABLE=1" }
]
```

This makes variant build dirs and report rows explicit instead of the derived `-f1_<flags>` suffix.

## Changes
- **build.py** — `--build-name <name>` (build dir) + `--cflag=<token>` (raw CFLAGS into `CFLAGS_CLI`, repeatable; the `=`-form keeps `-D…=1` tokens space-free so they survive the CI matrix's shell word-splitting). Dropped `-f1`.
- **hil_ci_set_matrix.py** — emit one build arg per variant.
- **hil_test.py** — iterate variants; report row + firmware dir = variant name.
- **hil_ci.sh** — `-b` runs copy the board's dir plus any `cmake-build-<board>-*` variant dirs (and still fail fast when none exist).
- **get_deps.py** — accept/ignore `--build-name`/`--cflag` (matrix args are passed through it).
- **tinyusb.json** — migrate all 6 `flags_on` boards to `variant`.

## Test evidence
- Matrix emits correct per-variant args; tokens survive shell-splitting.
- `build.py` builds both `stm32f723disco` variants; DMA gets `CFLAGS_CLI=-DCFG_TUH_DWC2_DMA_ENABLE=1`, base none.
- **Hardware (ci.lan rig):** both `stm32f723disco` variants flashed and tested; report shows separate `stm32f723disco` / `stm32f723disco-DMA` rows, 0 failed.

> Stacked on #3686 (the variant report-row change depends on that PR's HIL report feature). Base will retarget to `master` once #3686 merges.

author: ujeenet
body:
## What

Closes #343. Django's `RangeField` family — a typed model-field wrapper for native PostgreSQL range columns. Mirrors the `Array<T>` design (#341).

```rust
struct Event {
    seats: Range<i32>,                      // → int4range
    during: Range<chrono::DateTime<Utc>>,   // → tstzrange
}

let e = Event { seats: (1..100).into(), during: Range::closed_open(start, end), .. };

// composes with the existing range operators
Event::objects().where_(Event::seats.range_contains("[5,6)")).fetch_pool(&pool).await?;
```

| Rust field | PG column | Django |
|---|---|---|
| `Range<i32>` | `int4range` | `IntegerRangeField` |
| `Range<i64>` | `int8range` | `BigIntegerRangeField` |
| `Range<rust_decimal::Decimal>` | `numrange` | `DecimalRangeField` |
| `Range<chrono::NaiveDate>` | `daterange` | `DateRangeField` |
| `Range<chrono::DateTime<Utc>>` | `tstzrange` | `DateTimeRangeField` |

## The gap (audit said MISSING)

`SqlValue::RangeLiteral` + `range_contains`/`range_overlap`/… operators already shipped at the value layer; the **typed field wrapper** was missing. This adds it.

## Design (same pattern as #341 ArrayField)

- **`sql/range.rs`** — `Range<T>` newtype (`lower`/`upper`: `Bound<T>`) with ergonomic ctors + `From<a..b>` + serde + `Into<SqlValue::RangeLiteral>`. Carries **total** sqlx `Type`+`Decode` for all backends: real on Postgres (delegates to sqlx's `PgRange<T>`), erroring stubs on MySQL/SQLite — so `#[derive(Model)]`'s single shared `FromRow` body compiles on every backend.
- **`FieldType::Range(RangeElem)`** — one `Copy` sub-enum → one arm per `match FieldType` site.
- **PG-only by language semantics**: DDL emits the range type on PG; MySQL/SQLite degrade to `TEXT` and the bind/decode paths error there. Litmus build still compiles.
- INSERT binds a range literal (`[lower,upper)`, `[5,)`, `(,10)`) — PG implicit-casts; SELECT decodes via `PgRange<T>` → `Range<T>` bounds.

Wired through every `FieldType` consumer (snapshot round-trip + diff, row_to_json, admin render/widget, forms parse, fixtures, OpenAPI, label).

## Tests

- `tests/range_field.rs` — 6 unit: schema maps to `FieldType::Range`, PG column/cast types (`int4range`/…/`tstzrange`), MySQL/SQLite degrade to TEXT, literal serialization.
- `tests/range_field_pg_live.rs` — 3 live (verified against real PostgreSQL): insert→fetch round-trip incl. PG discrete-range canonicalization, unbounded-upper, `@>` containment filter.

## Gates

- ✅ Litmus `cargo build --no-default-features --features sqlite,tenancy`
- ✅ `cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-run` compiles
- ✅ 3175 lib tests pass
- ✅ Audit row #343 MISSING → SHIPPED

Closes #343.

author: patriotnewsactivism
body:
## Summary

Three fixes that address the Intake Inbox crash and prevent future page errors from breaking the sidebar navigation.

### Changes

**1. Fix Intake Inbox crash (root cause)**
- `IntakeInbox.tsx` and `PublicIntake.tsx` were creating standalone Supabase clients using `import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL || ''` — when the env var isn't set, `createClient('', '')` throws "supabaseUrl is required"
- Now both use the shared client from `services/supabaseClient.ts` which has hardcoded fallback defaults

**2. Per-route error boundary**
- Moved `<ErrorBoundary>` inside `<Layout>` to wrap only page content (`<main>`)
- When a page crashes, only the content area shows the error — sidebar and header remain functional
- Previously, the ErrorBoundary wrapped the entire router, so one crash replaced the whole UI

**3. Sidebar state persistence**
- Category expansion state (Front Desk, Case Management, etc.) now saves to `localStorage`
- Sidebar groups stay open across navigation, page reloads, and error recovery
- Previously, all groups collapsed on any re-render

**4. ErrorBoundary Go Home fix**
- "Go Home" button now navigates to `/app` (dashboard) instead of `/` (landing page)
- Preserves auth state on error recovery

### Testing
- Verified the standalone Supabase client pattern was the crash cause
- Only 2 files used this pattern (IntakeInbox, PublicIntake) — both fixed

## Summary

Removes the entire **arc-paste / share** stack (UI + standalone service + backend) and restores the **legacy planner** (`arc plan` → `/planner/[planId]`) as the sole design-review surface. The share/paste feature was not well received; the legacy planner was, and it remained fully intact in the tree — so this is an *additive-layer removal*, not a code-restore.

|---|---|

Legacy planner: `cmd/arc/plan.go`, `internal/api/plans.go`, `internal/storage/sqlite/plans.go`, `web/src/routes/planner/`, migrations `004/013/014`. `CHANGELOG.md` and historical `docs/plans/*` are deliberately untouched (historical records).

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Addresses five security findings from a codebase audit:

**Critical — plaintext API key persists on disk after migration:**
The legacy `"api_key"` field was never removed from the JSON config file after being migrated to Windows Credential Manager. Both `_migrate_legacy_api_key_if_needed` (UI) and `load_agent_config` (background) now delete the key from the file immediately after successful migration/load.

**Critical — update downloads accepted over HTTP:**
`fetch_update_manifest` accepted `http://` URLs, allowing MitM on update payloads. Now restricted to `https` (and `file://` for local testing). `download_update_asset` also rejects non-HTTPS download URLs.

**Medium — SHA-1 replaced with SHA-256:**
```diff
- hashlib.sha1(payload).hexdigest()[:12]   # make_credential_target, ui_singleton_mutex_name, backup naming
+ hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()[:12]
```

**Medium — zip path-traversal hardening:**
Added explicit rejection of absolute paths and `..` path components *before* the existing `relative_to()` check in `prepare_update_payload`, preventing edge cases where symlink resolution might bypass the existing guard.

**Low — warning on legacy key detection:**
`load_normalized_config` now appends a WARNING message when a plaintext `api_key` is still present, surfacing the issue to the user even if the automatic removal hasn't run yet.

author: markusneusinger
body:
## Problem

In the Einrichtungs-Wizard (`SetupWizard`), the crop images were invisible on a portrait phone. Rotating to landscape made them appear, and desktop was always fine.

## Cause

The dialog content laid out the crop **canvas** and the **340px side panel** in a horizontal flex row, with the panel pinned at `flexShrink: 0`:

```jsx
<Box sx={{ display: 'flex', flex: 1, minHeight: 0, gap: 2, p: 2 }}>
  {canvas}
  <Box sx={{ width: 340, flexShrink: 0, overflowY: 'auto' }}>{panel}</Box>
</Box>
```

On a narrow viewport the non-shrinking 340px panel consumed nearly the whole width, squeezing the canvas (`flex: 1`) to near-zero — so the crop image was effectively invisible. Landscape gave enough horizontal room for the canvas to reappear; desktop was always wide enough to be unaffected.

## Fix

Below the `md` breakpoint the dialog now:

- goes **full-screen** for maximum room, and
- **stacks** the canvas over the panel (flex column), with the panel capped at `40%` height and scrollable.

This guarantees the crop canvas always keeps a usable share of the viewport in portrait. Desktop (`md` and up) layout is unchanged.

## Verification

- `npm run type-check` passes.

author: arkadipta
body:
## Problem

Three distinct bugs combined to produce broken alarm behaviour:

1. **`AlarmDismissActivity` never launched on unlocked screen** — `setFullScreenIntent()` is documented to promote to a full-screen launch only when the device is locked. On an unlocked screen Android demotes it to a heads-up notification (HUN) and never starts the activity.

2. **Reverb / dual audio on locked screen** — posting a notification with `CATEGORY_ALARM` + `IMPORTANCE_HIGH` caused SystemUI's `RingtonePlayer` to play `alarm_alert` independently, while `AlarmDismissActivity`'s `MediaPlayer` also played. Opening the notification drawer revoked one audio-focus grant, stopping one of the two sources.

3. **Status-bar alarm icon triggered alarm early** — `scheduleAlarmClock()` passed the same `PendingIntent` as both the `AlarmClockInfo` show-intent and the operation. Tapping the clock icon in the status bar fired `ReminderReceiver` with `ACTION_REMINDER`.

## Changes

### `ReminderReceiver.kt`
For ALARM delivery, `handleReminder()` now calls `context.startActivity()` with the `AlarmDismissActivity` intent directly. `setAlarmClock()` places the app on Android's [background-activity-start whitelist](https://developer.android.com/guide/components/activities/background-starts), so this works on locked and unlocked screens on Android 10–16. No notification is posted for alarm delivery — the activity is the alarm UI, and removing the notification eliminates the SystemUI audio path and the unwanted panel entry.

### `ReminderScheduler.kt`
`scheduleAlarmClock()` now creates a separate `showIntent` (opens `MainActivity`) for `AlarmClockInfo`, distinct from the operation `PendingIntent` that fires `ReminderReceiver`.

### `NotificationHelper.kt`
Alarm channel renamed to `lifelog_alarms_v2` with `setSound(null, null)` explicitly set. The old `lifelog_alarms` channel (which lacked the silent sound config) is deleted on `createChannels()`, ensuring existing installs get the corrected channel.

## Expected behaviour after fix

| Screen state | AlarmDismissActivity | Audio sources | Panel notification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Locked | ✅ Launches | 1 (MediaPlayer only) | None |
| Unlocked | ✅ Launches | 1 (MediaPlayer only) | None |

## Test plan
- [ ] Schedule an ALARM reminder for 1–2 minutes from now
- [ ] Lock screen — confirm full-screen UI appears, single audio source, no reverb, no notification in panel
- [ ] Unlock screen — confirm full-screen UI appears, single audio source, no notification in panel
- [ ] Dismiss from alarm UI — confirm audio stops, activity finishes
- [ ] Snooze from alarm UI — confirm audio stops, alarm re-fires after 10 min
- [ ] Tap status-bar clock icon (if visible) — confirm it opens LifeLog, does not fire the alarm early
- [ ] NOTIFICATION reminder type — confirm unchanged behaviour (HUN + panel notification)

author: akiraveliara
body:
this could happen if a reconnect was initiated (i.e. by an IGatewayController that reconnected on Zombied) while the system was disconnected from the internet and at least one event had been sent to the gateway since the system disconnected

might be distro-specific or stack-specific, but the underlying issue is that the system doesn't report that sending the event failed, so as far as CWS is concerned, it's just taking its sweet time and we end up building up events and partial state changes that never get resolved and get the gateway stuck

also moves the isConnected check to where it actually makes sense, as opposed to getting us into an invalid state that needs another reconnect to recover. that was kind of silly.

author: michaelayoade
body:
## Summary

Validated the comprehensive mobile UI/UX audit against the actual `mobile/lib` code and implemented the findings that held up. About 40% of the audit was stale (screenshots predated recent code) — **dark mode, the fl_chart usage chart, support empty-state/status-chips, and login autofill/biometric were already shipped** and are left untouched.

One genuine gap couldn't be fully closed: the audit's "Verify email" action needs a backend resend endpoint that doesn't exist (`app/api/auth_flow.py` has no verify-email route). Rather than fake an API call, the unverified state is surfaced prominently and the gap is flagged in code.

## P0 — systemic
- **Caching + stale-while-revalidate:** a `cacheFor` helper keepAlives autoDispose data providers for 5 min after the last listener, so revisiting a screen shows cached data instantly instead of refetching from a bare spinner. `AsyncValueView` keeps stale data on screen during background refresh (thin progress bar) and on a failed refresh.
- **Skeleton loaders:** dependency-free `Shimmer` + `SkeletonBox`/`ListSkeleton`/`CardSkeleton`, wired into invoices, payments, activity, notifications, tickets, sessions, usage, invoice detail, and the dashboard service card.
- **Cold-start hardening:** cache last profile (`Me.toJson`) in secure storage; `bootstrap()` renders optimistically from it and refreshes `/auth/me` behind; only forces re-login on 401/403, keeps the cached session on transient network failures.

## P1 — per-screen
- **Dashboard:** suspended banner tappable → `/billing`; multi-service switcher chips when >1 subscription; Renew/Reactivate CTA on suspended/expiring services.
- **Invoices:** outstanding-balance header, status filter chips (All/Unpaid/Overdue/Paid), inline Pay on each unpaid row (pay flow extracted to shared `InvoicePayButton`).
- **Notifications:** items deep-link to the relevant tab (billing/support/usage) with a chevron affordance.
- **Profile:** hide empty Locale/Timezone rows; unverified email shown prominently.

## Testing
- `flutter analyze lib/` → clean
- `flutter test` → **62 pass** (52 existing + 10 new: profile-cache round-trip, invoice filters, notification routing, service selection)
- No new dependencies; no `pubspec.lock` churn.

### 1. Untitled 문서 타이틀을 사이드바에서 누르면 문서가 사라짐
이미 열려 있는 Untitled(fresh-blank) 메모의 사이드바 행을 클릭하면 `openMemo` → `leaveCurrent`가 그 메모를 purge한 뒤, 방금 삭제된 메모를 다시 열려고 해서 사이드바에서 사라졌음.

→ 이미 열려 있는 메모를 다시 클릭하면 no-op으로 처리 (hashchange / Alt+J,K 핸들러의 기존 가드와 동일).

### 2. 변경 없는 Untitled 문서는 휴지통에 들어갈 필요 없이 그냥 삭제
서버 메모 삭제는 항상 soft-delete(휴지통 + Undo 토스트)였음. 이번 세션에서 만들어졌고 내용을 가진 적 없는 빈 메모(`freshIds`로 추적)는 `?purge=1`로 hard-delete — 휴지통 행 없음, 토스트 없음. 대기 중인 저장 타이머도 취소해 되살아나지 않게 함.

author: jamiedz999
body:
moving_window_similarity1 rebuilt the Q×W RapidFuzz matrix per window and
ran the greedy assignment on every window -- ~0.30 s/doc at Q=8, ~1.30 s/doc
at Q=16 on an 8000-word doc.

- Precompute the Q×N normalized-distance matrix once (per-query-word cache
  dedupes identical doc words), removing the W× redundant recompute.
- Per-window lower bound = (Σ_k min_j∈window D[k][j]) / Q via a monotonic-deque
  sliding-window min. This provably bounds the greedy score from below.
- Run the greedy assignment only on windows whose lower bound ≤ threshold;
  always keep the global-best (lowest-bound) window so results[0] is never empty.
- Add dissimilarity_threshold (default ∞ ⇒ no pruning ⇒ byte-identical to
  before); run_search forwards its real threshold and uses .only() to skip
  unused field deserialization.

bench_search.py: 10.1× at Q=8, 20.6× at Q=16, best window unchanged.

Closes #17

## What

Low-batch fix: the drift check read an **unreadable** upstream validator version as "still current". `checkDrift` guarded the compare with `if (fetched.validatorVersion && …)`, so an empty/missing version was skipped silently; and `runDrift` collapsed "reachable PyPI but no `info.version`" and "offline" into the same `undefined`.
