author: tjgriffin
body:
Fixes #6.

## Problem
`findDuplicatesByIds(recordIds)` returns results in the order of the input `List<Id>`. But `getMergeCandidates` iterated `recordMap.keySet()` with a positional index `i` into `duplicateResults[i]`. `Map.keySet()` order is not guaranteed to match the `recordIds` list, so a record could be paired with another record's duplicate result — recording the wrong keep/merge ids on the candidate. Likely the root cause behind the earlier "findduplicate mismatch" commits.

## Fix
- `processRecords` now passes the same ordered `recordIds` list (the one handed to `findDuplicatesByIds`) into `getMergeCandidates`.
- New 4-arg `getMergeCandidates(recordMap, recordIds, duplicateResults, duplicateRules)` iterates `recordIds` by index, pairing each record with its own result.
- The original 3-arg overload is retained as a thin delegator for compatibility.
- Removed the now-redundant manual `i++` (the `for` loop increments).

## Verification note
`Datacloud.FindDuplicatesResult` has no public constructor and its nested `MatchRecord.getRecord()` structure is impractical to mock reliably, so an executable pairing test is deferred to Comprehensive Testing issue #15 (which explicitly covers "candidate pairing regardless of map ordering" and can introduce a proper injection seam). Fix verified by static review.

Pre-existing latent NPE at the `duplicateRule.ruleName` line (when no matching rule) was left untouched — out of scope for this fix.

🚀 This PR updates the ARM64 Docker image to Ubuntu 26.04 and tightens Python version limits for several export-related dependencies to avoid compatibility issues with Python 3.14.

## Fix

Addresses SSRF vulnerability in `validateHelmRepoURL` (#216): the function previously only validated the URL scheme, allowing `http://` and `https://` to private/cloud-metadata IPs.

### Changes

**`pkg/deploy/mcp/tools_helm.go`**
- Only `https://` is now accepted (`http://` is blocked)
- IP-literal hosts are checked directly against blocked ranges (no DNS needed)
- Domain names are resolved via `helmHostResolver` and all resolved IPs are checked against: loopback, private (RFC1918), link-local, CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10), cloud metadata (169.254.169.254/32), IETF (192.0.0.0/24)
- `helmHostResolver` is a package-level var (default: `net.LookupHost`) — injectable in tests

**`pkg/deploy/mcp/tools_helm_test.go`**
- Added `setHelmMockResolver` helper to stub DNS in tests
- Updated `TestHandleHelmInstallDiscoversClustersAndPassesFlags` to use the stub (fixes CI failure from #217 where `charts.example.com` failed DNS resolution)
- Added `TestValidateHelmRepoURL` — table-driven tests for scheme/IP-literal rejection

body:
@
## What

A self-contained, single-machine Sorcha deployment sized for **~10–20 users**.
Pulls the published `sorchadev/*` images — the target needs only a container
runtime, **no source tree or .NET SDK**.

```
docker/desktop/
  docker-compose.desktop.yml   # standalone, image-only, core + citizen-wallet
  .env.desktop.example         # config template (runtime .env stays git-ignored)
  postgres-init.sql
  README.md
scripts/deploy-desktop.{sh,ps1} # detect runtime → preflight → pull → up → health → bootstrap
```

## Design choices
- **License-free runtime first**: scripts detect Podman → Rancher → Docker.
- **Scope = core + citizen wallet**: drops `aspire-dashboard` + `mcp-server-http`
  (~1.5 GB RAM). Telemetry off (OTLP endpoint omitted → `ServiceDefaults` leaves
  the exporter unwired).
- **Rootless-safe**: gateway is HTTP-only on `:8880` (no <1024 bind); databases
  publish no host ports.
- **Fail-closed**: `${VAR:?}` guards refuse to start without JWT/DB secrets.
- Lives under `docker/` because `deploy/` is git-ignored for local runtime state.

## Verified
- `docker compose config` resolves (exit 0); telemetry off; all published ports >1024.
- Both scripts pass syntax/parse checks; required-var guard fires on missing secrets.
- `.sh` committed `100755` (executable on Unix targets).

## NOT verified (tracked in #989)
End-to-end boot on a clean machine (image pull, rootless Podman health-gates,
volume permissions, auto-bootstrap). The PowerShell `Test-DesktopResources`
gate policy is intentionally a stub for the operator.

Resolves part of #989 (artifacts); #989 tracks the clean-machine test.

author: mastersingh24
body:
Closes #122.

## Summary

When \`--agentic-small-model\` is unset, infer the cheap-tier model from the parent's provider rather than silently inheriting the parent's model. Operators on Opus/Pro who never set the flag now get the cost-efficiency win automatically — completing the \"it just works\" story started by PR #118 (agentic-tools default-on).

| Parent provider | Auto-default small model |
|---|---|
| \`gemini\`, \`vertex\` | \`gemini-2.5-flash\` |
| \`anthropic\`, \`anthropic-vertex\` | \`claude-haiku-4-5\` |
| \`echo\`, \`scripted\` | (no cheap-tier concept; subtasks inherit parent) |
| (operator-override via \`--agentic-small-model=ID\`) | whatever they passed |

## Why it composes via an optional interface

\`models.Provider\` itself is unchanged. The new \`SmallModelDefaulter\` is an *optional* extension that providers implement to declare their cheap-tier model:

\`\`\`go
type SmallModelDefaulter interface {
    DefaultSmallModel() string
}

func ResolveSmallModel(p Provider, override string) string {
    if override != "" { return override }
    if d, ok := p.(SmallModelDefaulter); ok { return d.DefaultSmallModel() }
    return ""
}
\`\`\`

External provider implementations don't break — they just don't get the new defaulting behavior unless they opt in. Mock providers (\`echo\`, \`scripted\`) intentionally don't implement it; subtasks inherit the parent's mock LLM as before.

## Startup observability

Resolution result is logged at startup so operators see what's in effect:

\`\`\`
core-agent: agentic subtasks: claude-haiku-4-5 (provider default)
core-agent: agentic subtasks: gemini-2.5-flash (operator override)
core-agent: agentic subtasks: inherit parent (echo — no cheap-tier default for provider \"echo\")
\`\`\`

## Hugo docs updated

- \`docs/site/content/docs/getting-started.md\` — \`--agentic-small-model\` help line.
- \`docs/site/content/docs/reference/context-management.md\` — Mechanism B \"Configuring\" examples.
- \`docs/site/content/docs/agent-design/cost-efficiency.md\` — Pro+Flash split now describes auto-default behavior since v2.5.

## Test plan

- [x] \`dev/ci/presubmits/build\` — clean
- [x] \`dev/ci/presubmits/vet\` — clean
- [x] \`dev/ci/presubmits/verify-go-format\` — clean
- [x] \`dev/ci/presubmits/test-unit\` — all green, including new \`pkg/models/provider_test.go\`, \`pkg/models/anthropic/anthropic_test.go\`, and added cases in \`pkg/models/gemini/gemini_test.go\`
- [x] \`dev/ci/presubmits/lint-go\` — no new findings on changed files (2 pre-existing findings in stale \`.claude/worktrees/\` paths, unrelated to this PR)
- [ ] Manual: \`core-agent --model claude-opus-4-7\` → startup log shows \"agentic subtasks: claude-haiku-4-5 (provider default)\"
- [ ] Manual: \`core-agent --model gemini-3.5-pro --agentic-small-model gemini-2.5-flash\` → log shows \"(operator override)\"

## Related

- #118 — agentic-tools default on (shipped). This PR completes the \"it just works\" story by ensuring the cost-efficiency win activates without operator config.
- #124 — transparent agentic MCP wrapping (design doc in PR #125, now merged). Hard-depends on this PR for cost-efficiency in the default case.

## Summary
- **Root cause (tap):** `<video onClick={togglePlay}>` meant every surface tap paused/played the video. `onTouchStart` on the wrapper also called `reveal()` before the click, causing a show→immediately-hide conflict on first tap.
- **Root cause (fullscreen):** Missing `type="button"`, no `stopPropagation`, and `webkitFullscreenElement` not checked when deciding whether to exit.

## Changes
- `aim-player.tsx`: remove `onTouchStart`; change video `onClick` → `toggleControls`; add `toggleControls` function; add `stopPropagation` to center play + fullscreen buttons; fix webkit fullscreen detection
- `aim-player.css`: update video comment only

## Behavior after fix
| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Tap empty player area (1st) | Show overlay controls |
| Tap empty player area (2nd) | Hide overlay controls |
| Tap center play/pause | Toggle play/pause only |
| Tap fullscreen button | Enter/exit fullscreen |
| Mouse move (desktop) | Reveal controls, auto-hide |

## What is NOT changed
- HLS playback, subtitles/CC, speed menu, volume, timeline, watch progress — all untouched

## Summary

This PR makes QA profile channel drivers executable and separates channel selection from the driver that provides it.

- Adds `crabline` as a QA Lab devDependency pinned to merged Crabline main commit `f7d034d90a8005c61fe38216462f385b9fe9f018`.
- Runs the `smoke-ci` Crabline path by asking Crabline for an OpenClaw adapter, then using the returned binding to configure OpenClaw's normal channel plugin against a Crabline fake provider server.
- Keeps the default synthetic QA path as `qa-channel`, keeps `live` declarative for release-profile wiring, and normalizes `qa-channel | crabline | live` before driver-specific setup.
- Keeps channel support, fake-provider startup, OpenClaw plugin config, target mapping, inbound payload mapping, and recorder decoding in Crabline's OpenClaw adapter instead of duplicating those semantics in QA Lab.
- Keeps Crabline scoped to QA Lab as a devDependency, with an explicit QA Lab-only contract exception for the optional runtime import so it does not become a production runtime dependency.

## Why

QA scenarios should ask for a channel such as `telegram`, while the selected profile decides whether that exchange uses the synthetic QA channel, a Crabline fake provider server, or a live provider. `smoke-ci` is the deterministic Crabline profile; release evidence remains reserved for live channel drivers.

## Summary

Implements the [workflow-instance-visibility proposal](https://github.com/lemmit/Loc/blob/main/docs/proposals/workflow-instance-visibility.md) (#1034): a **read-only surface for observing running workflow instances**, reusing the aggregate read pipeline rather than inventing new machinery.

Workflow sagas already persist a correlation/saga-state row per instance (`workflowStateTableShape` mirrors `tableForAggregate`), but until now there was no API and no UI to see them — only the `POST` trigger and the trigger *form*. This adds the read half (list + by-id) across all three backends, the React client, and scaffolding, derived from a new `instanceWireShape` on `WorkflowIR`.

## What's included (6 slices, each tested)

1. **IR/enrichment** — `WorkflowIR.instanceWireShape` derived for correlation-bearing, non-event-sourced workflows (correlation field as the `id`/`token` row, then state fields).
2. **Hono** — `GET /workflows/<snake>/instances` + `/{id}` inside the existing workflows router, over the saga Drizzle table, with `<Wf>InstanceResponse`/`...ListResponse` Zod DTOs.
3. **React** — `useAll<Wf>Instances()` / `use<Wf>InstanceById(id)` hooks + api-hook-detector patterns F/G (`<Wf>.instances.all` / `.byId(id)`) wired through `tsx-target`.
4. **Scaffold/walker** — `scaffoldInstanceList`/`scaffoldInstanceDetails` sentinels (registry + language mirror), `<Wf>InstancesList`/`<Wf>InstanceDetail` pages, expander → QueryView/Table + KeyValueRow Card, two new `PageOriginIR` kinds, conventional emit paths, App.tsx routing.
5. **.NET** — `<Wf>InstanceResponse` DTO + `<Ctx>WorkflowInstancesController` GET list/by-id over the EF saga DbSet.
6. **Phoenix** — saga-state Ecto schema emitted for every correlation workflow + `WorkflowInstancesController` (Repo-backed index/show, camelCase wire) + router routes.

Read-only by design; write paths unchanged. Driven off `instanceWireShape`, so an event-triggered-only saga is observable too.

## Testing

- Full fast suite green: **4153 passed**, `tsc -b` + Biome clean.
- New per-layer tests: enrichment, Hono routes, React hooks + detector, scaffold/expansion, .NET controller, Phoenix controller/router.
- The .NET (`dotnet build /warnaserror`) and Phoenix (`mix compile --warnings-as-errors`) compile gates run here in CI — those backends were validated at the string level locally (no local SDK/mix).

## Decisions deferred (per the proposal)

Event-sourced workflow instance views (fold-from-stream) and the per-instance event timeline; the `view`-source alternative. Opt-in vs default and pagination noted as open questions.

author: justinlooney
body:
## Summary

DEV/TEST tooling for the two-box prototype (not a shipped or safety artifact). Two new crates, **serde + bincode + std only**.

### `crates/kirra-wire-client` — the single shared wire mirror
Client-side mirror of `kirra-governor-service`'s UDP schema, reused by the bench now and the future car bridge node (so the wire types are defined once on the client side; no `kirra-runtime-sdk` dependency).
- `Proposal { seq, ts_nanos, ProposedCommand }` (Serialize) and `Verdict { seq, ClientEnforceAction, reason_code }` (Deserialize; `ClientEnforceAction { Allow, ClampLinear, ClampSteering, DenyBreach(ClientDenyCode) }`, `ClientDenyCode` with the 10 variants).
- **Wire-format invariant**: bincode puts no names on the wire — enums encode by positional variant index, structs by field order — so variant/field order here MUST mirror `src/gateway/kinematics_contract.rs` (`EnforceAction`/`DenyCode`/`ProposedVehicleCommand`) and the governor's `Proposal`/`Verdict`. A prominent boxed comment states this, and **`wire_layout` drift tests pin the byte layout**: a known-bytes deny verdict decodes+re-encodes, the Allow case, **all 10 deny indices**, the clamp `f64` payload, and the proposal prefix/size.

### `crates/kirra-proposal-bench` — UDP bench
Sends a sweep to `KIRRA_GOVERNOR_ADDR` (default `127.0.0.1:9760`), decodes each verdict via the mirror, prints a CASE/REASON/VERDICT table. Depends only on `kirra-wire-client`.

## Verification

`cargo tree` (both crates) → **bincode + serde only** (no tokio/r2r/ROS/axum/rusqlite/reqwest/hyper/parent-crate). `cargo build`/`cargo test` clean — wire-client drift tests: **5 passed**.

End-to-end against a live `kirra-governor-service` (`6/6` answered) — the observed table:

```
CASE                 | REASON                     | VERDICT
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
nominal accept       | ACCEPT                     | Allow
over-speed clamp     | CLAMP_LINEAR               | ClampLinear(35.000 m/s)
reverse over-speed   | CLAMP_LINEAR               | ClampLinear(-35.000 m/s)
hard steering step   | CLAMP_STEER                | ClampSteering(4.500 deg)
NaN deny             | NanInfLinearVelocity       | DenyBreach (reason_code=1)
zero-dt deny         | InvalidTimeDelta           | DenyBreach (reason_code=6)
```

The deny rows decoded to the **correct mirror variants** (`NanInfLinearVelocity`→1, `InvalidTimeDelta`→6) over the real wire — i.e. the governor encoded with the *core* types and the client mirror decoded the right semantics, which is the actual cross-crate drift check.

## Guardrails
- `src/gateway/kinematics_contract.rs` **unchanged** — not edited, not in the diff. Blob `997fb7ae15ce3e11adec9218044c7c84b049ad3b` verified start and end.
- No `git add -A`; staged only `Cargo.toml` (workspace members) + the two new crates.

author: stephendolan
body:
## Problem

Jack hit this: the Claude **sidekick** and both Claude **coaches** (pairing, drama-triangle) had exactly one live-follow path — catch up via `Bash --catchup`, then `Monitor` the continuous watcher. On **Bedrock, `Monitor` is disabled**, so live-follow had nowhere to go. The continuous watcher is an infinite loop; under plain `Bash` it blocks forever, the turn hangs, and nothing emits. That's the "Monitor wasn't working" symptom — the script was fine, the one path Claude was given depended on a tool that wasn't there.

Codex works because it has no `Monitor` and was already told to loop `--exit-on-batch` (run → batch → exit → repeat).

## Fix

Give each Claude harness the Codex-style fallback while keeping `Monitor` as the preferred path (it's superior — wakes on emit, lowest latency/cost — so we use it whenever it's available):

- **`Monitor` available** → subscribe to the continuous watcher, end turn, wait for records (unchanged).
- **No `Monitor`** (e.g. Bedrock) → loop `tuple-call-watcher.py --exit-on-batch` over `Bash`; never end the turn until `call_ended`.

### Watcher: new `--max-wait SECS`

The coaches' silence detection (quiet pair, silent driver, long grind, no goal) is driven by a fallback timer, because silence produces **no transcript records** to unblock `--exit-on-batch` — so a naive Bash-loop swap would block forever in a quiet room and silently disable half the coaching value.

`--max-wait SECS` makes `--exit-on-batch` return an empty batch after a silent stretch, handing the agent a turn to run its periodic checks. Each empty return is the same tick the Monitor path got from its fallback timer. The pairing coach uses it for real silence checks; the drama coach (purely line-based) just re-runs.

## Scope

| Trigger | Change |
|---|---|
| `sidekick-claude` | Monitor preferred + `--exit-on-batch` Bash fallback |
| `coach-pairing-claude` | same; empty `--max-wait 120` returns = silence ticks |
| `coach-drama-triangle-claude` | same; empty `--max-wait 300` returns are no-ops |
| `tuple-call-watcher.py` (×9) | new `--max-wait` flag, propagated byte-identically |
| READMEs | document the Bedrock fallback |

Untouched because already safe: **codex/opencode sidekicks** already loop `--exit-on-batch`; **call-summary** triggers run `--catchup` one-shot (no Monitor dependency, fire on `call-transcription-complete`).

## Validation

- `--max-wait` behavior tested empirically: times out to empty exit at the deadline, returns fast on a real batch, rejects non-numeric values (exit 2).
- All 9 watcher copies `py_compile` clean and remain byte-identical.
- All three reworked triggers pass their dry-run (`*_DRY_RUN=1`) and generate coherent prompts.

Received undefined` ### Fix Removed the unused `import.meta.url`/`fileURLToPath` compatibility block from `server.ts` (the values weren’t used elsewhere), so the CJS server no longer touches `import.meta`. ### Verification - `npm run build` succeeds. - `node dist/server.cjs` starts successfully. - `/api/health` responds with `{ status: "ok" }` when `GEMINI_API_KEY` is set. ### Deployment Render start command remains `node dist/server.cjs`.

## Problem

Fixes #9653. When a config combines an extension hook with a function-based prompt (e.g. a Python `file://prompt.py:create_prompt`), the prompt function stops being executed — the **raw source code of the prompt file is sent to the model as text** instead of the generated messages. Removing the hook restores correct behavior.

Reproduced with the exact config from the issue using the `echo` provider (echoes the rendered prompt):

**Without this fix** — the raw Python source is sent:
```
"def create_prompt(context: dict) -> list:\n    topic = context['vars']['topic']\n    return [ ... ]\n"
```

**With this fix** — the function runs and the messages are sent:
```json
[{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant who will answer the user's questions."},
 {"role":"user","content":"What is Linear Algebra?"}]
```

## Root cause

Extension hooks receive the test suite serialized as JSON — Python (and JS) hooks run in a subprocess, so the context is passed through `JSON.stringify`. JSON cannot represent the non-serializable `function` callable that `file://...:fn` prompts carry (`Prompt.function`), so it is dropped on the round-trip.

In `runExtensionHook`'s `beforeAll` branch, the returned (deserialized) prompts overwrite the in-memory prompts, so every prompt loses its `function`. At eval time `renderPrompt` checks `if (prompt.function)` — now false — and falls back to using `prompt.raw` (the file source) as the prompt text.

## Solution

After a `beforeAll` hook returns, re-attach the `function` to each returned prompt from the original in-memory prompts. A returned prompt is matched to an original by `label` (the stable identifier for file-based prompts), and the function is restored only when:

- the original carried a `function`, and
- the `raw` source is unchanged — so a hook that intentionally rewrites a prompt keeps its new behavior.

Labels that appear more than once are treated as ambiguous and skipped, to avoid restoring the wrong function. Hooks that don't return prompts are unaffected.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run test/evaluatorHelpers.test.ts` — added two regression tests: one asserting the function is restored after a serialized round-trip, one asserting it is **not** restored when the hook rewrites `raw`.
- Verified end-to-end with the issue's config (Python prompt + Python extension hook) against the `echo` provider, confirming the executed messages are sent instead of the raw source.

author: russellromney
body:
Fixes two adversarial-review findings in the proc-macro crates. Both are macro hygiene bugs where the generated code silently did the wrong thing for plausibly-named user input.

## H7 (High, data corruption) — `tina-rpc-macros`
The generated `<method>_request` builder bound `let encoding`/`let payload` locals. A trait method arg of the same name (e.g. `fn set(&self, encoding: ContentEncoding, payload: Vec<u8>)`) shadowed the caller's value, so the wire encoded the encoder default instead of the caller's value — silent wrong bytes.

- Rename generated locals to `__tina_encoding`/`__tina_payload` (defense-in-depth: can't shadow a user arg).
- Add `encoding`/`payload` to `RESERVED_REQUEST_PARAMS` so such args are rejected with a clear, spanned diagnostic at the arg, not an opaque `Json: Serialize is not satisfied` deep in generated code.
- Compile-fail fixtures pin the rejection for both names.

Before the fix, `fn charge(&mut self, encoding: u64)` failed with `the trait bound Json: serde::Serialize is not satisfied` spanned at the `#[service]` attribute — the user's `encoding` arg silently replaced by the encoder default in the args tuple.

## H8 (Medium) — `tina-macros`
`require_call_authority_mentioned` stringified the handler body token stream and searched for the bare token `call`. String-literal contents leak through token stringification, so a split `handle_request` whose body only mentions `call` inside a `&str` literal passed the must-use-authority gate without ever using caller authority.

- Replace the text scan with a `syn::visit` visitor that counts expression-position uses of the call binding. Literal contents and comments are never expressions, so they no longer satisfy the gate.
- Compile-fail fixture: a body mentioning `call` only in a string literal now fails with the authority-rail message. Pass fixture: a real `call` use alongside a misleading string still compiles.

Verified the old token scan would have passed the new fail fixture; the AST visitor rejects it.

## Tests
- `cargo test` clean for `tina-rpc`, `tina-rpc-macros`, `tina-macros`, `tina-runtime`.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean on all four touched crates.

author: lcsgmoraes-droid
body:
## Problema (achado da auditoria, severidade Alta)

O deploy de produção (`scripts/deploy_producao_seguro.sh`) roda `alembic upgrade head` **sem backup do banco antes** e **sem rollback**. Em qualquer migration problemática numa tabela financeira/fiscal, não há rede de segurança. O `db_backup_dir` (`backups/db`) já era criado, mas **nunca usado**; `HEAD_BEFORE` era gravado mas nunca usado para reverter.

## O que muda

Entre **subir o Postgres** e **aplicar as migrations**, adiciona uma etapa `backup_banco`:

1. **`pg_dump -F c`** (formato custom, compactado e restaurável via `pg_restore`) do `petshop_prod` para `backups/db/petshop_prod_<timestamp>.dump`.
2. **Validação**: se o `pg_dump` falhar **ou** o arquivo ficar vazio, **aborta ANTES de migrar** (`fail`) — não migra sem backup.
3. **Retenção**: mantém os últimos `DB_BACKUP_KEEP` dumps (default 10).
4. **Rollback acionável**: em qualquer falha **após** o backup (ex.: health pós-migration), o handler de erro imprime instruções prontas — `pg_restore --clean --if-exists`, `git reset --hard HEAD_BEFORE` e rebuild — com o caminho exato do dump.

## Decisões de design

- **Rollback manual, não automático.** Restaurar o banco automaticamente é destrutivo (se o código novo já gravou dados sob o schema novo, restaurar o dump perde isso). Para um ERP financeiro, o rollback deve ser **confirmado por um humano** — por isso instruções acionáveis em vez de auto-restore.
- **Não executa deploy nem altera o fluxo** existente — só adiciona a etapa de backup e o hint. O deploy real continua manual e sob autorização.

## Por que importa agora

Esta rede **desbloqueia as migrações de dados represadas** da frente multi-tenant (tornar `tenant_id` NOT NULL em `comissoes_itens`, `dre_periodos`, `ops_*`, `bling_webhook`, e corrigir o `VariacaoConfigFiscal` Integer→UUID) — que eu não recomendava rodar sem backup.

## Validação

- ✅ `bash -n` (sintaxe) OK.
- ⚠️ Não executável em CI (precisa do Postgres de produção). Revisar o trecho `backup_banco` e testar idealmente num deploy de staging.

author: raahulrahl
body:
## What this pull request adds

One new directory, `examples/agno-bindu/`, plus two short pointer lines (one each in
`README.md` and `docs/ko/README.md`). It exposes this project's contract-review
methodology as an [agno](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno) agent served over the
[Bindu](https://github.com/GetBindu/Bindu) Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol: you `POST`
contract text to a local HTTP endpoint and get back a clause-by-clause review.

The notable part: the agent does **not** reimplement your review logic. It **loads your
own `.claude/skills/` at runtime** through agno's Skills feature — reading
`review-domain-knowledge` (your four-lens framework and risk-grading guide),
`clause-segmenter`, and your `policies.default/` review modes — and reasons with them.
Your skills stay the source of truth.

This is **additive and low-risk**: no file under `.claude/`, `contract-review/`,
`scripts/`, or `tests/` is modified, CI is untouched, and the extra Python packages live
only in `examples/agno-bindu/requirements.txt` and install into a separate virtualenv.
Your skills are read in place — nothing is copied or generated.

## Who is contributing this

Contributed by the team at [Bindu](https://github.com/GetBindu/Bindu). This agent is one
entry in the Bindu example showcase; your project provides the actual review intelligence
it relies on, and the example links back here as the canonical source. We'll also link to
your repo from Bindu's examples index so discovery flows both ways.

## How the example is shaped

- A2A over JSON-RPC 2.0, with a DID identity and a public agent card.
- agno provides the agent loop (model call + tool-calling); the model is any OpenRouter
  model (default `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`).
- Entry points: `bindu_agent.py` (the A2A service) and `cli.py` (a one-shot local runner).

`skills_loader.py` is the only non-obvious piece. Your `SKILL.md` files mostly have no YAML
frontmatter, which agno's default loader requires. Rather than touch them, it ships a small
`ClaudeCodeSkills` adapter that loads them with validation off (folder name → skill name,
description backfilled from the line under each H1) and points `source_path` straight at
your skill folders, so their `references/` and `scripts/` are read in place.

## The API surface

On `http://localhost:3773`:

- `GET /.well-known/agent.json` — the agent card; the DID is under
  `capabilities.extensions[].uri` as `did:bindu:…`.
- `GET /.well-known/did.json` — the DID document.
- `GET /health` — health (`health: healthy`, `task_manager_running: true`).
- `POST /` — JSON-RPC: `message/send` (returns a task id, state `submitted`) then
  `tasks/get` (poll to `completed`). Each `message/send` carries four UUIDs.

The example README has a copy-paste snippet for the full round-trip. Contract text is sent
as a `text` part — A2A file attachments are unreliable in current Bindu versions, so the
example asks callers to paste text rather than shipping a path that silently fails.

## How the agent is instructed

The system prompt keeps the agent grounded and scoped:

1. **Ground in your skills first** — load `review-domain-knowledge` + `clause-segmenter`
   and the `review-guide.md` / `audience-firewall.md` references before analyzing; cite the
   loaded criteria rather than answering from memory.
2. **Follow your methodology** — classify the family, segment clauses, apply the four lenses
   (asymmetries, overbroad qualifiers, missing protections, structural traps), grade risk
   per the selected review mode (`strict` / `moderate` / `loose`).
3. **Respect the audience firewall** — `[EXTERNAL]` comments never carry strategy or
   fallback positions.
4. **Stay in scope** — review pasted text; decline non-contract questions; ask one
   clarifying question when the contract or party is missing; never attempt the full local
   pipeline (DOCX, library retrieval, hooks, pipeline-state).

## End-to-end verification

Run with a real `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (model `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`) against
`bindu 2026.21.2` / agno 2.6.5. Six representative examples, each through **both** the CLI
and the **live A2A service** (`message/send` → `tasks/get`):

| # | What we sent | Tools the agent loaded | CLI | Live A2A |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SaaS agreement, customer side (default *moderate*) | `get_skill_instructions`×2, `get_skill_reference`(review-guide, audience-firewall), `load_policy`(contract-families, review-mode) | ✅ family=SaaS; 3 Critical / 1 High / 1 Medium; redlines + `[EXTERNAL]`/`[INTERNAL]` split | ✅ `completed` (12.4 KB) |
| 2 | Single M&A rep clause, buyer, **strict**, strong leverage | + `load_policy`(review-mode) | ✅ SPA; strict; 3× Critical; cites lenses + fallback ladder | ✅ `completed` |
| 3 | Mutual NDA, **loose/quick** | grounding + `load_policy`(review-mode, contract-families) | ✅ NDA; loose; std-of-care floor / survival / assignment flagged | ✅ `completed` |
| 4 | Korean 공급계약 지체상금 clause, supplier side | grounding + `load_policy`(review-mode) | ✅ answers in Korean; cites 민법 §398, 약관규제법 §6 | ✅ `completed` (Korean) |
| 5 | Out-of-scope ("best pizza topping + a haiku") | none | ✅ declines, no tool call | ✅ declines |
| 6 | Ambiguous ("review my contract", no text) | none | ✅ asks one clarifying question | ✅ asks one question |

Independently checked: the agent card publishes a real `did:bindu:…` under
`capabilities.extensions[].uri`; `/health` is `healthy` with `task_manager_running: true`;
one server instance served every A2A call and stayed responsive throughout (the handler
`await`s agno, so a minute-long review doesn't block `/health` or other requests).

## Test plan for review

```bash
uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -r examples/agno-bindu/requirements.txt   # no upstream package needed — skills are read in place
cp examples/agno-bindu/.env.example examples/agno-bindu/.env   # then set OPENROUTER_API_KEY

# one-shot CLI:
uv run python examples/agno-bindu/cli.py "Review this NDA in loose mode: 'Either party may assign without consent.'"

# A2A service:
uv run python examples/agno-bindu/bindu_agent.py
curl -s localhost:3773/.well-known/agent.json | jq '.capabilities.extensions[].uri'   # did:bindu:…
curl -s localhost:3773/health | jq '{health, task_manager_running}'
# then one message/send + tasks/get — full snippet in examples/agno-bindu/README.md
```

## A note to the maintainers

This is additive, not a request for changes to your project. If you'd prefer a different
shape — moving the example to a separate repo under the Bindu org, different README
pointers, loading a different subset of skills, or dropping the Korean pointer — we're glad
to adjust. The example deliberately exposes only your text-native review skills; the full
local pipeline (tracked-change DOCX, house-library retrieval, ingestion, pipeline-state)
remains your application's domain, and we point readers to it as the real thing. Thank you
for open-sourcing this.

author: brilliantwasp
body:
Raises main/gobjwork from 93.64% to 93.86%.

## Per-function gains
- **CalcStatus (CCaravanWork)**: 90.33% -> 92.17%. Flattened the temp-stat-buff dispatch (0x17D/0x180/0x183/0x185 range) into a consecutive comparison ladder followed by labeled bodies via goto, matching the target's block emission order (R14). mwcc was inlining each range test before its body; the target emits the full ladder up front then the str/def/mag bodies.
- **GetMagicCharge**: 86.99% -> 87.41%. Gave the second command-list scan loop its own counter variable instead of reusing the shared `scanCount`; this let mwcc fuse the loop guard with the bdnz CTR loop, dropping a redundant zero-check and matching the target's bdnz.
- **SearchRomLetterWork**: 89.79% -> 89.88%. Dropped the redundant `if (maxResults > 0)` guard around the result-clearing for-loop, removing extra setup instructions and matching the target's unrolled zero-loop induction.

## Plausibility
All changes are ordinary source-level restructurings (loop-counter scoping, removing a redundant guard, expressing a range dispatch as a labeled ladder). No hardcoded addresses, fake symbols, pointer-offset tricks, or layout hacks.

## Blocker
The dominant remaining gap is a callee-saved register-COUNT wall: SearchRomLetterWork's target saves r20-r31 (12 regs) while ours saves r22-r31 (10) — the target promotes the zero-loop induction variables to the two extra low callee-saved registers, shifting nearly every register number. GetCmdListItemName/DelCmdListAndItem/GetNextCmdListIdx/FindItem are blocked by mwcc strength-reduction and register-coloring order (the shared command-list scan-loop idiom emits one extra count-zero check the target elides; FindItem folds a running index into base+constant). These resisted 10+ targeted variants (do-while, for, fresh vars, type changes, index-bound loops) and signedness permutation found no wins.

## Problem

Cluster secrets (API keys, BYOC credentials) were manually created and not tracked anywhere. Rebuilding a cluster from scratch requires knowing which secrets exist and their values.

## Solution

- Sealed-secrets controller deployed via ArgoCD on both clusters
- Existing secrets sealed with `kubeseal` and committed to `clusters/<name>/sealed-secrets/`
- Bootstrap script and deploy workflow apply SealedSecret manifests

Sealed secrets per cluster:
- **dev-decoy**: `speedscale-apikey`
- **staging-decoy**: `speedscale-apikey`, `byoc-fluentbit-gcs`, `byoc-fluentbit-s3`, `byoc-azureblob`

To seal a new secret: `kubectl get secret <name> -n <ns> -o yaml | kubeseal --cert <cert.pem> --format yaml`

- [x] Existing secrets sealed and committed

body:
## Why

Closes the workflow gap from **leadbay/product#3703** — reps prospecting through Claude hit companies with no suggested contacts and switched to Attio + Full Enrich because there was no way to manage contacts in-conversation.

## What's in this PR

Five new composite write tools for full contact management on a company, without leaving the chat — each a thin wrapper over the exact endpoint the Leadbay web UI uses:

| Tool | Endpoint | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `leadbay_add_contact` | `POST /leads/{id}/contacts` | Create a contact (name + optional LinkedIn / title / email / phone) |
| `leadbay_update_contact` | `POST /contacts/{id}/update` | Edit a contact in place |
| `leadbay_remove_contact` | `POST /contacts/{id}/archive` | Remove (archive) a contact |
| `leadbay_pin_contact` | `POST /contacts/{id}/pin` | Mark a contact as priority |
| `leadbay_unpin_contact` | `POST /contacts/{id}/unpin` | Clear the pin |

Plus routing (triggers + cross-routing anti-triggers, reciprocal anti-trigger from `research_lead_by_id`), WORKFLOWS rows #15–#19 + eval contracts, and unit tests per tool.

## Design notes (learned from live probing through Desktop)

- **Add uses the direct endpoint, not the import pipeline.** The first cut routed add through `leadbay_import_and_qualify` (CONTACT_* import fields), but `POST /imports` returns **401 on the test account** (surfaced misleadingly as "LEADBAY_TOKEN is no longer valid"). The direct `POST /leads/{id}/contacts` works with the same token, so all tools wrap the direct `/contacts` endpoints.
- **Update body shape:** `POST /contacts/{id}/update` requires a **snake_case** body that **includes `first_name` + `last_name`** (validates the full identity; 400 "invalid contact" on a partial body, 400 "JSON deserialization error" on camelCase). The tool requires first/last name and asks the agent to pass current values for unchanged fields.

## Verification

- **Live, through Desktop's exact `bin.js` + token:** full cycle add → update (title OLD → SVP Engineering, same id, edited in place) → pin → unpin → remove; company ends at 0 contacts. Test data cleaned up.
- **Suite green:** core 332/332, promptforge 16/16, mcp 366/366 (routing-block, workflows, composite-file-names, _triggered_by-mandate, tool-description-source audits all pass).

body:
Adds `G_F_/v3/` containing `rk_builder_adapt_wkb_vfinal.py`.

This is the optimized bounce-side coupled-channel RK Green's-function builder. The key change vs. the previous version: instead of building the dense `(nr, nr, 2, 2)` `G_rk` tensor with an `O(nr^2)` double loop and writing ~128 MB per slice, it computes only the diagonal trace that the downstream `gbar` consumer actually reads:

```python
trace_diag = np.einsum('kib,bc,kic->k', f_plus, omega_inv, f_minus)
```

- **Bit-identical** to the old `np.trace(G_rk[k,k])` diagonal (~1.8e-15).
- **~16-33x faster** per build (dense build ~17 s -> einsum ~0.3 ms).
- Drops the 128 MB per-slice dense-tensor I/O.

## What

Fixes `MISSING_MESSAGE: Could not resolve 'templates.list.draftUntitled'` crashing the templates list page.

## Root cause

`client.tsx:396` rendered a draft template's title with `t("draftUntitled")`, where `t` is bound to the **`templates.list`** namespace — so it resolved to the nonexistent `templates.list.draftUntitled`. The key actually lives at **`templates.columns.draftUntitled`** (it already exists in both en/es), which is the `columnsT` namespace — and its sibling fallback `columnsT("untitled")` on the very same line already used it correctly. `columns.tsx` was unaffected (its `t` is bound to `templates.columns`).

## Fix

One line — draft titles now resolve `draftUntitled` via `columnsT`, matching `untitled`:

```diff
- (row.__isDraft ? t("draftUntitled") : columnsT("untitled"));
+ (row.__isDraft ? columnsT("draftUntitled") : columnsT("untitled"));
```

No message files changed (the keys already exist in `templates.columns` for en + es).

## Add a TypeScript Clean Architecture starter

This adds `ts/encore-clean-arch-starter` — a small Encore.ts service (greet,
list, version, health) built as a complete, textbook **Clean Architecture**
reference. The behavior is intentionally simple; the value is the structure and
the fact that the architecture is enforced automatically.

### What it demonstrates

- **Real Encore primitives**, not stubs:
  - `SQLDatabase` (Postgres) + a migration, behind a repository that implements a domain port.
  - Pub/Sub `Topic` + `Subscription`: the create-greeting flow publishes a domain event that a subscription consumes.
- **Clean Architecture, end to end** — a pure domain (entities, value objects, a domain service, typed domain errors, domain events, a repository port), application use-cases (command + query) depending only on ports, infrastructure adapters, thin Encore handlers with HTTP error mapping, and a single composition root that wires the adapters.
- **The dependency rule is enforced, not just documented.** It ships an `arch-contract.yaml` ([ArchContract](https://www.npmjs.com/package/arch-contract)) wired to `npm run arch:check` that fails the build on any drift: inward-only layer dependencies, every file assigned to a layer, ports are interfaces, use-cases are `*UseCase` classes with `execute()`, the domain imports no framework/runtime, and handlers never instantiate adapters.
- **Framework-free unit tests** for the domain and use-cases (they run with no database and no Encore runtime).

author: yrashk
body:
## Summary

- replace build-time GitHub release downloads with optional `tidesdb-src-vX-Y-Z` source archive crates
- extend `scripts/sync-versions.py` to survey crates.io state, prepare source crates, dry-run checks, and require explicit upload
- generate CI-only local source crate patches so PRs can test unpublished source crates
- disable optional compression codecs for source-built TidesDB v9.3.4+ so default source builds no longer need zstd/lz4/snappy installed
- bump the Rust crate to `0.10.0` and ignore Python cache artifacts

## Architecture

Each TidesDB C release now maps to a small source crate named after the release, for example `tidesdb-src-v9-3-5`. That crate owns the vendored upstream archive under `vendor/` and exposes a single `archive_path()` function. The main `tidesdb` crate keeps the existing version feature shape, but every `vX_Y_Z` feature now enables the matching optional build-dependency.

`build.rs` no longer reaches out to GitHub during builds. It selects the enabled source crate at compile time with a generated `cfg_if!` ladder, reads the archive path from that dependency, extracts it into `OUT_DIR`, and then continues with the existing CMake build flow. If multiple version features are enabled, the selection order matches the previous highest-version behavior.

For TidesDB v9.3.4 and newer, the source build passes `TIDESDB_WITH_SNAPPY=OFF`, `TIDESDB_WITH_LZ4=OFF`, and `TIDESDB_WITH_ZSTD=OFF`. Those upstream releases can compile with no optional compression backends, so source builds do not need those system packages unless we later add an explicit opt-in for compression-enabled vendored builds.

`scripts/sync-versions.py` is the control plane for keeping this synchronized. It fetches upstream TidesDB releases, reads the current Rust feature set, surveys crates.io for matching source crates, compares expected metadata and vendored archive size/hash, and then prints a plan. Missing crates are prepared at `0.1.0`; changed crates get a patch bump. Publishing remains explicit via `--publish`; normal non-dry-run flows only run `cargo publish --dry-run` for prepared source crates.

The script still updates the root `Cargo.toml`, generated `build.rs` archive selector, and CI default when requested, so version feature sync and source crate publishing are not separate workflows.

For PR CI, the same script has a local patch mode. CI prepares path crates for every current `tidesdb-src-*` dependency and writes a temporary `.cargo/config.toml` with `[patch.crates-io]` entries. Cargo can then resolve the optional source dependencies even before those crates are published. By default, the local patch mode only downloads the default version archive, so CI does not multiply GitHub archive downloads across every historical version just to satisfy dependency resolution.

## Why

The current build downloads TidesDB C release archives from GitHub inside `build.rs`. That makes ordinary Cargo builds depend on network access, GitHub availability, API/rate-limit behavior, and whatever local environment happens to be running the build script. Moving the archives into crates.io source crates makes the C source a normal Cargo dependency instead.

That gives downstream users no-network builds once Cargo has resolved and fetched dependencies, which matters for CI caches, offline builds, sandboxed package builds, and reproducible release pipelines. It also puts archive integrity under Cargo's package checksum model instead of ad hoc build-script downloading.

This should also improve incremental build behavior. Cargo can cache the source archive crate like any other dependency, and `build.rs` no longer has to perform network work or manage downloaded tarballs itself. Version changes become dependency graph changes, while rebuilding the same selected TidesDB version can reuse Cargo's existing cache path.

The source crates also give us a place to ship hotfixes to archive packaging metadata without changing the main binding crate or requiring users to hit GitHub during their build. The main crate pins to the source-crate compatibility line, and the sync script detects metadata/archive drift so updates are visible before publishing.

Disabling optional compression in the vendored source path also narrows the default native dependency surface. CI and downstream users still need the normal compiler/CMake toolchain, and objectstore builds still need curl/OpenSSL, but default source builds for current TidesDB no longer require separate codec development packages.

## Validation

- `python3 -m py_compile scripts/sync-versions.py`
- `rustfmt --check build.rs`
- `git diff --check`
- `./scripts/sync-versions.py --prepare-local-patches /private/tmp/tidesdb-local-patches --write-cargo-patch-config /private/tmp/tidesdb-cargo-home/config.toml --versions current --yes`
- `CARGO_HOME=/private/tmp/tidesdb-cargo-home cargo metadata --format-version=1`
- `CARGO_HOME=/private/tmp/tidesdb-cargo-home cargo check`
- `CARGO_HOME=/private/tmp/tidesdb-cargo-home cargo test --lib -- --test-threads=1`
- verified active v9.3.5 CMake cache has `TIDESDB_WITH_SNAPPY`, `TIDESDB_WITH_LZ4`, and `TIDESDB_WITH_ZSTD` set to `OFF`
- `./scripts/sync-versions.py --dry-run --source-crates-only --versions 9.3.5 --default-version 9.3.5 --publish-versions selected --yes`
- `./scripts/sync-versions.py --dry-run --versions all --default-version 9.3.5 --publish-versions none --yes`
- `cargo check --no-default-features --features v9_2_0,v9_3_5` with local source crate patches

**Option B** (keep filter sticky, add explicit clear affordance). Option A (persisting a completed-scope marker) would require a new settings field and cross-device sync consideration. author: saravananravi08
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in `inline_images` / `inlineImages` feature that extracts embedded PDF images, encodes them as PNG base64, and inserts them into parsed page text as markdown data URI images:

```md
![](data:image/png;base64,...)
```

This allows consumers to render parsed text and embedded images together from the returned text stream, while keeping the existing default behavior unchanged.

## Why this is useful

LiteParse currently does a strong job extracting text and coordinates, but many real-world PDFs contain important non-text content that gets lost in text-only output, such as:

- signatures, seals, stamps, and letterheads
- charts, diagrams, screenshots, and figures
- QR codes, barcodes, logos, and product images
- form attachments or image snippets embedded inside a mostly text-based PDF

Inlining images as markdown data URIs makes the parse result self-contained and directly renderable by downstream applications without needing separate image files, storage, or hosting.

## Where this helps

- **Web app document preview:** render `result.text` as markdown and show both text and images in order.
- **RAG / LLM ingestion:** preserve visual context that may be important for document understanding.
- **Invoice, form, and report parsing:** keep signatures, stamps, charts, product photos, QR codes, and similar embedded assets near surrounding text.
- **Markdown export:** save parsed output as one `.md` document with embedded images.
- **Offline/browser workflows:** avoid external image URLs because the image bytes are included directly in the parse result.

The feature also exposes structured image metadata on pages, so consumers can either use the inline markdown text or use coordinates/base64 for custom rendering.

## What changed

- Added embedded image extraction/rendering via PDFium image objects.
- Added `ImageItem` metadata on parsed pages.
- Added inline image placeholders before grid projection and replacement after projection.
- Ensured inline image markdown lines are left-trimmed so they are not treated as indented markdown/code blocks.
- Added `inline_images` / `inlineImages` config support across:
  - Rust core + CLI
  - Node/NAPI bindings + CLI
  - Python bindings + CLI
  - WASM bindings
- Added structured image output in JSON/bindings when inline images are enabled.
- Added implementation docs for inline base64 images and WASM OCR memory-safe rendering.

## Usage

Rust CLI:

```bash
lit parse document.pdf --inline-images
```

Node:

```ts
const parser = new LiteParse({ inlineImages: true });
const result = await parser.parse("document.pdf");
```

Python:

```py
parser = LiteParse(inline_images=True)
result = parser.parse("document.pdf")
```

## Notes

This feature is disabled by default because embedded base64 images can significantly increase output size and memory usage.

## Validation

Ran successfully:

```bash
cargo fmt
cargo check -p liteparse -p liteparse-napi -p liteparse-python --all-targets
cargo check -p liteparse-wasm
npm --prefix packages/node run build:ts
cargo test -p liteparse --lib
cargo test -p liteparse image_merge --lib
```

## Summary
- **`prefix + I`** toggles a split pane that browses every image the Claude session in the current pane has touched (Read / Write / MCP screenshots).
- A **PostToolUse hook** (`claude-images-update`) appends image paths to a per-pane JSONL manifest under `$CLAUDE_STATUS_DIR/images/<pane>.jsonl` — a sibling of the existing `panes/`/`issues/` state, keyed by `$TMUX_PANE`, deduped by `(path,mtime)`.
- The viewer is a **full-pane keyboard navigator** (n/p/digit/q), not fzf and not a popup.
- **Terminal-aware render ladder**: `kitten icat --unicode-placeholder` (kitty/ghostty) → `chafa -f kitty` (kitty, no kitten) → `chafa -f sixel` (foot/wezterm/…) → `chafa -f symbols` (universal floor — never a blank pane).

author: sbriggssjc
body:
## Summary

Fixes a critical starvation bug in the intake rematch loop where the scan never reached eligible rows, and introduces a new `needs_address` flagging system to surface address-less items with deal signal for human triage instead of silently re-skipping them forever.

## Key Changes

- **Reverse fetch order** (`created_at.desc` → newest-first): The old `created_at.asc` filled every tick's 400-row window with the oldest cooldown'd and dead rows, starving the newest (and rematch-eligible) items. Fetching newest-first up to the PostgREST 1000-row cap ensures the eligible tail is always in-page.

- **Eligibility-first sorting**: After fetch, sort rows into three tiers (address-bearing + cooldown-expired → cooldown'd → address-less) and process tier-0 first. Within each tier, never-rematched rows come first, then oldest rematch (closest to cooldown expiry), then oldest created_at. This ensures real rematches happen every tick instead of the budget being spent re-grinding the same front-of-queue dead rows.

- **Replace `skipped_no_address` with two new counters**:
  - `flagged_needs_address`: rows with deal signal but no address, flagged once via `needs_address: true` in the payload and surfaced in the inbox for human address entry
  - `needs_address_pending`: already-flagged rows (not re-written or re-skipped)
  - `skipped_no_address`: retired (stays 0)

- **Add `REMATCH_FETCH_CAP` env**: Allows tuning the fetch limit independently of `limit * 4` for future optimization.

## Implementation Details

- The `tierOf()` helper classifies rows by address presence and cooldown status; the sort comparator uses tier, rematch history, and created_at for deterministic ordering.
- Address-less rows with deal signal are flagged exactly once via a PATCH to `raw_payload.needs_address = true`, then skipped on subsequent ticks (counted as `needs_address_pending`).
- The per-tick `processed >= limit` break only increments on tier-0 rows, so tier-1/2 processing is bounded and doesn't consume the budget once tier-0 pressure drops.
- Dry-run mode respects the flag write guard (no PATCH on dryRun).

body:
Closes #220.

## Rule
While the salon is within its **open hours** ("on shift"), a nail tech who isn't clocked in cannot run checkouts or edit their calendar. **Off shift** (salon closed) they edit freely. **Admins exempt.** Decisions: on-shift = salon open hours (`settings.storeHours`); checkout requires *every credited tech* clocked in; admins exempt.

## Changes (web + mobile parity)
- **Shared helpers** `src/lib/shiftGate.js` + `mobile/src/lib/shiftGate.js` — `isSalonOpenNow`, `isEntryClockedIn` (on-break still counts; flat snapshot fallback), `clockedInNameSet`, `offClockTechNames`, `attendanceKey`. **20 unit tests.**
- **Checkout** — web `CheckoutModal.complete()` + mobile `CheckoutScreen` (cash / card / send-to-front-desk all gated; mobile card button disabled when blocked so money is never captured first). Walk-in retail (no service techs) is not gated.
- **Calendar** — web `ScheduleAdmin.handleSave()`; mobile `ScheduleScreen` create/edit `save()` + both drag-to-reschedule handlers. Only the editing tech is gated; admins/schedulers/non-techs pass.
- **No-PIN clock-in fix** — both kiosks (`TimeClockKiosk`, `ClockKioskScreen`) disable tiles for techs without a PIN and show "No PIN set — ask an admin" instead of opening a keypad that could only fail. Server already rejected no-PIN since #163; this closes the UI gap + adds defense-in-depth.

All gates fail **open** if attendance can't be read (a nudge, not a hard lock at the register).

## Not in scope (documented follow-ups)
- **Not server-enforced** — workflow guard, not a data-confidentiality boundary (bypass only creates writes the tech can already make; clock-in stays PIN-enforced). Firestore-rule enforcement deferred.
- 'On shift' = salon open hours, not per-tech working hours.
- #219 (reassign no-preference online bookings to first-clocked-in tech) builds on this attendance signal.

author: jgranstrom
body:
Remote caching of all jars was [disabled some time ago](https://github.com/pantsbuild/pants/pull/21290) due to it being slower to fetch from cache than re-executing the process to produce the jar. However, this is not the case if you have a fast remote cache on an internal network in a CI environment, especially when executing a high volume of these tasks. It turns into a bit of a fork bomb on a fully remotely cached run as it has to spawn a ton of tiny processes to construct these jars.

These changes allow enabling remote cache for the intermediate jars, which are both generally small and can be numerous. In my case we have over 1000 compile targets that are going through these processes, and the cost of churning them greatly outweighs going to the remote cache in CI.

This PR:
- Adds the `[jvm].intermediate_jars_remote_cache` option to enable remote cache of intermediate and intermediate-stripped jars.
- Adds the `[jvm].intermediate_jars_remote_cache_speculation_delay` to configure a delay before spawning these micro-processes.

Here's some benchmarks on 1000+ targets simulating a CI environment where these would be cached remotely but not locally.

| Core Metric | Fully Cached Run | Shallow Incremental Change | Large Cascading Change |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Wall-Clock Time** | 83s → **11s** `(-87%)` | 81s → **17s** `(-79%)` | 208s → **61s** `(-71%)` |
| **User CPU Time** | 201s → **10s** `(-95%)` | 205s → **11s** `(-95%)` | 1,442s → **14s** `(-99%)` |
| **Kernel CPU Time**| 164s → **7s** `(-95%)` | 160s → **9s** `(-94%)` | 267s → **51s** `(-81%)` |
| **Local OS Forks** | 2,449 → **4** `(-100%)` | 2,451 → **11** `(-100%)` | 2,981 → **540** `(-82%)` |
| **Context Switches** | 2,520,167 → **671,455** `(-73%)` | 2,522,822 → **715,700** `(-72%)` | 6,038,084 → **944,366** `(-84%)` |
| **Page Reclaims** | 15,488,957 → **576,400** `(-96%)` | 15,511,196 → **593,848** `(-96%)` | 20,572,938 → **670,674** `(-97%)` |
| **Max RSS Memory** | 2,860 MB → **2,510 MB** `(-12%)` | 2,753 MB → **2,180 MB** `(-21%)` | 2,534 MB → **2,280 MB** `(-10%)` |

author: zeus-deus
body:
Closes #72.

## Summary
The terminal pane rendered with xterm.js's slower DOM renderer. `@xterm/addon-webgl` was already a dependency but **never loaded**. This loads it after `term.open()` to offload glyph rasterization to the GPU — the recommended renderer for the fast, long-running, high-output agent sessions Codemux streams — with a clean fallback to the DOM renderer.

## Changes (`src/components/terminal/TerminalPane.tsx`)
- Import `WebglAddon` and load it **after** `term.open(containerEl)` (the addon needs the opened terminal's DOM element).
- Register the required `onContextLoss` handler that disposes the addon so xterm falls back to the DOM renderer (rather than rendering a blank pane) when the GPU drops the canvas context.
- Wrap construction/`loadAddon` in try/catch so an environment without WebGL2 support falls back to the DOM renderer instead of throwing.
- Track `webglAddonRef` (matching the existing `fitAddonRef`/`serializeAddonRef` pattern) and dispose it on pane unmount so the GPU context/canvas is released (no leak); the wrapped dispose unregisters it from xterm's addon manager so `term.dispose()` won't double-dispose.

Also updates `docs/features/terminal.md` to reflect WebGL rendering + DOM fallback.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Terminal uses the WebGL renderer when available — verified: a live `webgl2` canvas + texture-atlas canvas, `.xterm-rows` absent (= GPU rendering, not DOM).
- [x] On WebGL context loss the terminal keeps working (DOM fallback) — no blank pane: forced `WEBGL_lose_context`, canvases removed, `.xterm-rows` reappeared, content preserved.
- [x] No regressions in selection/copy/paste, theming (`buildThemeFromCSS`), cursor, or fit/resize — viewport resize re-fit the WebGL canvas; theming/cursor render correctly on both paths.
- [x] Addon disposed on pane unmount (no leak).

## Verification
- `npm run check` (tsc) — clean
- `npm run test` (vitest) — 1818 passed
- `cargo check` — compiles
- Manual (dev browser): fresh mount renders via a live WebGL2 canvas; `WEBGL_lose_context` swaps to the DOM renderer with content preserved; resize/fit and theming unaffected; console clean (no fallback warning).

Note: two `cargo test` failures (`resolve_binary_finds_native_binary_from_project_root`, `project_codemux_entry_is_filtered_out`) are pre-existing and environment-specific (host has a system-wide `/usr/bin/agent-browser`; host MCP config), unrelated to this frontend-only change.

author: gladly-hyphenated-21
body:
The following summary of changes was generated with the assistance of Claude. 

The issue reported two display bugs on a hand-graded assignment where the active (graded) submission was an older one than the latest. Both turned out to be independent bugs that happened to surface together. The underlying grade was correct; two views misrepresented it.

Bug #1 — Assignments tab showed the wrong submission (81.67/90 instead of 87.67/100)
Root cause: The Postgres RPC get_assignments_for_student_dashboard chose each student's submission with ORDER BY created_at DESC — i.e. the most recent one — and never consulted submissions.is_active. When staff activate an older submission for grading, the latest submission is autograder-only and inactive, so the dashboard surfaced its score and incomplete denominator instead of the active, hand-graded submission's released total. Every other view in the app (gradebook, submissions list, RLS) keys off is_active, so the dashboard was the lone outlier — exactly the inconsistency the reporter spotted.

Fix: New migration 20260608000000_dashboard_rpc_prefer_active_submission.sql — a CREATE OR REPLACE that prefers is_active = true before created_at DESC in both submission-selection LATERALs and the chosen_submission tiebreak, falling back to latest-by-date when nothing is active. Everything else (auth gate, release gate, all other CTEs, the signature) is byte-identical to the prior version.

Why this way: It matches the rest of the codebase's "the active submission is the one that counts" convention, and is a minimal, surgical change to a known-good function rather than a rewrite.

Bug #2 — "Hand grading 15 / 9" (points earned exceeded points possible)
Root cause: In HandGradingSection.tsx, the per-criterion earned formula handled only additive and non-additive criteria. A deduction-only criterion (whose max is 0) fell through to the non-additive branch max(total_points − applied, 0), which credited positive points — e.g. "Code Complexity" with a −1 deduction showed 2 instead of −1. Summed across several deduction-only criteria, earned ballooned above the max, yielding the nonsensical "15 / 9". The backend recompute and the grader-facing sidebar both handle all three branches; this student-facing view (added mid-semester) was the only place missing the deduction-only case.

Fix:

Added earnedPointsForCriterion to lib/rubric/points.ts, mirroring all three backend scoring branches — deduction-only → max(−applied, −total_points) — co-located with the existing maxPointsForCriterion.
HandGradingSection.tsx now calls the helper instead of the inline 2-branch formula.
Added unit tests in points.test.ts covering all three branches plus the exact issue case.
Why this way: Extracting a pure helper makes the logic unit-testable and keeps the frontend's per-criterion scoring in one place that demonstrably matches the backend, so the two can't silently drift again.

How it was verified
Bug #1 — built the exact scenario in the live local DB (active older #14 + newer inactive #15) in a rolled-back transaction and called the real RPC: it returned the active #14 → 87.67/100, where the old ordering returned #15 → 50/90.
Bug #2 — unit tests (20 passing) plus a seeded hand-graded submission in the UI that rendered "6 / 9" (the correct +6 hand grading) where the old code produced "15 / 9". (That UI seed data has since been removed.)
Final state: tsc clean, eslint clean, tests green.

Note: two tests are still failing, but those appear to have been not working for a while? Did get the docker images working and verified the fix on the dev site.

author: josephfarina
body:
## The gap

Finding the right thing in XDS today means four separate calls and manual scanning: `xds component --list`, `xds hook --list`, `xds docs`, `xds template --list`. There is no single "I'm looking for X" entry point. `discover` only finds *external packages*, not a content search across what's already in the system. This is the biggest workflow gap for both humans and AI agents.

## What this adds

A new flagship command — `xds search <query>` — that returns one ranked, typed result set spanning **all four content domains**: components, hooks, docs topics, and templates (page + block). Each result is tagged with its domain and carries enough to act on it (description + the follow-up command + import path where relevant).

```
$ xds search button

Results for "button" (20):

  [component]  Button
               Button triggers an action when clicked. Use it for form submissions…
               → xds component Button

  [component]  IconButton
               A button that shows only an icon with no visible text…
               → xds component IconButton

  [hook]       useClickableContainer
               Makes a container element clickable while preserving nested interactive…
               → xds hook useClickableContainer

  [template]   Banner — Collapsible
               Combine an action button, dismiss control, and expandable detail area…
               → xds template BannerCollapsibleContent
```

## Scoring

Keyword + fuzzy ranking (deliberately **not** semantic/embeddings — that's a future follow-up). Same signal weighting as the existing component fuzzy resolver in `lib/string-utils.mjs`, so name and keyword matches always outrank incidental prose mentions, with Levenshtein fuzziness for typos:

| Score | Signal |
| ----- | ------ |
| 100 | exact name match |
| 90 | exact keyword match |
| 80 | name distance 1 |
| 70 | keyword substring / distance 1 |
| 60 | name substring (≥4 chars, ≥50% coverage) |
| 50 | description / doc prose mentions the term |
| 40 | name distance 2 |
| 30 | keyword distance 2 |
| 20 | name distance 3 |

`xds search buton` still finds `Button` (distance 1).

## Options

- `--type <component|hook|doc|template>` — restrict to one domain
- `--limit <n>` — cap results (default 20)
- `--detail` — include import path + match reason/score
- `--json` — typed envelope

## JSON envelope

```json
{ "apiVersion": 1, "type": "search", "data": { "query": "button", "results": [
  { "domain": "component", "name": "Button", "score": 100, "reason": "exact name",
    "description": "Button triggers an action…", "import": "@xds/core/Button",
    "command": "xds component Button" }
] } }
```

A no-match query is a **valid, successful** outcome: clean message, empty `results`, **exit 0** (per the exit-code policy in `cli-error.mjs` — search-with-no-results is success, not failure). Invalid `--type`/`--limit` and an empty query exit 1.

## Design notes

- New `api/search.mjs` exporting `search(query, options)` — available programmatically too, consistent with `component`/`hook`/`docs`/`template`. Exported from `@xds/cli/api`.
- New `commands/search.mjs`, registered in `index.mjs` and added to `JSON_SUPPORTED`.
- **Reuses existing discovery + loader modules** rather than reinventing: `component-discovery`, `hook-discovery`, the docs topic enumeration, and the `template` discovery API. The scoring helper mirrors `searchComponents` in `string-utils.mjs`.
- Types: new `types/search.d.ts` (`SearchResponse`, `SearchResultEntry`), wired into `base.d.ts` union, `api.d.ts`, and `index.d.ts`. `json-api` typecheck passes.

## Verification

- `vitest run packages/cli` — **819 passed** (22 new in `search.test.mjs`: ranking, cross-domain, `--type`/`--limit` filters, typo tolerance, empty results + exit 0, `--json` envelope, CLI exit codes).
- API↔CLI parity (`api-cli-parity-test.mjs`) — **303/303 pass**, including 5 new `search` parity cases.
- `tsc --project tsconfig.json-api.json` — clean.

author: mandeepashf-collab
body:
## Why

The existential risk for a shared comms platform: one tenant's spam/bounces get the **shared** Resend/carrier reputation blacklisted, taking every tenant down. This adds the missing layer — real-time bounce/complaint monitoring that **auto-pauses a bad tenant** before a provider acts.

## What

- **mig 193 `reputation_events`** — per-tenant delivered/bounced/complained log (service-write, org-read).
- **`lib/compliance/reputation.ts`**:
  - `decideReputationAction(counts)` — pure, unit-tested thresholding.
  - `recordReputationEvent` / `evaluateOrgChannel` / `applyReputationGuard`.
  - **Spam complaints = nuclear signal**: ≥3 in 24h (any volume) or ≥0.3% at volume → quarantine. **Extreme bounce rate**: ≥15% with n≥30 → quarantine. Lighter signals → warn + owner email. Min-sample guards so an honest small batch with a couple dead scraped addresses is **never** nuked.
- **Resend webhook** (`/api/webhooks/resend`):
  - Accepts **either** account's signing secret — cold outreach sends from a *separate* Resend account (`RESEND_COLD_WEBHOOK_SECRET`).
  - Resolves org from `messages` **or** `email_outreach_sends` (cold sends), so attribution + reputation work for both paths.
  - Records a reputation event on every delivery event; runs the guard on bounce/complaint.
  - Quarantine uses the existing `compliance_quarantine` whole-org path → `is_org_quarantined` true → **all outbound guards already block**. Owner gets an alert email; lift via Settings → Compliance.

This is layer 4 ("reputation auto-throttle") of the anti-abuse strategy — the one gap the platform didn't have. Identity/KYC, AUP, consent/opt-out, quarantine tooling, per-org domains, and audit already exist.

## Config needed
- `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (main account) + `RESEND_COLD_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (cold account).
- Point **both** Resend accounts' webhooks at `/api/webhooks/resend` with `email.delivered` / `email.bounced` / `email.complained` enabled.

author: panyam
body:
## What changes

\`make demo-up\` and \`make -C docker up\` can now run concurrently — the event-server + push-server emit OTel traces via OTLP/gRPC to the shared LGTM stack at \`docker/observability/\`. Spans land in Grafana (http://localhost:3000) → Explore → Tempo under service names \`whole-enchilada-event-server\` and \`whole-enchilada-push-server\`.

\`EXPORTER=auto\` (compose default) means **best-effort OTLP with silent Noop fallback** — \`make demo-up\` works whether the observability stack is up or not. Override to \`EXPORTER=otlp\` to fail loudly when the collector is missing.

## Reviewer's guide

1. \`examples/events/whole-enchilada/event-server/main.go\` — adopts the canonical \`common.RegisterTelemetryFlags\` + \`commonotel.SetupTelemetry\` pattern already used by examples/auth / tasks / mrtr / elicitation / otel/stdout. Passes the TracerProvider to \`server.WithTracerProvider\` so SEP-414 spans flow through.
2. \`examples/events/whole-enchilada/push-server/main.go\` — same pattern; no \`WithTracerProvider\` consumer here (push-server doesn't host an MCP server) but \`SetupTelemetry\` still installs the global TP so the eventsclient pusher's outbound HTTP gets instrumented automatically.
3. \`examples/events/whole-enchilada/tools/gen-compose/compose.tmpl\` — new \`mcpkit\` shared network declared with \`name: mcpkit\` (literal, no project prefix). Event-server + push-server attach to it AND \`whole_enchilada\`. Env vars wired: \`EXPORTER\` (default auto) + \`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT\` (default mcpkit-otel-collector:4317).
4. \`docker/observability/docker-compose.yml\` — otel-collector gets attached to the same \`mcpkit\` network alongside its default network. Other LGTM components stay on default — only the collector needs to be reachable from outside this stack.
5. \`examples/events/whole-enchilada/docker-compose.yaml\` — rendered output of the template change.
6. \`examples/events/whole-enchilada/README.md\` — new "Observability (traces in Grafana)" section explaining the two-stack launch order + how to find traces.

Skim or skip: \`go.mod\` / \`go.sum\` boilerplate.

## Decision log

- **Network named \`mcpkit\`** (literal, via \`name: mcpkit\`) — not \`mcpkit-observability\` or similar. Compose normally prefixes networks with the project name; \`name: mcpkit\` makes both stacks resolve the same docker-side network. Keeping it short matches the project's existing naming conventions.

- **EXPORTER=auto as the default** — picks up the existing \`examples/common/otel\` "auto = best-effort OTLP, Noop fallback" mode. Means a fresh \`make demo-up\` without the observability stack running emits zero warnings + zero traces. Operators who want hard failures on missing collector set \`EXPORTER=otlp\` in their shell.

- **Both stacks declare the network** so whichever starts first creates it. \`docker compose down\` on one stack doesn't take the network down while the other is still attached.

- **event-server + push-server only** in this PR — host-side client binaries (poller / webhook / inject) emitting client-side traces is useful but a separate, smaller concern. Deferred.

## Risk / blast radius

- **Affects**: the whole-enchilada demo + docker/observability/. Other examples untouched. No library changes.
- **Tests**: existing event-server e2e suite (13 cases incl. tenant isolation) still green. No new tests in this PR — the wiring is config + plumbing; spans are validated by running both stacks and opening Grafana.
- **Be paranoid about**: the indirect deps explosion in event-server's go.mod from pulling in examples/common (it transitively pulls demokit + charm + bubble-tea via shared example helpers). All dead-code-eliminated from the actual binary — go.mod looks heavier but the docker image isn't.

## Out of scope (deliberately deferred)

- Client-side OTel on poller / webhook / inject — file separately if useful.
- Metrics + log emitters from mcpkit — no surface yet; the Mimir + Loki lanes in the observability stack remain idle per existing posture.
- Custom Grafana dashboards for this demo — \`docker/observability/grafana/provisioning\` auto-discovers data sources; dashboards are explicit and live outside this PR's scope.

author: samaig-araviel
body:
## Summary

Deleting the currently-open conversation from the sidebar menu left the URL pointing at `/conversations/<deleted-id>`. The chat surface emptied — "Good evening" greeting and a fresh prompt input — but the address bar still showed the dead id. A refresh or share-link copy would 404, and the URL state no longer matched what the user was looking at.

Root cause: `Sidebar.jsx:512-514` cleared Redux via `dispatch(createNewChat())` when the deleted conversation was the active one, but `createNewChat` is a pure state reducer (it just nulls `currentChatId` and clears messages). Nothing called `navigate('/')`.

## Change

One file. After the `createNewChat` dispatch inside `confirmDelete`, add `navigate('/')` — gated on the same `currentChatId === chatId` check, so deleting a non-active conversation from the list still doesn't touch the URL.

## Related (not in this PR)

`ConversationsView.jsx` has two delete paths (single at L230 and bulk at L693) that don't check `currentChatId` at all. Because that view lives at `/conversations` (the list page, not a specific chat), there's no URL-stale bug — but if the user deletes the previously-active chat from the list, Redux's `currentChatId` is left pointing at a tombstoned id. Lower-impact than this PR's bug, separate concern, separate change.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 564 relevant tests pass (one pre-existing `authSlice` failure unrelated)
- [ ] Manual: open any conversation, delete it from its sidebar menu — verify URL pops to `/` and the new-chat greeting renders
- [ ] Manual: from inside an open conversation, delete a *different* one in the sidebar list — verify the URL is unchanged and the open conversation stays loaded

author: gandhi56
body:
Relaxes the LoadStoreVectorizer to support merging contiguous loads and stores of different element types (e.g., merging an i32 and an i16 load).

Key changes:
- Remove `ElementSize` from the `EqClassKey`, allowing instructions with different scalar types to be grouped together if they share the same underlying object and address space.
- Calculate the vector element type using the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) of all scalar bitwidths in the chain.
- Update `vectorizeChain` to use shuffles, extracts, and bitcasts to reconstruct original values from the vectorized result (for loads) or prepare values for insertion (for stores).
- Update and add extensive tests covering mixed integer sizes, pointer types, and floating-point mixes. Existing AMDGPU, X86 and NVPTX tests are updated to reflect the more aggressive vectorization.

Resolves #97715

body:
## Subtask 7.0.6 — `/ready` page + sidebar nav entry + count badge

The human mirror of the AI dispatch surface (Story 7.0): a `/ready` page listing the active project's ready-to-start work items, plus the sidebar "Ready" entry and its readiness count badge. Built to the `design/ready/` mockup (7.0.1) with the shipped design system — no new vocabulary.

**Dependencies** (all merged on `main`): 7.0.1 (design ✓), 7.0.2 (`listReady`/`getNextReady` service ✓), 7.0.3 (DTOs ✓). Does **not** depend on the in-flight endpoint subtasks 7.0.4/7.0.5 — the page reads the service directly (the established Server-Component path) and streams more pages via a co-located Server Action.

### What's here
- **Page** (`app/(authed)/ready/page.tsx`, Server Component): resolves the active project (`getActiveProject`), reads `workItemsService.listReady` + `countReady` directly. Header = serif title + neutral count chip + project subtitle + the "What is this?" predicate popover; then the flat dispatch list, or the `EmptyState` (panel 3) when nothing is ready. `?peek=<key>` reuses the **same** `IssueQuickView` peek `/issues` + the board use (notes.html #7) — row click opens the peek, never a full-page nav.
- **`ReadyList`** (client): a new arrangement of shipped primitives — `IssueTypeIcon` (hued), the `PriorityValue` chip, the initial-letter `Avatar` + the dashed-circle unassigned placeholder (mirrors `BoardCard`), and a hover copy button + `Tooltip`. **Scale shape (finding #57):** virtualizes loaded rows via `useRowWindow` (degrades to render-all under no measurable viewport) AND streams subsequent cursor pages on scroll via the `loadMoreReadyAction` Server Action — neither the DOM nor the initial payload grows with the backlog. Whole card opens the peek via a stretched-`::after` button; the copy button is raised above it (`relative z-10`).
- **Sidebar**: new "Ready" entry **between Issues and Boards** (lucide `CirclePlay`, the 7.0.1-locked glyph — `Zap` is the epic issue type). `SidebarItem` gains a presentation-agnostic `badge` slot; `layout.tsx` resolves the count **once** via `workItemsService.countReady` and threads it to the rail **and** the drawer (no double-fetch). Badge hidden at zero; shows `99+` past the cap.
- **`workItemsService.countReady`**: a **bounded** readiness count that reuses the exact `listReady` predicate (so the badge can never disagree with the page) — capped at `READY_COUNT_CAP` (99 → `99+`) and `READY_COUNT_MAX_PAGES`, `hasMore` keeps the cap visible (never a silent truncation). `buttonVariants` is now exported so a `Link` can render as a styled secondary button (the empty-state "View all issues").
- **i18n**: `shell.nav.ready` + a new `ready` namespace (en + zh, catalog parity test green).

### Tokens / a11y
- Colour strictly `--el-*` (issue-type hues, priority `Pill` tones, `--el-muted` badge, `--el-success` toast, `--el-code-bg` chips); shape via element-semantic tokens (`--radius-card/-control/-badge`, `--spacing-control-*/-icon-btn/-kbd-*`, `--height-control`, `--shadow-subtle`). `rounded-full` only on the circular avatar.
- `role="list"`/`listitem`, keyboard-reachable copy button with `aria-label`, `role="status"` toast, single `h1`, predicate not colour-alone.

### Verification
- `pnpm typecheck` ✓ · `pnpm lint` ✓ · `next build` ✓ (`/ready` in the route manifest) · i18n catalog parity ✓ · sidebar/app-layout/tree-nav component tests ✓.
- Live signed-in behaviour (badge live-update, clipboard, peek) is covered by **Subtask 7.0.8** (Playwright E2E) and the Story verification recipe — manual merge mode, so this PR opens ready-for-review and stops.

### Findings
- **#66** logged: the badge count must scan candidates (readiness is a computed predicate, not a stored column); shipped a bounded/capped count + flagged a future materialized `is_ready` flag for an O(1) badge. Also notes the list builds `prodect run <key>` client-side (the list DTO carries no `runCommand`).

`src/backend/tests/matchingService.test.ts` の `runMatchingPipeline 通知配線` で、`shouldNotify=true` のとき `sendInApp` が呼ばれ `notified` にカウントされることを **Side-B / Side-A 両方の note ID** で保証。
