author: ltphongssvn
body:
## Summary
De-flake e2e/docker-api-build-clean.spec.ts. The flaky failure was a WSL2 + Docker Desktop credential-helper fault, NOT an api-code or test-logic problem.

## Root cause
The spec shells out to `docker build -f Dockerfile.api`, whose first step is `load metadata for docker.io/library/node:22-alpine`. On WSL2 + Docker Desktop that step invoked the Windows credential helper (docker-credential-desktop.exe) across the WSL to Windows boundary, which intermittently failed (a vsock race: `<3>WSL ... UtilAcceptVsock:273: accept4 failed 110` then `error getting credentials - err: exit status 1` then `failed to solve`). The build aborted BEFORE running any Dockerfile layer, so none of the gyp/compiler/python guards executed, yet the old assertion `expect(log).toContain('naming to docker.io')` failed, reding the whole suite on an ENVIRONMENTAL fault (Playwright marked it flaky: passed on retry).

## Two-layer fix
1. Environment (host, not in repo): `~/.docker/config.json` had `credsStore: desktop.exe` with EMPTY auths, so every pull — including public Docker Hub base images that need no auth — was routed through the flaky Windows helper. Removed the global credsStore (kept auths) so public docker.io metadata loads no longer invoke it. Verified deterministically: 3 of 3 consecutive `docker build --no-cache -f Dockerfile.api` runs now exit 0 with ZERO `error getting credentials` / `accept4 failed` occurrences. A backup was saved to `~/.docker/config.json.bak-<ts>`.
2. Test hardening (this PR): distinguish `build never started` (an infra fault -> test.skip with the reason) from `build ran and failed` (a real regression -> assert). The spec checks BuildKit stage/export markers (`[builder `, `[stage-2 `, `exporting to image`) to confirm the build reached the Dockerfile layers; only then are the gyp/compiler/python offender assertions meaningful, plus a clean exit and the `naming to docker.io` success marker. A future pre-start infra fault now skips instead of failing, without masking a genuine native-build regression.

## 2026 best practice applied
Public-registry pulls should not depend on a private credential helper (docker/for-win #11261, docker forums); route only registries that need auth via credHelpers, and never red a test suite on a host credential/vsock fault you do not control.

## Verification
- e2e/docker-api-build-clean.spec.ts now PASSES (not skips) on a healthy build after the credsStore removal, exercising the real offender + success-marker assertions.
- Build runs all api layers and reaches `naming to docker.io ... done`.
- Pre-commit hooks (detect-secrets, Lint CI mirror, Typecheck CI mirror) all passed.

## Commits
- b954824 fix(e2e): de-flake docker-api-build-clean (WSL2 credential-helper fault)

Changes the `argocd` manager `packageRule` in `renovate.json` to group Helm chart updates by the Argo CD `Application` file name in `gitops/apps/`, producing one PR per app with a specific title.

## Why

Today all Helm chart updates fall under a single `helm charts` group, yielding generic titles like `chore(deps): update helm charts to v0.33.0` (e.g. #36, #35, #34). The PR title and Dependency Dashboard entries don't reveal which app is being updated until the PR is opened and the file diff is inspected.

Grouping by file name aligns with the repo convention of one app per file in `gitops/apps/` and produces titles like:

- `chore(deps): update vault to v0.33.0`
- `chore(deps): update istio to v1.22.0`
- `chore(deps): update cert-manager to v1.16.0`

Dependency Dashboard items become individualized per app as well, so each app can be triaged independently before accepting.

## Type

- [ ] Terraform / Infrastructure
- [ ] GitOps / Kubernetes
- [x] CI/CD
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Bug fix

## Checklist

- [x] \`pre-commit run --all-files\` passed
- [x] No secrets or sensitive data committed

author: abpai
body:
This PR changes the workflow surface so tutorial writing is its own `/tutorial` plugin, while `/code` keeps only coding workflow subcommands.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Before: /code explain + /code scratch] --> B[After: /tutorial standalone]
  A --> C[/code keeps PR, review, walkthrough, understand, dead-code, dependencies]
  B --> D[Hands-on code-first tutorials]
  C --> E[Focused coding workflows]
```

## Behavior change

- Adds a standalone `tutorial` plugin for hands-on, code-first tutorials.
- Removes the old `explain` and `scratch` workflows from the `/code` umbrella and deletes their command shims/modules.
- Updates `walkthrough` so it starts with mission/prior-knowledge capture, writes `.walkthrough/<topic>/mission.md`, writes `.walkthrough/<topic>/checklist.md`, and records demonstrated mastery separately from coverage.
- Syncs README, docs gallery, marketplace keywords, command wrappers, and related references so deleted `explain`/`scratch` surfaces are not advertised.
- Bumps `visualize` to `1.2.1` because its shared design-system terminology changed from scratch skeleton to import skeleton.

## Why it matters

Tutorial writing is a writing workflow, not a coding PR workflow. Splitting it out makes `/tutorial` discoverable directly and keeps `/code` focused on implementation, review, understanding, and maintenance tasks.

## How it works

`tutorial/` ships paired Claude/Codex manifests plus `tutorial/skills/tutorial/SKILL.md`. The `code` plugin is bumped to `2.1.0`, drops the removed subcommands, and keeps the grouped command-shim model under `code/skills/<workflow>/SKILL.md`.

## Validation

- `bun code/skills/code/scripts/finish-lane.ts --seal --base origin/main` passed at `7e81ad6`.
- `bash scripts/validate-skills.sh` passed: 17 plugins, 16 Codex marketplace entries, 17 skills.
- `bash scripts/validate-npx-install.sh` passed: all 37 SKILL.md files discoverable.
- `bash scripts/test-wrapper-parity.sh` passed.
- `bash scripts/test-gate-before-push.sh` passed.
- Targeted docs parser confirmed 17 static cards: `code` v2.1.0, `tutorial` v1.0.0, and `visualize` v1.2.1.
- Targeted stale-reference searches found no deleted `/code:explain`, `/code:scratch`, old `.walkthrough/<topic>.md`, or `scratch skeleton` references in the changed public surfaces.
- Fresh read-only Codex review found stale docs count drift; fixed in `127bff7`.
- GitHub `Validate PR` checks at `7e81ad6` are all green: `check-version-bump`, `validate-skills`, `wrapper-parity`, and `npx-install`.

author: brittanyjohns
body:
## Summary

- Decouples the **public-URL slug** (`/my/:slug`, `/u/:slug`, `/v/:slug`) from the **communicator login username** (`ChildAccount.username`) at the API contract, and lets the owner edit the slug on the existing `PATCH /api/profiles/:id` endpoint.
- Edits are **rate-limited to once every 7 days** (admin override). The controller returns a structured `slug_locked` / `slug_taken` / `slug_reserved` / `slug_invalid` error so the UI can render field-level messages and a "next change on <date>" hint.
- Adds `GET /api/profiles/check_slug?slug=…` (no auth required) for the wizard / edit-form's live availability check.
- The MySpeak onboarding controller now accepts an optional `params[:slug]` so the new "Pick your link" wizard step can submit a user-chosen slug; it falls back to the existing auto-derived-from-name path when blank.

The frontend half is [brittanyjohns/itty-bitty-frontend#335](https://github.com/brittanyjohns/itty-bitty-frontend/pull/335).

## Why

Today the slug is derived from `Profile.username` at create time and is effectively immutable from the UI. Brittany wanted: (1) the slug editable for any account type without changing the login username they happen to share, (2) a guard against churn on shared public URLs (7-day window), and (3) one consistent error vocabulary across the wizard, the edit endpoint, and the availability check.

## Model changes ([app/models/profile.rb](app/models/profile.rb))

- `SLUG_FORMAT` regex — 3–40 chars, lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphen.
- `RESERVED_SLUGS` list — public-URL route prefixes (`m`/`u`/`v`/`p`/`c`) plus administrative-looking names (`admin`, `api`, `settings`, `dashboard`, `myspeak`, `speakanyway`, …). Pure-numeric slugs are also rejected.
- `Profile.slug_available?(value, except_id:)` — cross-checks `Profile.slug`, `Profile.username`, and `ChildAccount.username`, mirroring the onboarding controller's existing `slug_or_username_taken?` guard.
- `Profile.slug_unavailable_reason(value)` — returns `:format` / `:reserved` / `:taken` / `nil`. Same vocabulary the controllers and the frontend speak.
- `#slug_editable?` / `#slug_editable_at` — 7-day window helpers.
- `before_save :touch_slug_changed_at` — stamps `slug_changed_at` only on edits, never on initial create, so onboarding-generated slugs don't immediately consume the window.
- New format / reserved / numeric validations are gated on `slug_format_validatable?` (new record OR slug changing), so legacy rows with non-conforming slugs are left alone on unrelated saves.

## Migration

`db/migrate/20260608120000_add_slug_changed_at_to_profiles.rb` adds `profiles.slug_changed_at :datetime` and backfills it from `created_at` so every existing row can edit its slug immediately.

## Controller changes

- [`API::ProfilesController#update`](app/controllers/api/profiles_controller.rb) only touches the slug when a non-empty value differs from the current. Runs the 7-day check (admin bypass), then format/reserved/availability, then renders structured 422 errors. Exposes `slug_editable_at` in `api_view` / `safety_view`.
- New `#check_slug` action (skips auth) returns `{ available, reason, slug }`.
- [`API::V1::Onboarding::MyspeakController`](app/controllers/api/v1/onboarding/myspeak_controller.rb) accepts `params[:slug]` and validates it via the same reason vocabulary.

## Test plan

```
RAILS_ENV=test SECRET_KEY_BASE=dummy DEVISE_JWT_SECRET_KEY=dummy RAILS_MASTER_KEY="" \
  bundle exec rspec spec/models/profile_spec.rb \
                    spec/requests/api/profiles_spec.rb \
                    spec/requests/api/v1/onboarding/myspeak_spec.rb
```

74 examples / 0 failures locally. Coverage:

- [ ] Model: format / reserved / pure-numeric rejection (on change only); `slug_editable?` window math; `slug_changed_at` set on edits but NOT on create; `slug_available?` excludes own id, blocks Profile.slug, Profile.username, and ChildAccount.username.
- [ ] `PATCH /api/profiles/:id`: happy path stamps `slug_changed_at`; no-op when value equals current; 422 `slug_locked` with `next_edit_at` during the window; admin bypasses lockout; 422 `slug_invalid` / `slug_reserved` / `slug_taken`.
- [ ] `GET /api/profiles/check_slug`: `ok` / `format` / `reserved` / `taken`; no auth required.
- [ ] Onboarding: picked-slug happy path; `slug_invalid` / `slug_reserved` / `slug_taken` rejections; blank slug falls back to auto-generated.

author: thakorrohan
body:
Hi there! 👋

We've been using this module heavily in production at FlashRDP, and we wanted to contribute back the massive UI/UX overhaul and logic refinements we've built on top of your fantastic backend foundation. 

We completely understand if you don't want to merge this entirely since it introduces some opinionated design choices, but we wanted to open this PR so you can see the code and perhaps cherry-pick the parts you like!

### 🎨 Major UI & UX Improvements
- **Complete Visual Overhaul:** Replaced the generic WHMCS styling with a modern, glassmorphism-inspired UI featuring smooth transitions and micro-animations.
- **Card-Based Rebuild Wizard:** Replaced the simple `confirm()` dialog for server rebuilds with a beautiful, multi-step card wizard. It visually fetches and renders OS templates and seamlessly integrates your new SSH Key selection logic.
- **Native Sidebar Injection:** Added robust `hooks.php` logic to inject a custom, sticky "Manage Server" sidebar directly into the WHMCS client area, improving navigation.
- **Datatables Removal:** Stripped out the heavy DataTables jQuery plugin in favor of modern, lightweight CSS-grid tables for better performance.

### ⚙️ Logic Improvements (Highly Recommended)
We revamped two critical user flows to fix edge-case bugs and reliability issues:

1. **Windows Password Reset Flow (`client.php`)**
   - **The Problem:** The previous password reset logic hardcoded the target user as `root`. This meant that customers running Windows Server templates couldn't reset their passwords because Windows uses the `Administrator` account.
   - **The Fix:** We updated the `resetPassword` endpoint to accept an explicit `user` parameter, whitelisting it strictly to `['root', 'Administrator']`. The frontend UI detects the OS type and passes the correct username, ensuring password resets work flawlessly across both Linux and Windows templates.

2. **VNC Connection Flow (`client.php`)**
   - **The Problem:** When VirtFusion rotates the VNC token, the hypervisor needs a moment to actually bind the websocket port. Previously, the browser would try to connect to the websocket proxy *instantly*, resulting in the proxy dropping the connection immediately with a `1006` WebSocket error.
   - **The Fix:** We rewrote the `vncViewer` endpoint to serve a dedicated HTML skeleton.
     - **Timing Fix:** It now injects the `noVNC` bundle via a Javascript `setTimeout` of `2500ms`. This 2.5-second delay guarantees the hypervisor is ready, completely eliminating the sporadic `1006` connection drops.
     - **Security:** We added extremely strict `Content-Security-Policy` (CSP) and `X-Frame-Options` headers to ensure the VNC console cannot be embedded in an unauthorized iframe or cached by intermediaries, protecting the short-lived rotated token.

### 🔄 Upstream Sync
This branch is fully synced with your recent `1.5.1` commits (including the new SSH key backend and PHP 8.2 fixes).

Feel free to merge it, close it, or cherry-pick specific files (like the Windows password logic or the CSS). Thanks for maintaining an awesome module!

author: gamma-software
body:
## What

The Connections panel's update badge could show a stale **"Up to date"** for up to 6h — e.g. a remote on v0.4.0 stayed green even after `server-v0.5.0` shipped.

## Why

`useLatestServerVersion` caches the latest dist release in `localStorage` with a 6h TTL (to respect GitHub's 60 req/hr unauthenticated limit). Nothing busted that cache: the panel's **Refresh** button only refreshed connection statuses (`useConnections().refresh()`), never the latest-release lookup. So the badge compared the reported version against a stale `latest`.

## Change

- `useLatestServerVersion` now returns `{ latest, refresh }`. `refresh(force?)` re-checks `releases/latest`; `force` bypasses the 6h cache. Still never throws.
- **Refresh** button now force-rechecks latest alongside the connection refresh (`Promise.all([refresh(), refreshLatest(true)])`) — a click can't leave a stale badge.
- **Auto-poll every 30s** while the panel is open, so statuses, reported versions and the badge stay live without a click.
  - The latest-release check on each tick is **non-forced** — it honors the 6h cache, so the timer can't blow GitHub's rate limit. Only the cheap connection refresh actually runs every tick.
  - Polling **pauses while the window is hidden** (`document.hidden`, e.g. minimized to the tray).

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean (panel was the only consumer of the hook)
- `npx biome check` (changed files) — clean
- Confirmed `Myra-Agents-Server-Dist` `releases/latest` returns `server-v0.5.0`; with this change a force-refresh updates the badge to amber **"Update available"** for a v0.4.0 server.

## Note

Not runtime-verified (no full `tauri:build` here) — needs a manual click-through of Settings → Connections.

author: thinh2
body:
## What changes are proposed in this pull request?
  
Time-travel timestamp resolution can currently land on a commit version that no longer has the log files needed to reconstruct the table (e.g. an "orphan" commit left behind after log cleanup, with no commit 0 or anchoring
checkpoint). This PR lets callers restrict resolution to versions the table can actually be reconstructed from.

Key changes:
  - `latest_version_as_of` and `first_version_after` now take a `resolved_commit_type: HistoryCommitType` parameter. When `Recreatable` is passed, resolution is bounded below by the earliest recreatable version, so
the returned version is guaranteed loadable via time travel.
  - updated the user guide document to reflect the new parameter of the public function `latest_version_as_of` and `first_version_after`.
  - 
### This PR affects the following public APIs
- latest_version_as_of
- first_version_after

## How was this change tested?
 - A new parameterized test was added to verify the behavior difference when using HistoryCommitType of the `latest_version_as_of` and `first_version_after` in the log clean up scenario.

author: brandonrc
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1754. That PR serialized the `cleanup_stuck_scans_*` tests, but the **Code Coverage** gate is still red — a sibling DB test fails under nextest for the *same* root cause:

```
FAIL services::storage_gc_service::tests::test_run_gc_removes_abandoned_oci_upload_session_storage
panicked: "GC result should include the upload temp and part keys"  → nextest exit 100, no lcov.info
```

The `test_run_gc_*` tests run a **cluster-wide GC reap** and assert on the exact set of collected keys. They serialize via the in-process `STORAGE_GC_TEST_LOCK` / `storage_gc_test_guard()` (`storage_gc_service.rs:1670`), which — like `CLEANUP_TEST_LOCK` — does nothing across nextest's per-test **processes**. So concurrent GC tests reap each other's fixtures and the exact-result assertions fail nondeterministically.

**Fix:** generalize the nextest test-group to a single `db-serial` group covering **both** the `cleanup_stuck_scans_*` and `storage_gc_service::tests` suites, so no two cluster-wide-state DB tests ever run concurrently under nextest.

## Regression test (required for `fix/*` PRs)
- [ ] This PR is a `fix/*` AND adds/updates a test that would have caught the bug
- [x] N/A — fixes **test-harness scheduling**, not product code. **Verified locally:** the 91 affected tests pass under `cargo nextest run --lib --test-threads 4` (CI's mode) with this config — serialized — against a real Postgres; they flaked before. (I installed nextest + ran a local Postgres to confirm, since this can only be reproduced under nextest + DB.)

- [x] No regressions (config-only; affects only nextest scheduling in the coverage job; `cargo test` unit job unaffected; locally verified green under nextest)

author: coreyrdean
body:
## What
The client hardcoded its English chat strings; the Blitz engine reads them from `Game Data/Language.txt` (`Language.bb::LoadLanguage`), which a project edits to **translate the game**. Honoring it is the "respect the engine's customizable nature" goal — with the hardcoded English kept as a soft fallback so the default (English) project renders unchanged.

## Pieces
- **`rcce-data::language`** — a faithful parser of `Language.txt`, mirroring `LoadLanguage` *exactly*: `Trim$` each line; skip blanks and comment-only lines (`;` first); strip an inline comment to the text before `;` (**not** re-trimmed, matching Blitz `Left$`); collect the rest 0-indexed per the `LS_*` constants. `ls::` consts for the indices used; `get` / `get_or` with an English fallback.
  - The `190..219` slash-command-name upper-casing in `LoadLanguage` is a *server* chat-dispatch concern with no effect on the display strings the client renders — intentionally not replicated (documented).
- **`AssetStore`**: loads `Game Data/Language.txt` (UTF-8 text; absent/unreadable → empty table → English fallback) + a `language()` accessor; threaded into `World` at enter-world exactly like `template_genders` / `health_stat`.
- **`World::lang(idx, default)`** resolves a string; the XP toast and the kill toast now flow through it.

## Parity fix (bundled)
The kill toast also gains a fix: Blitz is `LanguageString$(LS_YouKilled) + " " + Name$ + "!"` = **"You killed: \<name\>!"** (ClientNet.bb:1091, `LS_YouKilled` = "You killed:"). The prior hardcoded Rust line dropped the colon.

## Verification
- `cargo +1.95.0 clippy … --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` → clean.
- `cargo +1.95.0 test -p rcce-data -p rcce-client` → green: 4 parser cases (comment/blank skipping, inline-comment strip without re-trim, indent handling, empty/default fallback) + `chat_toasts_honor_translated_language` (a German `Language` table flows through to both toasts). The two existing kill-message asserts updated for the restored colon.
- Default (no/English `Language.txt`) renders byte-identically (soft fallback); pure-logic, no render path.

Follow-up: the helper makes localizing each remaining hardcoded client string a one-liner — a natural batch follow-up.

body:
`waitForCondition(page, () => /<re>/.test(page.url()))` was the standing flake source. Migrates every URL-poll site to the new toolkit primitive `waitForUrl` (e2e-toolkit#1), which wraps Playwrights navigation-event-driven `page.waitForURL` and chains the toolkits network-quiet check. Submodule pointer advanced.

## Summary

- Registers `folk` as a seminar level in the V7 wiki-completeness gate.
- Replaces the deferred seminar `NotImplementedError` with seminar-specific thresholds and checks for section shape, two-source citation coverage, citation registry resolution, source-reference resolution, and all-cited-source verification semantics.
- Extends focused gate tests with seminar PASS/FAIL fixtures and preserves existing core gate coverage.

## New seminar checks

- `seminar_sections`: requires the six compiled seminar H2 sections to be present and non-empty.
- `distinct_sources`: enforces at least two distinct inline `[S#]` citations.
- `citation_resolution`: requires every cited `[S#]` to be defined in the sibling `.sources.yaml` registry.
- `source_ref_resolution`: requires cited literary/textbook sources to carry `file`, and cited wikipedia/external sources to carry `url`.
- `all_chunk_verify_quote`: verifies every cited source when a real adapter is supplied; otherwise degrades to source registry/reference resolution and reports `verify_quote adapter not configured`.

## Impact

cross-track infra: affects all seminar levels (bio/hist/lit*/oes/ruth/istorio/folk) — they were fully blocked (NotImplementedError) before this; this gives them a working gate, no regression,

author: elronbandel
body:
## Problem

#39 ("standardize agent/benchmark path conventions") moved to native Docker ENTRYPOINT/CMD composition: benchmark images do `exec "$@"` + `CMD /grade.sh` (a bare benchmark grades-on-run), and the **stitched eval image** was meant to override `CMD` to `/usr/local/bin/run` to launch the full pipeline. That override was **documented in `combination.Dockerfile` but never implemented**, and the agent-entrypoint move (`/opt/agent/entrypoint.sh` → `/run.sh` at the image root) was **never propagated into the combination `COPY`**.

Result: the eval image inherited `CMD /grade.sh` and ran the **verifier only** — the agent never ran in **any** of the three deploy modes (container/compose/job), bypassing the rule-12 three-phase pipeline. The only end-to-end test is `#[ignore]`'d, so CI stayed green.

## Fix

- **`core/combination.Dockerfile`**: `COPY --from=agent /run.sh /run.sh` (the agent launch script lives at the image root, not under `/opt/agent/`, so the existing `/opt/agent/` COPY missed it) + `CMD ["/usr/local/bin/run"]` (the stitched image launches the pipeline). Bare benchmark images keep `CMD /grade.sh`, preserving #39's grade-on-run composition.
- **`benchmarks/_chart/values.yaml`**: the k8s Job overrides the image command, so its `runnerArgs` must invoke the launcher itself — `/entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/run` (`/entrypoint.sh` does task setup, then execs `run`).
- **`tests/sanity/check.rs`**: `eval_image_launches_the_pipeline` guard pins all three stitch points (daemon-free, runs on the per-PR lane).

## Verification

End-to-end via the replay harness (`docker compose` + `models/replay`), isolated compose projects, real images:

| | BEFORE (`CMD /grade.sh`, no `/run.sh`) | AFTER (fixed) |
|---|---|---|
| agent model-calls | **0** | **2** |
| `result.json` | **absent** | **written** |

BEFORE the agent never runs and no result is produced; AFTER it runs and a result lands.

- `cargo test --test check` — all pass (incl. the new guard).
- Negative check: reverting either stitch point makes the guard fail.

Separate from #67 (the task-id leak fix).

💡 **What:** 
Replaced standard synchronous `open()` with `async with aiofiles.open()` inside the `get_config_raw` API endpoint. Updated the tests to correctly mock the asynchronous file read operations using `AsyncMock`.

🎯 **Why:**
The previous implementation performed synchronous file I/O within a FastAPI async endpoint, causing the main event loop to block while waiting for the disk read. This limits concurrency and degrades application performance under load.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
Measured event loop delays under simulated concurrent load reading large files:
* **Baseline (Sync `open`):** Maximum event loop blocking: 0.0443s
* **Optimized (Async `aiofiles`):** Maximum event loop blocking: 0.0273s

author: samthorold
body:
## Summary

Fixes #403. `oscillation_strength`'s flat-series guard keyed only on *relative* variance (`residual_var <= 1e-6 * raw_var`). A near-constant series with a tiny monotone creep slips past it: the linear detrend removes the creep, leaving noise whose variance is not small relative to the (also tiny) raw variance, so its autocorrelation reports a spurious deep anti-correlation at a long lag. The `example10_predator_prey_hopf` seed-4 witness ranges only ~0.997–1.000 (~0.3% swing) yet scored 0.28.

## Fix

Add an **absolute** peak-to-peak floor (`MIN_SWING = 0.01`) before the detrend: a producer share that moves less than 1% over the window is a frozen fixed point with noise, not an oscillation, regardless of residual structure. The threshold sits at the top of the issue's "<~0.5–1% is not a regime signal" band, with comfortable margin over the ~0.3% witness.

## Tests

- New regression test `oscillation_strength_zero_for_near_flat_drift_with_noise` reproduces the seed-4 witness shape (0.997→1.000 drift + small noise): scored `0.096` before the fix, `0.0` after.
- Genuine-oscillator tests (sustained sine, damped sine; ~0.6 swing) unaffected — the floor doesn't suppress real signal.
- Full crate suite: 79 passed; `cargo fmt --check` clean.

## Acceptance (per #403)

- [x] A near-constant series (amplitude ≲ floor) reads ≈0 regardless of detrended-residual structure.
- [x] example10 seed-4 reads ≈0 like its siblings.
- [x] Existing positive cases (genuine oscillators) unaffected; regression test for a real sinusoid kept.
